# Behavior extracted from Radix UI Primitives and MUI Base UI test suites

Each `it`/`test` block in both libraries' suites restated as one observable behavior per bullet,
grouped by component slug and then by concern. Source tags carry the repo-relative path and the
literal test name, so any bullet can be traced back to the assertion it came from. The
**Coverage ledger** near the end says exactly which test files are represented, which are not, and
why.

Read this as raw input for a conformance suite, not as a design document: where the two libraries
disagree, both behaviors are listed with their own tags.

There is no `cypress/` directory any more: the Cypress specs were ported to Playwright under
`e2e/`, and they still target the same Storybook story ids (`*--cypress`) through
`e2e/helpers.ts`'s `visitStory`. There are no Storybook-based test runners (`*.stories.test.*`)
and no visual-regression suite.

### mui/base-ui

- Repo: `https://github.com/mui/base-ui`
- Commit: `a4f5e0ed25575f4abe94bec08bac50903085b034`
- Commit date: 2026-09-11
- Cloned (shallow) and read: 2026-09-13
- 393 test/spec files, 5352 `it`/`test` blocks (counted mechanically; `it.each`/`describe.each`/`forEach` templates count once), spread over `packages/react/src/**`,
  `packages/utils/src/**`, `packages/react/test/**`, `test/e2e`, `test/regressions`,
  `test/screen-reader` and `docs/src`.

The file list is too long to reproduce in full here; each bullet below carries its own
repo-relative path, and the complete inventory (file path plus `it` count) was generated with:

```
find base-ui \( -name '*.test.tsx' -o -name '*.test.ts' -o -name '*.spec.ts' -o -name '*.spec.tsx' \) \
  | grep -v node_modules | sort
```

Base UI ships several components Radix does not (`drawer`, `autocomplete`, `combobox`,
`preview-card`, `meter`, `fieldset`, `input`, `toolbar`, `field`, `csp-provider`) plus a vendored
fork of Floating UI React under `packages/react/src/floating-ui-react/` whose tests are the real
specification for dismissal, outside-press, focus trapping, list navigation and typeahead.

## button

### Roles and attributes

- Given `<Button nativeButton={false} render={<span />}>Save</Button>` inside a `<div onClick>`, when rendered, then the element is a `SPAN` carrying `role="button"` and `tabindex="0"`; when it is focused with Tab and `Enter` then `Space` are pressed, real click events are dispatched so the render element's `onClickCapture`, its `onClick`, the `Button`'s `onClick` and the ANCESTOR's `onClick` each fire twice. (base-ui: `packages/react/src/button/Button.test.tsx`: "prop: nativeButton > custom element: applies button semantics and dispatches real clicks from keyboard activation")
- Given a `<span>` rendered from `useButton({ native: false })`, when the returned `getButtonProps()` object is inspected, then it has no `type` property (no `type` is forced onto non-native hosts). (base-ui: `packages/react/src/internals/use-button/useButton.test.tsx`: "non-native button > keyboard interactions > does not set a type prop")
- Given `useButton()` with no params on a native `<button>` host, when `getButtonProps()` is called, then it returns `tabIndex: 0` and the rendered button has `tabIndex` 0. (base-ui: `packages/react/src/internals/use-button/useButton.test.tsx`: "param: tabIndex > returns tabIndex in getButtonProps when host component is BUTTON")
- Given `useButton({ native: false })` on a `<span>` host, when `getButtonProps()` is called, then it returns `tabIndex: 0` and the rendered span has `tabIndex` 0. (base-ui: `packages/react/src/internals/use-button/useButton.test.tsx`: "param: tabIndex > returns tabIndex in getButtonProps when host component is not BUTTON")
- Given `useButton({ tabIndex: 3 })`, when the button renders, then its `tabIndex` property is `3` (explicit `tabIndex` wins over the default). (base-ui: `packages/react/src/internals/use-button/useButton.test.tsx`: "param: tabIndex > returns tabIndex in getButtonProps if it is explicitly provided")

### Keyboard

- Given `<Button nativeButton={false} render={<a href="#target" />}>Go</Button>`, when the link is focused with Tab and `Space` is pressed, then the keydown's default is prevented (so the page does not scroll — `fireEvent.keyDown` returns `false`), `onClick` fires exactly once, and `window.location.hash` becomes `"#target"`. (base-ui: `packages/react/src/button/Button.test.tsx`: "prop: nativeButton > custom link element: Space activates the link without scrolling the page")
- Given `<Button nativeButton={false} render={<span />} onClick>`, when `Shift+Enter` is pressed while focused, then `onClick` fires once and the synthesized click event carries `shiftKey: true` — keyboard activation preserves modifier state. (base-ui: `packages/react/src/button/Button.test.tsx`: "prop: nativeButton > custom element: keyboard activation clicks carry modifier key state")
- Given a `<span>` rendered with `useButton({ native: false })` and an `onClick` spy, when the span is focused with Tab and `Enter` is pressed, then `onClick` fires exactly once. (base-ui: `packages/react/src/internals/use-button/useButton.test.tsx`: "non-native button > keyboard interactions > can be activated with Enter key")
- Given a `<span>` rendered with `useButton({ native: false })` and an `onClick` spy, when the span is focused with Tab and `Space` is pressed, then `onClick` fires exactly once. (base-ui: `packages/react/src/internals/use-button/useButton.test.tsx`: "non-native button > keyboard interactions > can be activated with Space key")
- Given a non-native `useButton` host that attaches an open shadow root containing a focusable inner `<span>`, when the inner element is focused and dispatches a composed bubbling `keydown` with key `Enter`, then the host's `onClick` fires once (the handler resolves the target through `composedPath`). (base-ui: `packages/react/src/internals/use-button/useButton.test.tsx`: "non-native button > keyboard interactions > can be activated with Enter when the keyboard event originates inside a shadow root") (browser-mode only)
- Given a `<span>` from `useButton({ native: false })` (non-composite), when `keydown` with key `' '` fires then `keyup` with key `' '`, then `onClick` fires only after `keyup` (0 clicks after keydown, 1 after keyup). (base-ui: `packages/react/src/internals/use-button/useButton.test.tsx`: "event handlers > key: Space fires keyup then click on non-composite buttons")
- Given a `<span>` from `useButton({ native: false, composite: true })` with `tabIndex={0}`, when `keydown` with key `' '` fires, then `onClick` fires immediately on keydown and does not fire again on `keyup`. (base-ui: `packages/react/src/internals/use-button/useButton.test.tsx`: "event handlers > key: Space fires keydown then click on composite buttons")
- Given an `<a href="#test">` from `useButton({ native: false, composite: true })`, when `keydown` with key `' '` fires, then `onClick` fires once on keydown and not again on `keyup`. (base-ui: `packages/react/src/internals/use-button/useButton.test.tsx`: "event handlers > key: Space fires keydown then click on composite links")
- Given an `<a href="#test">` with `role="menuitem"` from `useButton({ native: false, composite: true })` whose consumer `onKeyDown` calls `event.preventDefault()`, when `keydown` with key `' '` fires, then `onClick` never fires (Space stays available for text navigation). (base-ui: `packages/react/src/internals/use-button/useButton.test.tsx`: "event handlers > does not click composite links when Space is prevented for text navigation")
- Given a `<div role="gridcell" tabIndex={0}>` from `useButton({ native: false, composite: true })` whose `onKeyDown` calls `preventDefault()`, when `keydown` with key `' '` fires, then `onClick` never fires. (base-ui: `packages/react/src/internals/use-button/useButton.test.tsx`: "event handlers > does not click composite gridcells when Space is prevented")
- Given a `<div role="switch" tabIndex={0}>` from `useButton({ native: false, composite: true })` whose `onKeyDown` calls `preventDefault()`, when `keydown` with key `' '` fires, then `onClick` still fires once (switch role keeps Space activation despite prevented default). (base-ui: `packages/react/src/internals/use-button/useButton.test.tsx`: "event handlers > clicks composite switches when Space is prevented")
- Given a native `<button>` from `useButton({ composite: true })`, when `keydown` with key `' '` fires, then `onClick` fires once on keydown and not again on `keyup`. (base-ui: `packages/react/src/internals/use-button/useButton.test.tsx`: "event handlers > key: Space fires keydown then click on native composite buttons")
- Given a native `<button>` from `useButton({ composite: true })`, when a real `[Space]` key press is typed through userEvent (keydown plus keyup plus the browser's own click), then `onClick` fires exactly once, not twice. (base-ui: `packages/react/src/internals/use-button/useButton.test.tsx`: "event handlers > does not fire duplicate clicks for Space on native composite buttons")
- Given one `<span tabIndex={0}>` whose props come from two nested `useButton({ native: false, composite: true })` calls composed as `outer.getButtonProps(inner.getButtonProps(props))`, when `[Space]` is typed then `[Enter]`, then `onClick` fires once per key press (1 then 2 total), not once per hook. (base-ui: `packages/react/src/internals/use-button/useButton.test.tsx`: "event handlers > fires a single click for nested non-native composite buttons")
- Given a `<span tabIndex={0}>` from `useButton({ native: false, composite: true })` whose `onKeyDown` calls `event.preventBaseUIHandler()`, when `keydown` with key `' '` fires, then `onClick` never fires. (base-ui: `packages/react/src/internals/use-button/useButton.test.tsx`: "event handlers > does not click composite buttons when keydown calls preventBaseUIHandler")
- Given a `<span tabIndex={0}>` from `useButton({ native: false })` whose `onKeyDown` and `onKeyUp` both call `event.preventBaseUIHandler()`, when `keydown` with key `Enter` fires and then `keydown`/`keyup` with key `' '`, then `onClick` never fires for either activation path. (base-ui: `packages/react/src/internals/use-button/useButton.test.tsx`: "event handlers > does not click non-composite buttons when keydown/keyup calls preventBaseUIHandler")
- Given a `<span tabIndex={0}>` from `useButton({ native: false })` whose `onKeyDown` calls `event.preventDefault()`, when `[Enter]` is typed, then `onClick` never fires, matching native button behavior. (base-ui: `packages/react/src/internals/use-button/useButton.test.tsx`: "event handlers > key: Enter does not click non-native buttons when keydown calls preventDefault")
- Given a `<span tabIndex={0}>` from `useButton({ native: false })` whose `onKeyUp` calls `event.preventDefault()`, when `[Space]` is typed, then `onClick` never fires, matching native button behavior. (base-ui: `packages/react/src/internals/use-button/useButton.test.tsx`: "event handlers > key: Space does not click non-native buttons when keyup calls preventDefault")
- Given a `<span tabIndex={0}>` from `useButton({ native: false })` (no explicit `composite`) rendered inside `<CompositeRoot>`, when `keydown` with key `' '` fires, then `onClick` fires on keydown (composite context is inherited) and not again on `keyup`. (base-ui: `packages/react/src/internals/use-button/useButton.test.tsx`: "event handlers > key: Space fires keydown then click when in composite root context")
- Given a native `<button>` from `useButton()` rendered inside `<CompositeRoot>`, when `keydown` with key `' '` fires, then `onClick` fires on keydown and not again on `keyup`. (base-ui: `packages/react/src/internals/use-button/useButton.test.tsx`: "event handlers > key: Space fires keydown then click on native buttons in composite root context")
- Given a `<span>` from `useButton({ native: false, composite: false })` inside `<CompositeRoot>`, when `keydown` with key `' '` fires then `keyup`, then `onClick` fires only on keyup (explicit `composite: false` overrides the inherited composite context). (base-ui: `packages/react/src/internals/use-button/useButton.test.tsx`: "event handlers > `composite=false` keeps keyup activation inside composite root context")
- Given a `<span>` from `useButton({ native: false })`, when `keydown` with key `Enter` fires, then `onKeyDown` fires once and `onClick` fires once on the same keydown. (base-ui: `packages/react/src/internals/use-button/useButton.test.tsx`: "event handlers > key: Enter fires keydown then click on non-native buttons")

### Pointer

- Given `<Button disabled focusableWhenDisabled onMouseMove onClick />`, when the button is hovered `onMouseMove` fires, and when it is clicked `onClick` does not — hover handlers stay live while activation is blocked (the element carries `data-disabled` and `aria-disabled="true"` and no native `disabled`). (base-ui: `packages/react/src/button/Button.test.tsx`: "prop: focusableWhenDisabled > native button: allows hover handlers while blocking activation") (browser-mode only)

### Focus management

- Given `<Button disabled onClick onMouseDown onPointerDown onKeyDown />` as a native button, when rendered, then it carries the native `disabled` attribute plus `data-disabled` and NOT `aria-disabled`; Tab does not focus it, and clicking, `Space` and `Enter` fire none of the four handlers. (base-ui: `packages/react/src/button/Button.test.tsx`: "prop: disabled > native button: uses the disabled attribute and is not focusable")
- Given `<Button disabled nativeButton={false} render={<span />} />` with the same four handlers, when rendered, then it carries `data-disabled`, `aria-disabled="true"` and `tabindex="-1"` and NOT the native `disabled` attribute; Tab does not focus it and clicking, `Space` and `Enter` fire none of the handlers. (base-ui: `packages/react/src/button/Button.test.tsx`: "prop: disabled > custom element: applies aria-disabled and is not focusable")
- Given `<Button disabled focusableWhenDisabled />` as a native button, when rendered, then it drops the native `disabled` attribute and carries `data-disabled`, `aria-disabled="true"` and `tabindex="0"`; Tab DOES focus it, yet clicking, `Space` and `Enter` still fire none of the handlers. (base-ui: `packages/react/src/button/Button.test.tsx`: "prop: focusableWhenDisabled > native button: prevents interactions but remains focusable")
- Given `<Button disabled focusableWhenDisabled nativeButton={false} render={<span />} />`, when rendered, then it carries `data-disabled`, `aria-disabled="true"` and `tabindex="0"` and no native `disabled`; Tab focuses it, yet clicking, `Space` and `Enter` fire none of the handlers. (base-ui: `packages/react/src/button/Button.test.tsx`: "prop: focusableWhenDisabled > custom element: prevents interactions but remains focusable")
- Given a `focusableWhenDisabled` button that disables itself inside its own `onClick`, when it is clicked once, then `onClick` fired once, the button KEEPS focus, and it now carries `aria-disabled="true"`; further clicks, `Enter` and `Space` do not fire `onClick` again and focus is retained. (base-ui: `packages/react/src/button/Button.test.tsx`: "prop: focusableWhenDisabled > keeps focus and suppresses interactions after becoming disabled")
- Given a native `<button disabled>` whose props come from `useButton({ disabled: true, focusableWhenDisabled: true })`, when `element.focus()` is called, then the button receives focus. (base-ui: `packages/react/src/internals/use-button/useButton.test.tsx`: "param: focusableWhenDisabled > allows disabled buttons to be focused")
- Given `<CompositeRoot>` wrapping a `<button disabled>` built from `useButton({ disabled: true, focusableWhenDisabled: true })`, when the button is focused, then it receives focus, and it still does after the component is re-keyed (ref identity change) and re-rendered. (base-ui: `packages/react/src/internals/use-button/useButton.test.tsx`: "param: focusableWhenDisabled > force overrides disabled attribute when put in a composite")

### State and controlled/uncontrolled

- Given a `<span>` from `useButton({ disabled: true, focusableWhenDisabled: true, native: false })` wired with `onClick`, `onKeyDown`, `onKeyUp`, `onFocus`, `onBlur`, when the element is tabbed to, `[Enter]` and `[Space]` are typed and it is clicked, then only `onFocus` (and later `onBlur` on tabbing away) fire; `onKeyDown`, `onKeyUp` and `onClick` are never called. (base-ui: `packages/react/src/internals/use-button/useButton.test.tsx`: "param: focusableWhenDisabled > prevents interactions except focus and blur")

### Forms

- Given a native `<button type="submit">` from `useButton({ composite: true })` inside a `<form onSubmit>`, when `keydown` with key `' '` fires, then the form's submit handler runs once on keydown and not again on `keyup`. (base-ui: `packages/react/src/internals/use-button/useButton.test.tsx`: "event handlers > key: Space preserves native submit semantics on composite buttons")
- Given a native `<button type="reset">` from `useButton({ composite: true })` inside a `<form onReset>`, when `keydown` with key `' '` fires, then the form's reset handler runs once on keydown and not again on `keyup`. (base-ui: `packages/react/src/internals/use-button/useButton.test.tsx`: "event handlers > key: Space preserves native reset semantics on composite buttons")

### SSR and hydration

- Given a `<span>` from `useButton({ disabled: true, native: false })`, when rendered to string on the server, then the first child has `role` `'button'`. (base-ui: `packages/react/src/internals/use-button/useButton.test.tsx`: "server-side rendering > should server-side render") (browser-mode only)
- Given a native `<button>` from `useButton({ disabled: true })`, when rendered to string on the server, then the button carries the native `disabled` attribute. (base-ui: `packages/react/src/internals/use-button/useButton.test.tsx`: "server-side rendering > adds disabled attribute") (browser-mode only)

### Notes and edge cases

- Given `<Button />`, the shared `describeConformance` suite runs with `{ refInstanceof: window.HTMLButtonElement, button: true }`. (base-ui: `packages/react/src/button/Button.test.tsx`: "describeConformance")
- Given `Button`, when type-checked, then `<Button />`, `<Button type="submit" form="form-id" name="action" />`, `<Button nativeButton={false} render={<span />} />` and `<Button nativeButton={false} render={(props) => <div {...props} />} />` all type-check (type-only spec). (base-ui: `packages/react/src/button/Button.spec.tsx`: "type contract")
- Given `useButton()` on a native `<button>`, when arbitrary props such as `data-testid` are passed through `getButtonProps({ 'data-testid': ... })`, then they land on the host element. (base-ui: `packages/react/src/internals/use-button/useButton.test.tsx`: "arbitrary props > are passed to the host component")
- Given `useButton({ native: true })` whose `buttonRef` is attached to a `<span>`, when rendered, then `console.error` is called once with "Base UI: A component that acts as a button expected a native <button> because the `nativeButton` prop is true. ... Use a real <button> in the `render` prop, or set `nativeButton` to `false`." (base-ui: `packages/react/src/internals/use-button/useButton.test.tsx`: "dev warnings > errors if nativeButton=true but ref is not a button")
- Given `useButton({ native: false })` whose `buttonRef` is attached to a `<button>`, when rendered, then `console.error` is called once with "Base UI: A component that acts as a button expected a non-<button> because the `nativeButton` prop is false. ... Use a non-<button> in the `render` prop, or set `nativeButton` to `true`." (base-ui: `packages/react/src/internals/use-button/useButton.test.tsx`: "dev warnings > errors if nativeButton=false but ref is a button")

## toggle

### Roles and attributes

- Given `<Toggle.Root>Like</Toggle.Root>` with no pressed props, when rendered, then the `button` accessible as "Like" carries `aria-pressed="false"` and `data-state="off"`. (radix: `packages/react/toggle/src/toggle.test.tsx`: "given a Toggle with text > should render with attributes as false/off by default")
- Given `<Toggle.Root defaultPressed asChild>` wrapping `<button type="button">Toggle</button>`, when rendered, then the element is a `BUTTON` carrying `aria-pressed="true"` and `data-state="on"`, keeps `className="custom-class"` and the inline `outlineColor: rgb(1, 2, 3)`, the ref resolves to it, and clicking fires the author `onClick`. (radix: `packages/react/toggle/src/toggle.test.tsx`: "Toggle.Root > forwards props to the child element when `asChild` is set")
- Given `<Toggle disabled onPressedChange>`, when rendered, then the button carries the native `disabled` attribute, `data-disabled` and `aria-pressed="false"`, and clicking it neither calls `onPressedChange` nor changes `aria-pressed`. (base-ui: `packages/react/src/toggle/Toggle.test.tsx`: "prop: disabled > disables the component")

### Pointer

- Given an uncontrolled `<Toggle.Root>Like</Toggle.Root>` starting off, when a bubbling cancelable `click` MouseEvent is dispatched on the button, then it flips to `aria-pressed="true"` and `data-state="on"`. (radix: `packages/react/toggle/src/toggle.test.tsx`: "given a Toggle with text > Click event should change pressed attributes to true/on")
- Given `<Toggle.Root defaultPressed>Like</Toggle.Root>`, when a bubbling cancelable `click` MouseEvent is dispatched on the button, then it flips back to `aria-pressed="false"` and `data-state="off"`. (radix: `packages/react/toggle/src/toggle.test.tsx`: "given a Toggle with text and defaultPressed=\"true\" > Click event should change attributes back to off/false")

### State and controlled/uncontrolled

- Given `<Toggle.Root defaultPressed>Like</Toggle.Root>`, when rendered, then the button starts at `aria-pressed="true"` and `data-state="on"`. (radix: `packages/react/toggle/src/toggle.test.tsx`: "given a Toggle with text and defaultPressed=\"true\" > should render with attributes true/on by default")
- Given `<Toggle.Root disabled>Like</Toggle.Root>`, when rendered then clicked, then the button carries the bare `disabled` attribute and stays at `aria-pressed="false"` and `data-state="off"` after the click. (radix: `packages/react/toggle/src/toggle.test.tsx`: "given a Toggle with text and disabled=\"true\" > on click the attributes do not change")
- Given a controlled `<Toggle.Root pressed onPressedChange={fn}>Like</Toggle.Root>` rendering `aria-pressed="true"` and `data-state="on"`, when the button is clicked, then `onPressedChange` fires exactly once with `false` and the attributes stay `aria-pressed="true"` / `data-state="on"` because the parent owns the value. (radix: `packages/react/toggle/src/toggle.test.tsx`: "given a controlled Toggle (with pressed and onPressedChange) > Click event should keep the same attributes, and pass the new state to onPressedChange")
- Given a controlled `<Toggle pressed>` driven by an external checkbox, when the checkbox is toggled twice, then `aria-pressed` follows the controlled prop from `"false"` to `"true"` and back. (base-ui: `packages/react/src/toggle/Toggle.test.tsx`: "pressed state > controlled")
- Given `<Toggle defaultPressed={false}>`, when the button is clicked twice, then `aria-pressed` goes `"false"` → `"true"` → `"false"`. (base-ui: `packages/react/src/toggle/Toggle.test.tsx`: "pressed state > uncontrolled")
- Given `<Toggle defaultPressed={false} onPressedChange>`, when clicked, then `onPressedChange` is called exactly once with `true`. (base-ui: `packages/react/src/toggle/Toggle.test.tsx`: "prop: onPressedChange > is called when the pressed state changes")
- Given `onPressedChange` that calls `eventDetails.cancel()`, when the toggle is clicked, then `aria-pressed` stays `"false"` — cancelling the event details vetoes the state change. (base-ui: `packages/react/src/toggle/Toggle.test.tsx`: "prop: onPressedChange > does not change the pressed state when the event is canceled")
- Given a `<ToggleGroup onValueChange>` whose first `<Toggle value="one">` cancels in `onPressedChange`, when that toggle is clicked, then it stays `aria-pressed="false"` AND the group's `onValueChange` is never called. ### Keyboard

- Given a three-toggle group under each of `ltr`+horizontal, `ltr`+vertical, `rtl`+horizontal and `rtl`+vertical, when Tab focuses the first item (`tabindex="0"`) and the orientation's next key is pressed repeatedly, then focus and the `tabindex="0"` roving tab stop advance item by item and LOOP back to the first; the previous key walks backwards with the same loop; and the two keys from the other axis move nothing (four generated cases; `rtl` inverts only the horizontal pair). (base-ui: `packages/react/src/toggle-group/ToggleGroup.test.tsx`: "keyboard interactions > ltr/rtl > orientation: horizontal/vertical") (browser-mode only)
- Given a three-toggle group with focus on the third item, when `Home` is pressed, then the first item gets `tabindex="0"` and focus, and this holds again after moving to the second item. (base-ui: `packages/react/src/toggle-group/ToggleGroup.test.tsx`: "keyboard interactions > Home key moves focus to the first item") (browser-mode only)
- Given a three-toggle group with focus on the first item, when `End` is pressed, then the last item gets `tabindex="0"` and focus, and this holds again after moving back one. (base-ui: `packages/react/src/toggle-group/ToggleGroup.test.tsx`: "keyboard interactions > End key moves focus to the last item") (browser-mode only)
- Given a focused toggle inside a group, when `Enter` is pressed twice, then `aria-pressed` goes `"false"` → `"true"` → `"false"`. (base-ui: `packages/react/src/toggle-group/ToggleGroup.test.tsx`: "keyboard interactions > key: Enter toggles the pressed state") (browser-mode only)
- Given a focused toggle inside a group, when `Space` is pressed twice, then `aria-pressed` goes `"false"` → `"true"` → `"false"`. (base-ui: `packages/react/src/toggle-group/ToggleGroup.test.tsx`: "keyboard interactions > key: Space toggles the pressed state") (browser-mode only)

### Pointer

- Given an uncontrolled `ToggleGroup` with two toggles, when the first is clicked it becomes `aria-pressed="true"` with `data-pressed` and the second stays false; when the second is clicked the pressed state moves to it. (base-ui: `packages/react/src/toggle-group/ToggleGroup.test.tsx`: "uncontrolled > pressed state") (browser-mode only)
- Given `<ToggleGroup multiple defaultValue={['one']}>`, when the second toggle is clicked, then BOTH toggles are `aria-pressed="true"`. (base-ui: `packages/react/src/toggle-group/ToggleGroup.test.tsx`: "prop: multiple > multiple items can be pressed when true")
- Given `<ToggleGroup defaultValue={['one']}>` without `multiple`, when the second toggle is clicked, then the first becomes `aria-pressed="false"` and only the second is pressed. (base-ui: `packages/react/src/toggle-group/ToggleGroup.test.tsx`: "prop: multiple > only one item can be pressed when false")

### Focus management

- Given a `ToggleGroup` as the first focusable element inside a Dialog (story `togglegroup--cypress`), when the dialog opens, then focus lands inside the element with `role="radiogroup"` (the wrapper or its first roving item) and not on the "close" button, so focus does not skip past the group. Playwright e2e, regression test for issue 3077. (radix: `e2e/toggle-group.spec.ts`: "ToggleGroup > given a ToggleGroup as the first focusable element inside a Dialog > should move focus into the group when the dialog opens")
- Given a `ToggleGroup defaultValue={['one']}` either standalone or nested in `Toolbar.Group`, when `multiple` is flipped false → true → false while clicking toggles between each change, then the selection semantics switch correctly each time (single-select replaces, multi-select accumulates), `data-multiple` tracks the prop, and roving focus still works afterwards (`ArrowLeft` moves focus back to the first item) — remounting on the `multiple` transition would lose both (`it.each` over the standalone and Toolbar.Group cases). (base-ui: `packages/react/src/toggle-group/ToggleGroup.test.tsx`: "prop: multiple transitions > preserves selection and roving focus when %s") (browser-mode only)

- Given `<Checkbox.Root checked>` wrapping `<Checkbox.Indicator data-testid="indicator" />`, when rendered, then the indicator is present in the DOM. (base-ui: `packages/react/src/checkbox/indicator/CheckboxIndicator.test.tsx`: "should render indicator when checked")
- Given `<Checkbox.Root>` (unchecked) wrapping `<Checkbox.Indicator keepMounted />`, when rendered, then the indicator stays mounted. (base-ui: `packages/react/src/checkbox/indicator/CheckboxIndicator.test.tsx`: "prop: keepMounted > should keep indicator mounted when unchecked")
- Given `<Checkbox.Root checked>` wrapping `<Checkbox.Indicator keepMounted />`, when rendered, then the indicator is mounted. (base-ui: `packages/react/src/checkbox/indicator/CheckboxIndicator.test.tsx`: "prop: keepMounted > should keep indicator mounted when checked")
- Given `<Checkbox.Root indeterminate>` wrapping `<Checkbox.Indicator keepMounted />`, when rendered, then the indicator is mounted. (base-ui: `packages/react/src/checkbox/indicator/CheckboxIndicator.test.tsx`: "prop: keepMounted > should keep indicator mounted when indeterminate")
- Given a controlled `<Checkbox.Root checked>` with an indicator that has no CSS exit animation, when a "Close" button sets `checked` to `false`, then the indicator is removed from the DOM. (base-ui: `packages/react/src/checkbox/indicator/CheckboxIndicator.test.tsx`: "should remove the indicator when there is no exit animation defined") (browser-mode only — calls `skip()` when `isJSDOM`)
- Given `globalThis.BASE_UI_ANIMATIONS_DISABLED = false` and a controlled `<Checkbox.Root checked>` whose `<Checkbox.Indicator keepMounted className="animation-test-indicator">` runs `animation: test-anim 1ms` under `[data-ending-style]`, when a "Close" button unchecks it, then the indicator's `onAnimationEnd` eventually fires. (base-ui: `packages/react/src/checkbox/indicator/CheckboxIndicator.test.tsx`: "should remove the indicator when the animation finishes") (browser-mode only — calls `skip()` when `isJSDOM`)
- Given `globalThis.BASE_UI_ANIMATIONS_DISABLED = false`, an indicator with `transition: opacity 1ms` and `opacity: 0` under `[data-starting-style]` / `[data-ending-style]`, and a ref that replaces `element.getAnimations` with a spy returning `[]`, when a "Check" button checks the previously unchecked `<Checkbox.Root>`, then the indicator mounts (it was absent), `onTransitionEnd` eventually fires, and `getAnimations` is never called. (base-ui: `packages/react/src/checkbox/indicator/CheckboxIndicator.test.tsx`: "animations > triggers enter animation via data-starting-style when mounting") (browser-mode only)
- Given `globalThis.BASE_UI_ANIMATIONS_DISABLED = false` and an indicator with `animation: test-anim 1ms` under `[data-ending-style]` inside a controlled checked `<Checkbox.Root>`, when an "Uncheck" button unchecks it, then the indicator is first still present with a `data-ending-style` attribute and only afterwards removed from the DOM. - Given `globalThis.BASE_UI_ANIMATIONS_DISABLED = false` and 10 controlled `<Checkbox.Root checked>` each with an exit-animated `<Checkbox.Indicator data-testid={`indicator-${index}`}>` inside a `React.Profiler` that records the live indicator count per commit, when a single "Uncheck" button unchecks all of them, then every indicator is eventually removed and each post-uncheck commit observed either 10 or 0 indicators (never a partial count), i.e. they unmount in one commit. (base-ui: `packages/react/src/checkbox/indicator/CheckboxIndicator.test.tsx`: "animations > removes all indicators in a single commit when multiple checkboxes are unchecked") (browser-mode only)

### SSR and hydration

- Given `<Field.Root>` + `<Field.Label data-testid="label">` + `<Checkbox.Root id="explicit">` rendered to a string (cases: `nativeButton=false` targeting the hidden `input[type="checkbox"]`, `nativeButton=true` with `render={<button />}` targeting the role-`checkbox` element), when the server markup is inspected, then the control carries the provider's generated non-empty id rather than `"explicit"` and `Field.Label`'s `for` points at that generated id; after `hydrate()`, the control's `id` becomes `"explicit"` and the label's `for` becomes `"explicit"`. (base-ui: `packages/react/src/checkbox/root/CheckboxRoot.test.tsx`: "id > defers an explicit id until hydration but keeps Field.Label associated during SSR (nativeButton=%s)")
- Given `<Field.Root name="apple">` wrapping `<CheckboxGroup allValues={['fuji']}>` with `<Field.Item>` containing `<Field.Label data-testid="label">Fuji</Field.Label>` and `<Checkbox.Root value="fuji" />`, rendered to a string with `SafeReact.useId` mocked to `undefined` (React 17 fallback, `.react17.test.tsx`) for cases `nativeButton=false` and `nativeButton=true`, when the server markup is inspected, then no element has an `id` at all (`document.querySelectorAll('[id]')` is empty) and the label has no `for`; after `hydrate()`, the control gets a non-empty fallback id and the label's `for` matches it. (base-ui: `packages/react/src/checkbox/root/CheckboxRoot.react17.test.tsx`: "assigns the label association once the fallback ids arrive (nativeButton=%s)")

### Accessibility tooling

- Given a default checkbox provider/trigger/indicator, when audited with `axe`, then there are no accessibility violations. (radix: `packages/react/checkbox/src/checkbox.test.tsx`: "given a default Checkbox > should have no accessibility violations")
- Given a `disabled` checkbox, when audited with `axe`, then there are no accessibility violations. (radix: `packages/react/checkbox/src/checkbox.test.tsx`: "given a disabled Checkbox > should have no accessibility violations")
- Given a `defaultChecked` uncontrolled checkbox, when audited with `axe`, then there are no accessibility violations. (radix: `packages/react/checkbox/src/checkbox.test.tsx`: "given an uncontrolled `checked` Checkbox > should have no accessibility violations")
- Given a controlled checkbox with sibling toggle buttons, when audited with `axe`, then there are no accessibility violations. (radix: `packages/react/checkbox/src/checkbox.test.tsx`: "given a controlled Checkbox > should have no accessibility violations")
- Given a legacy `<Checkbox.Root aria-label>` with indicator, when audited with `axe`, then there are no accessibility violations (the nested bubble input is `hidden` and additionally gets `aria-hidden="true"` in the test harness because axe does not honour `hidden` for the unlabelled input). (radix: `packages/react/checkbox/src/checkbox.test.tsx`: "Legacy Checkbox > given a default Checkbox > should have no accessibility violations")
- Given a legacy `disabled` checkbox, when audited with `axe`, then there are no accessibility violations. (radix: `packages/react/checkbox/src/checkbox.test.tsx`: "Legacy Checkbox > given a disabled Checkbox > should have no accessibility violations")
- Given a legacy `defaultChecked` checkbox, when audited with `axe`, then there are no accessibility violations. (radix: `packages/react/checkbox/src/checkbox.test.tsx`: "Legacy Checkbox > given an uncontrolled `checked` Checkbox > should have no accessibility violations")

### Notes and edge cases

- Given `<Checkbox.Root checked={false}>` inside a `<div onClick>` inside a form, when `checked` is flipped to `true` programmatically by a re-render, then the ancestor `onClick` is NOT called while the form still receives a change event with `true` (regression for radix-ui/primitives#3265, where the synthetic input click bubbled to ancestors). (radix: `packages/react/checkbox/src/checkbox.test.tsx`: "given a Checkbox with a clickable ancestor inside a form > should not trigger the ancestor `onClick` when `checked` is updated programmatically")
- Given an uncontrolled `<Checkbox.Root>` inside a `<div onClick>` inside a form, when the checkbox is really clicked, then the ancestor `onClick` fires exactly once. (radix: `packages/react/checkbox/src/checkbox.test.tsx`: "given a Checkbox with a clickable ancestor inside a form > should trigger the ancestor `onClick` on a real user click")
- Given a controlled `<Checkbox.Root checked={false} onCheckedChange={noop}>` inside a `<div onClick>`, when the user clicks (producing no state change) and the parent later flips `checked` programmatically, then the ancestor `onClick` is not called again while the form still sees the change (regression for radix-ui/primitives#3265). (radix: `packages/react/checkbox/src/checkbox.test.tsx`: "given a Checkbox with a clickable ancestor inside a form > should not trigger the ancestor `onClick` on a programmatic update after a click that did not change `checked`")
- Given `<Checkbox.Root defaultChecked>` with `ref`, `data-testid`, `className`, inline `style` and `onClick`, when rendered, then the unconsumed props land on the rendered element, the ref resolves to it, and clicking fires `onClick`. (radix: `packages/react/checkbox/src/checkbox.test.tsx`: "Checkbox.Root > spreads props it does not consume onto the element it renders")
- Given `<Checkbox.unstable_Trigger>` with unconsumed props, when rendered, then they land on the trigger element, the ref resolves to it, and clicking fires the author `onClick`. (radix: `packages/react/checkbox/src/checkbox.test.tsx`: "Checkbox.unstable_Trigger > spreads props it does not consume onto the element it renders")
- Given `<Checkbox.unstable_BubbleInput>` with an author `onClick`, when the (visually hidden) input is clicked, then the author handler still runs, proving the part composes rather than replaces `onClick` while it dispatches synthetic clicks at forms. (radix: `packages/react/checkbox/src/checkbox.test.tsx`: "Checkbox.unstable_BubbleInput > spreads props it does not consume onto the element it renders")
- Given `<Checkbox.Root />`, the shared `describeConformance` suite runs with `{ refInstanceof: window.HTMLSpanElement, testComponentPropWith: 'span', button: true, render }`, so the part is asserted to forward props, forward refs, support the `render` prop and merge classNames, and to behave as a button. (base-ui: `packages/react/src/checkbox/root/CheckboxRoot.test.tsx`: "describeConformance")
- Given `<Checkbox.Root ref={(element) => { element.focus(); element.blur(); element.click(); }} />`, when the ref callback drives focus, blur and click before the hidden input has mounted, then nothing throws and the checkbox remains `aria-checked="false"`. (base-ui: `packages/react/src/checkbox/root/CheckboxRoot.test.tsx`: "interactions > tolerates imperative interaction in its ref callback before the hidden input mounts")
- Given `<Checkbox.Indicator />`, the shared `describeConformance` suite runs with `{ refInstanceof: window.HTMLSpanElement }` and a custom `render` that wraps the node in a `CheckboxRootContext.Provider` supplying `{ checked: true, disabled: false, readOnly: false, required: false, indeterminate: false, dirty: false, touched: false, valid: null, filled: false, focused: false }`, so the part is asserted to forward props, forward refs, support the `render` prop and merge classNames. (base-ui: `packages/react/src/checkbox/indicator/CheckboxIndicator.test.tsx`: "describeConformance")
- Given `<Checkbox.Indicator />` rendered with no surrounding `<Checkbox.Root>`, when rendering, then it rejects with the error `"Base UI: CheckboxRootContext is missing. Checkbox parts must be placed within <Checkbox.Root>."`. (base-ui: `packages/react/src/checkbox/indicator/CheckboxIndicator.test.tsx`: "throws a descriptive error when rendered outside <Checkbox.Root>")

## checkbox-group

### Roles and attributes

- Given `<CheckboxGroup id="group-id" />`, when rendered, then the element with role `group` has `id="group-id"`. (base-ui: `packages/react/src/checkbox-group/CheckboxGroup.test.tsx`: "prop: id > is forwarded to the root element")
- Given `<CheckboxGroup disabled>` wrapping three `<Checkbox.Root name="red|green|blue">`, when rendered, then every checkbox has `aria-disabled="true"`. (base-ui: `packages/react/src/checkbox-group/CheckboxGroup.test.tsx`: "prop: disabled > disables all checkboxes when `true`")
- Given `<CheckboxGroup disabled={false}>` wrapping three checkboxes, when rendered, then none of them has `aria-disabled="true"`. (base-ui: `packages/react/src/checkbox-group/CheckboxGroup.test.tsx`: "prop: disabled > does not disable all checkboxes when `false`")
- Given `<CheckboxGroup disabled>` where one child sets `disabled={false}`, when rendered, then the group wins and all three checkboxes still have `aria-disabled="true"`. (base-ui: `packages/react/src/checkbox-group/CheckboxGroup.test.tsx`: "prop: disabled > takes precedence over individual checkboxes")
- Given `<Field.Root name="fruits">` wrapping `<CheckboxGroup defaultValue={['apple']}>` with `Field.Item`-wrapped checkboxes `value="apple"` and `value="banana"`, when the group first renders it has no `data-dirty`; after clicking `banana` the element with role `group` has `data-dirty=""`; after clicking `banana` again (returning to the default value) `data-dirty` is removed. (base-ui: `packages/react/src/checkbox-group/CheckboxGroup.test.tsx`: "Field > [data-dirty]")
- Given `<Field.Root name="fruits">` wrapping `<CheckboxGroup defaultValue={['cherry']}>` whose only rendered checkbox is `value="apple"`, when rendered the group has `data-filled=""`, and after clicking `apple` twice it still has `data-filled=""` — the flag tracks the group value, including values with no matching rendered checkbox. (base-ui: `packages/react/src/checkbox-group/CheckboxGroup.test.tsx`: "Field > [data-filled] follows the group value even without a matching rendered checkbox")
- Given `<Field.Root name="apples">` with `<Field.Label>Apples</Field.Label>` and `<CheckboxGroup allValues={['fuji', 'gala']}>` containing a `parent` checkbox plus `value="fuji"` and `value="gala"` (cases: `nativeButton=false`, `nativeButton=true` with `render={<button />}`), when rendered, then exactly 7 ids exist for `nativeButton=false` and 4 for `nativeButton=true`, all unique, and the parent's `aria-controls` split on `" "` equals `[fuji exposed id, gala exposed id]` — the exposed checkboxes, not the hidden inputs. (base-ui: `packages/react/src/checkbox-group/CheckboxGroup.test.tsx`: "Field.Label > keeps checkbox ids unique when the group shares one Field.Root (nativeButton=%s)")
- Given `<Field.Root name="apples">` with `<Field.Label>` and a `<CheckboxGroup>` with no `allValues` containing `value="fuji"` and `value="gala"` (cases: `nativeButton=false`, `nativeButton=true`), when rendered, then exactly 5 ids exist for `nativeButton=false` and 3 for `nativeButton=true`, all unique. (base-ui: `packages/react/src/checkbox-group/CheckboxGroup.test.tsx`: "Field.Label > keeps ids unique without allValues in a shared Field.Root (nativeButton=%s)")
- Given `<Field.Root name="apples">` wrapping `<CheckboxGroup allValues={['fuji', 'gala']}>` where each of the `parent`, `fuji` and `gala` checkboxes sits inside its own native `<label>` with text "All", "Fuji" and "Gala", when rendered, then each checkbox's `aria-labelledby` points at an element whose text content is its own label — every checkbox gets its own accessible name despite sharing one `Field.Root`. - Given `<Field.Root name="apple">` wrapping `<CheckboxGroup defaultValue={['fuji-apple', 'gala-apple']}>` where each `<Field.Item>` has a `<Field.Label>` that wraps its `<Checkbox.Root>` plus text, when rendered, then for each checkbox the label's `for` equals the matching hidden `input[type="checkbox"]`'s `id` and the label's non-null `id` equals the checkbox's `aria-labelledby`; when the third label ("Granny Smith") is clicked, then that checkbox's `onCheckedChange` fires once. - Given `<Field.Root name="apple">` wrapping `<CheckboxGroup defaultValue={['fuji-apple', 'gala-apple']}>` where each `<Field.Item>` holds a `<Checkbox.Root>`, a sibling `<Field.Label>` and a sibling `<Field.Description>`, when rendered, then per item the label's `for` equals the hidden input's `id`, the label's `id` equals the checkbox's `aria-labelledby`, and the description's non-null `id` equals the checkbox's `aria-describedby`; when the "Gala" label text is clicked, then that checkbox's `onCheckedChange` fires once. ### Animation and presence

- Given a `Radio.Indicator` with no exit animation defined, when the group's value moves away from that radio, then the indicator is removed from the DOM. (base-ui: `packages/react/src/radio/indicator/RadioIndicator.test.tsx`: "should remove the indicator when there is no exit animation defined") (browser-mode only)
- Given a `keepMounted` `Radio.Indicator` with a 1ms exit `@keyframes` bound to `[data-ending-style]`, when the group's value moves away, then `onAnimationEnd` fires. (base-ui: `packages/react/src/radio/indicator/RadioIndicator.test.tsx`: "should remove the indicator when the animation finishes") (browser-mode only)
- Given a `Radio.Indicator` with a CSS `transition` and `[data-starting-style] { opacity: 0 }`, when the group's value moves TO that radio, then the indicator mounts and the enter transition runs to completion (`transitionend` fires). (base-ui: `packages/react/src/radio/indicator/RadioIndicator.test.tsx`: "animations > triggers enter animation via data-starting-style when mounting") (browser-mode only)
- Given a `Radio.Indicator` with an exit `@keyframes` bound to `[data-ending-style]`, when the group's value moves away, then the indicator synchronously gains `data-ending-style` and is only removed from the DOM after the animation. (base-ui: `packages/react/src/radio/indicator/RadioIndicator.test.tsx`: "animations > applies data-ending-style before unmount") (browser-mode only)

### Accessibility tooling

- Given a default radio group, when audited with `axe`, then there are no accessibility violations. (radix: `packages/react/radio-group/src/radio-group.test.tsx`: "given a default RadioGroup > should have no accessibility violations")
- Given a `disabled` radio group, when audited with `axe`, then there are no accessibility violations. (radix: `packages/react/radio-group/src/radio-group.test.tsx`: "given a disabled RadioGroup > should have no accessibility violations")
- Given the composable radio group, when audited with `axe`, then there are no accessibility violations. (radix: `packages/react/radio-group/src/radio-group.test.tsx`: "Composable RadioGroup > given a default composable RadioGroup > should have no accessibility violations")
- Given the `Radio` e2e fixture driven by a real screen reader through `@guidepup/playwright`, when the reader is navigated (up to 10 steps) to the item matching `/fuji/i`, then the item text matches `/fuji/i` and the last spoken phrase contains both `/fuji/i` and `/radio/i` — the option's accessible name and its radio role are both announced. (base-ui: `test/screen-reader/radio.spec.ts`: "announces a radio option's accessible name")

### Notes and edge cases

- Given the composable radio group, when rendered, then exactly three `role="radio"` elements exist and all are `aria-checked="false"`. (radix: `packages/react/radio-group/src/radio-group.test.tsx`: "Composable RadioGroup > given a default composable RadioGroup > should render all items unchecked")
- Given a controlled `<RadioGroup name="pet">` inside a `<div onClick>` inside a form, when the controlled value changes from `null` to `'2'` programmatically, then the ancestor `onClick` is not called while the form still receives a change event with `'2'` (regression for radix-ui/primitives#3265). (radix: `packages/react/radio-group/src/radio-group.test.tsx`: "given an uncontrolled RadioGroup in a form > should not trigger a clickable ancestor `onClick` when the value is set programmatically")
- Given an uncontrolled radio group inside a `<div onClick>` inside a form, when a radio is really clicked, then the ancestor `onClick` fires exactly once. (radix: `packages/react/radio-group/src/radio-group.test.tsx`: "given an uncontrolled RadioGroup in a form > should trigger a clickable ancestor `onClick` on a real user click")
- Given a controlled radio group with `value="1"` inside a `<div onClick>`, when the already-selected radio is clicked (no change) and the value is then changed programmatically to `'2'`, then the ancestor `onClick` is not called again (regression for radix-ui/primitives#3265). (radix: `packages/react/radio-group/src/radio-group.test.tsx`: "given an uncontrolled RadioGroup in a form > should not trigger a clickable ancestor `onClick` on a programmatic change after re-selecting the checked radio")
- Given `defaultValue="1"` with each item wrapped in a `<div onClick>` that programmatically clicks its own item via a ref, when the wrapper of the unchecked second radio is clicked, then the first radio ends `aria-checked="false"` and the second `aria-checked="true"` — deselecting the default radio must not bubble a click that re-selects it (regression for radix-ui/primitives#1982). (radix: `packages/react/radio-group/src/radio-group.test.tsx`: "given an uncontrolled RadioGroup in a form > should not re-select the previously checked radio when another is clicked programmatically via a ref")

### Notes and edge cases

- Given `<Switch.Root ref={callbackRef}>` whose ref callback returns a cleanup function, when the tree unmounts, then the cleanup function is invoked (React 19 ref-cleanup contract). (radix: `packages/react/switch/src/switch.test.tsx`: "given a default Switch > should correctly invoke the cleanup function of a ref callback")
- Given a controlled `<Switch.Root checked={false}>` inside a `<div onClick>` inside a form, when `checked` flips to `true` programmatically, then the ancestor `onClick` is not called while the form still receives a change event with `true` (regression for radix-ui/primitives#3265). (radix: `packages/react/switch/src/switch.test.tsx`: "given a Switch with a clickable ancestor inside a form > should not trigger the ancestor `onClick` when `checked` is updated programmatically")

(radix: `packages/react/switch/src/switch.test.tsx`: "given a Switch with a clickable ancestor inside a form > should trigger the ancestor `onClick` on a real user click")
- Given a controlled switch whose parent rejects the change, when the user clicks (no state change) and the parent later flips `checked` programmatically, then the ancestor `onClick` is not called again while the form still sees `true` (regression for radix-ui/primitives#3265). (radix: `packages/react/switch/src/switch.test.tsx`: "given a Switch with a clickable ancestor inside a form > should not trigger the ancestor `onClick` on a programmatic update after a click that did not change `checked`")

### State and controlled/uncontrolled

- Given a controlled `<Slider.Root value={[10, 20, 30]} min={0} max={100}>` with a "shrink" button that sets the value to `[10, 20]`, when thumb 2 is pressed at `clientX: 30` and dragged to `clientX: 50` (yielding `onValueChange([10, 20, 100], { reason: 'drag' })`), the range is then shrunk to two thumbs mid-drag via `fireEvent.click` (deliberately avoiding a `pointerup`), and a further `pointermove` to `clientX: 50` plus `pointerup` occur, then neither `onValueChange` nor `onValueCommitted` fires again — the removed index-2 value is never resurrected. ### RTL and i18n

- Given `<Slider.Root defaultValue={40}><Slider.Value data-testid="output" /></Slider.Root>`, when the root's `format` prop changes to `{ style: 'currency', currency: 'USD' }`, then the output's text content is recomputed and equals `new Intl.NumberFormat(undefined, { style: 'currency', currency: 'USD' }).format(40)` (it was the bare `Intl.NumberFormat(undefined).format(40)` before). (base-ui: `packages/react/src/slider/value/SliderValue.test.tsx`: "recomputes the formatted output when the format option changes")
- Given `<TestSlider value={30} />` inside `<div dir="rtl">` and `<DirectionProvider direction="rtl">` with the control rect mocked to `DOMRect(0, 0, 100, 10)`, then the thumb's `style.insetInlineStart` is `30%`; when `touchstart` at `clientX: 20` is followed by `touchmove` to `clientX: 22`, then `onValueChange` fires twice with values `80` then `78` — the axis is mirrored. (base-ui: `packages/react/src/slider/root/SliderRoot.test.tsx`: "rtl > should handle RTL") (browser-mode only; skipped in WebKit)
- Given `<TestSlider defaultValue={50} format={{ style: 'currency', currency: 'USD' }} />`, then the `Slider.Value` output's text content equals `Intl.NumberFormat(undefined, USD).format(50)` and the thumb input's `aria-valuetext` is that same formatted string. (base-ui: `packages/react/src/slider/root/SliderRoot.test.tsx`: "prop: format > formats the value")
- Given `<TestSlider defaultValue={50} />` with no `format`, then the input has no `aria-valuetext`; when `format` is set to `{ style: 'currency', currency: 'USD' }`, then `aria-valuetext` becomes the USD-formatted `50`. (base-ui: `packages/react/src/slider/root/SliderRoot.test.tsx`: "prop: format > recomputes the thumb aria text when the format option changes")
- Given `<TestRangeSlider defaultValue={[50, 75]} format={USD} />`, then the output text is `` `${format(50)} – ${format(75)}` `` and the two inputs have `aria-valuetext` of `` `${format(50)} start range` `` and `` `${format(75)} end range` ``. (base-ui: `packages/react/src/slider/root/SliderRoot.test.tsx`: "prop: format > formats range values")
- Given `<TestSlider value={70.51} step={0.01} locale="de-DE" format={{ style: 'decimal', minimumFractionDigits: 2, maximumFractionDigits: 2 }} />`, then the `Slider.Value` text matches `new Intl.NumberFormat('de-DE', format).format(70.51)` (German decimal comma). (base-ui: `packages/react/src/slider/root/SliderRoot.test.tsx`: "prop: locale > sets the locale when formatting a single value")
- Given `<TestRangeSlider value={[24.8, 70.51]} step={0.01} locale="de-DE" format={{ style: 'decimal', minimumFractionDigits: 2, maximumFractionDigits: 2 }} />`, then the `Slider.Value` text is the two `de-DE`-formatted numbers joined by ` – `. (base-ui: `packages/react/src/slider/root/SliderRoot.test.tsx`: "prop: locale > sets the locale when formatting a range value")

### SSR and hydration

- Given a 100px-wide `<Slider.Root defaultValue={30}>` with `<Slider.Value />`, `<Slider.Track>`, `<Slider.Indicator />` and one `<Slider.Thumb />` rendered with `renderToString`, then the server-rendered thumb's computed `left` is already `30px` before hydration. (base-ui: `packages/react/src/slider/thumb/SliderThumb.test.tsx`: "server-side rendering > single thumb") (browser-mode only)
- Given a 100px-wide `<Slider.Root defaultValue={30} thumbAlignment="edge">` rendered with `renderToString`, then a `<script>` element is present in the document — the inline pre-hydration script that positions edge-aligned thumbs. (base-ui: `packages/react/src/slider/thumb/SliderThumb.test.tsx`: "server-side rendering > renders the inline pre-hydration script for edge-aligned thumbs") (browser-mode only)
- Given a 100px-wide `<Slider.Root defaultValue={[30, 40]} thumbAlignment="edge">` with two thumbs rendered with `renderToString`, then the container holds exactly one `<script>` and it is contained by the LAST thumb element, so every preceding thumb is already in the DOM when the script runs. (base-ui: `packages/react/src/slider/thumb/SliderThumb.test.tsx`: "server-side rendering > renders a single pre-hydration script with the last thumb") (browser-mode only)
- Given a 100px-wide `<Slider.Root defaultValue={[30, 40]}>` with `<Slider.Thumb index={0} />` and `<Slider.Thumb index={1} />` rendered with `renderToString`, then the server-rendered thumbs' computed `left` values are `30px` and `40px`. (base-ui: `packages/react/src/slider/thumb/SliderThumb.test.tsx`: "server-side rendering > multiple thumbs") (browser-mode only)
- Given `<Slider.Root defaultValue={30} data-testid="root">` with a `<Slider.Label>` and a thumb rendered via `renderToString`, then the label and root both have non-empty `id`s but neither the root nor the `role="slider"` input has an `aria-labelledby` attribute before hydration. (base-ui: `packages/react/src/slider/root/SliderRoot.test.tsx`: "server-side rendering > does not link Slider.Label before hydration")

### Notes and edge cases

- Given `<Slider.Root ref>`, when the component re-renders, then the composed ref identity stays stable across renders (regression for radix-ui/primitives#3963, asserted via the shared `assertStableComposedRef` helper). (radix: `packages/react/slider/src/slider.test.tsx`: "ref stability > keeps a stable composed ref on the root")
- Given `<Slider.Thumb ref>`, when the component re-renders, then the composed ref identity stays stable across renders (regression for radix-ui/primitives#3963). (radix: `packages/react/slider/src/slider.test.tsx`: "ref stability > keeps a stable composed ref on the thumb")
- Given `<Slider.Root>` with `ref`, `data-testid`, `className`, inline `style` and `onClick`, when rendered, then the unconsumed props land on the root element and the ref resolves to it. (radix: `packages/react/slider/src/slider.test.tsx`: "Slider.Root > spreads props it does not consume onto the element it renders")
- Given `<Slider.Track>` with unconsumed props, when rendered, then they land on the track element and the ref resolves to it. (radix: `packages/react/slider/src/slider.test.tsx`: "Slider.Track > spreads props it does not consume onto the element it renders")
- Given `<Slider.Thumb>` with unconsumed props, when rendered, then they land on the thumb element and the ref resolves to it. (radix: `packages/react/slider/src/slider.test.tsx`: "Slider.Thumb > spreads props it does not consume onto the element it renders")
- Given `<Slider.ThumbTrigger>` with unconsumed props, when rendered, then they land on the trigger element and the ref resolves to it. (radix: `packages/react/slider/src/slider.test.tsx`: "Slider.ThumbTrigger > spreads props it does not consume onto the element it renders")
- Given `<Slider.BubbleInput>` with unconsumed props, when rendered, then they land on the hidden input and the ref resolves to it. (radix: `packages/react/slider/src/slider.test.tsx`: "Slider.BubbleInput > spreads props it does not consume onto the element it renders")
- Given the pure helper `roundValueToStep(value, step, min)`, when called as `roundValueToStep(0.35, 0.1, 0.25)`, then it returns exactly `0.35`, preserving the decimal precision implied by the step origin `min` rather than producing a floating-point artifact. (base-ui: `packages/react/src/slider/utils/roundValueToStep.test.ts`: "roundValueToStep > preserves precision from the step origin")
- Given the pure helper `roundValueToStep(value, step, min)`, when called as `roundValueToStep(13.2, 1.5, 10.2)`, then it returns exactly `13.2`, so a step greater than one still keeps one decimal of precision taken from the larger of `step` and `min` precision. (base-ui: `packages/react/src/slider/utils/roundValueToStep.test.ts`: "roundValueToStep > preserves decimal precision for steps greater than one")
- Given the pure helper `getSliderValue(valueInput, index, min, max, range, values)` with `range: false` and `values: [50]`, when called with an out-of-bounds input, then the scalar result is clamped to the range: `getSliderValue(150, 0, 0, 100, false, [50])` returns `100` and `getSliderValue(-10, 0, 0, 100, false, [50])` returns `0`. (base-ui: `packages/react/src/slider/utils/getSliderValue.test.ts`: "getSliderValue > clamps a single value to the min/max range")
- Given `getSliderValue` in range mode where a neighbour's value is exactly `0` (a falsy number), when a thumb is moved past that neighbour, then the neighbour still bounds it rather than being treated as absent: `getSliderValue(5, 0, -10, 10, true, [-10, 0])` returns `[0, 0]` and `getSliderValue(-5, 1, -10, 10, true, [0, 10])` returns `[0, 0]`. (base-ui: `packages/react/src/slider/utils/getSliderValue.test.ts`: "getSliderValue > range neighbours > does not let a thumb cross a neighbour whose value is 0")
- Given `getSliderValue` in range mode with three thumbs `[20, 40, 80]` and the middle thumb (`index: 1`) moving, then the result is clamped between the two real neighbours and re-sorted ascending: input `50` gives `[20, 50, 80]`, input `90` gives `[20, 80, 80]`, input `10` gives `[20, 20, 80]`. (base-ui: `packages/react/src/slider/utils/getSliderValue.test.ts`: "getSliderValue > range neighbours > bounds a thumb between its real neighbours")
- Given `getSliderValue` in range mode with `[-20, 0]` on a `-50..50` range, when the first thumb (no lower neighbour) moves to `-30` then `[-30, 0]` is returned, and when the last thumb (no upper neighbour) moves to `40` then `[-20, 40]` is returned, so a missing neighbour imposes no bound beyond `min`/`max`. (base-ui: `packages/react/src/slider/utils/getSliderValue.test.ts`: "getSliderValue > range neighbours > leaves the outer edges unbounded by missing neighbours")
- Given the pure helper `getPushedThumbValues(values, index, nextValue, min, max, step, minStepsBetweenValues, initialValues?)` with `[20, 40]` and `minStepsBetweenValues: 0`, when thumb `0` moves to `70` (past thumb 1), then the next thumb is pushed forward to the same value and `[70, 70]` is returned. (base-ui: `packages/react/src/slider/utils/getPushedThumbValues.test.ts`: "getPushedThumbValues > pushes the next thumb forward when moving past it")
- Given `getPushedThumbValues([20, 40], 0, 60, 0, 100, 1, 5)`, when thumb `0` is pushed to `60` with `step: 1` and `minStepsBetweenValues: 5`, then the pushed thumb keeps the required gap of `step * minStepsBetweenValues = 5` and `[60, 65]` is returned. (base-ui: `packages/react/src/slider/utils/getPushedThumbValues.test.ts`: "getPushedThumbValues > ensures minimum distance between thumbs while pushing forward")
- Given `getPushedThumbValues([20, 40], 1, -10, 0, 100, 1, 0)`, when the upper thumb is dragged below the lower one and below `min`, then both values collapse to the clamped `min` and `[0, 0]` is returned. (base-ui: `packages/react/src/slider/utils/getPushedThumbValues.test.ts`: "getPushedThumbValues > pushes previous thumbs backward when moving before them")
- Given `getPushedThumbValues([10, 50, 90], 1, 95, 0, 100, 1, 5)`, when the middle thumb is driven to `95`, then the pressed thumb is capped by the space reserved for the thumbs above it and the chain is pushed in sequence, returning `[10, 95, 100]`. (base-ui: `packages/react/src/slider/utils/getPushedThumbValues.test.ts`: "getPushedThumbValues > pushes multiple thumbs in sequence")
- Given `getPushedThumbValues([0, 1], 0, 1.4, 0, 10, 1, 0.4)`, when a fractional `minStepsBetweenValues` of `0.4` is used, then `result[0]` is `1.4` and `result[1]` is exactly `1.8` (no floating-point drift, because every output is passed through `toFixed(12)`). (base-ui: `packages/react/src/slider/utils/getPushedThumbValues.test.ts`: "getPushedThumbValues > allows fractional minimum distances")
- Given `initialValues: [30, 50]` passed as the 8th argument, when thumb `1` is first dragged to `20` (pushing thumb 0 down, yielding `[20, 20]`) and then back up to `35`, then the pushed thumb is restored toward its initial value rather than clinging, returning `[30, 35]`. (base-ui: `packages/react/src/slider/utils/getPushedThumbValues.test.ts`: "getPushedThumbValues > restores pushed thumbs towards their initial value when space allows")
- Given `resolveThumbCollision(behavior, values, currentValues, initialValues, pressedIndex, nextValue, min, max, step, minStepsBetweenValues)` with `behavior: 'none'`, `[20, 40]`, `pressedIndex: 0`, `nextValue: 70`, then the pressed thumb is clamped to its neighbour and the result is `{ value: [40, 40], thumbIndex: 0, didSwap: false }`. (base-ui: `packages/react/src/slider/utils/resolveThumbCollision.test.ts`: "resolveThumbCollision > prevents thumbs from passing each other when behavior is \"none\"")
- Given `resolveThumbCollision('push', [20, 40], undefined, undefined, 0, 70, 0, 100, 1, 0)`, then the neighbour is pushed and the result is `{ value: [70, 70], thumbIndex: 0, didSwap: false }`, with no clinging of the pushed thumb. (base-ui: `packages/react/src/slider/utils/resolveThumbCollision.test.ts`: "resolveThumbCollision > pushes thumbs forward without cling when behavior is \"push\"")
- Given `behavior: 'push'` where `[20, 40]` was first pushed to `[70, 70]` by moving thumb `0` to `70`, when thumb `0` then moves back to `30` with `currentValues` `[70, 70]` and `initialValues` `[20, 40]`, then the pushed thumb stays where it was and the result is `{ value: [30, 70], thumbIndex: 0, didSwap: false }`. (base-ui: `packages/react/src/slider/utils/resolveThumbCollision.test.ts`: "resolveThumbCollision > keeps pushed thumbs in place when moving backward in push mode")
- Given `resolveThumbCollision('swap', [20, 40], undefined, undefined, 0, 65, 0, 100, 1, 0)`, then the thumbs exchange places and the result is `{ value: [40, 65], thumbIndex: 1, didSwap: true }`, so the caller must follow the returned `thumbIndex` for the rest of the drag. (base-ui: `packages/react/src/slider/utils/resolveThumbCollision.test.ts`: "resolveThumbCollision > swaps thumbs when behavior is \"swap\"")
- Given `behavior: 'swap'` with `minStepsBetweenValues: 10` and start values `[20, 80]`, when thumb `0` moves to `85` then the result is `{ value: [70, 85], thumbIndex: 1, didSwap: true }`, and when the drag continues from that state with `pressedIndex: 1` to `95` then the result is `{ value: [70, 95], thumbIndex: 1, didSwap: false }`, so the swapped identity persists without swapping again. (base-ui: `packages/react/src/slider/utils/resolveThumbCollision.test.ts`: "resolveThumbCollision > maintains swap continuity with minimum steps when provided current and initial values")
- Given `resolveThumbCollision('swap', [25, 45], [40, 45], [25, 45], 0, 44, 0, 100, 1, 5)`, when the pressed thumb has not yet reached the neighbour's value, then no swap occurs and the result is `{ value: [40, 45], thumbIndex: 0, didSwap: false }`. (base-ui: `packages/react/src/slider/utils/resolveThumbCollision.test.ts`: "resolveThumbCollision > does not swap before reaching neighbour value with minimum steps")
- Given `resolveThumbCollision('swap', [25, 45], [40, 45], [25, 45], 0, 45, 0, 100, 1, 5)`, when the pressed thumb reaches exactly the neighbour's value `45`, then the swap fires and the result is `{ value: [40, 45], thumbIndex: 1, didSwap: true }` — the visible values are unchanged but the active thumb index moves to `1`. (base-ui: `packages/react/src/slider/utils/resolveThumbCollision.test.ts`: "resolveThumbCollision > swaps once reaching the neighbour value with minimum steps")
- Given `resolveThumbCollision('swap', [25, 45], [25, 40], [25, 45], 1, 29, 0, 100, 1, 5)`, when the upper thumb moves backward but has not reached the lower thumb's value, then no swap occurs and the result is `{ value: [25, 30], thumbIndex: 1, didSwap: false }` (clamped to the `minStepsBetweenValues` gap of 5). (base-ui: `packages/react/src/slider/utils/resolveThumbCollision.test.ts`: "resolveThumbCollision > does not swap backward before reaching neighbour value with minimum steps")
- Given `resolveThumbCollision('swap', [25, 45], [25, 40], [25, 45], 1, 25, 0, 100, 1, 5)`, when the upper thumb moves backward to exactly the lower thumb's value `25`, then the swap fires and the result is `{ value: [25, 30], thumbIndex: 0, didSwap: true }`. (base-ui: `packages/react/src/slider/utils/resolveThumbCollision.test.ts`: "resolveThumbCollision > swaps backward once reaching the neighbour value with minimum steps")
- Given `resolveThumbCollision('swap', [40, 45], [40, 45], [25, 45], 0, 46, 0, 100, 1, 5)` where the neighbour was already clamped to `45` by the minimum distance, when the pressed thumb crosses to `46`, then the clamped neighbour is not dragged along and the result is `{ value: [40, 46], thumbIndex: 1, didSwap: true }`. (base-ui: `packages/react/src/slider/utils/resolveThumbCollision.test.ts`: "resolveThumbCollision > does not move the clamped neighbour when swapping across with minimum steps")
- Given `resolveThumbCollision('swap', [20, 40], [20, 40, 60], [20, 40], 1, 70, 0, 100, 1, 0)` where the controlled range gained a third thumb mid-interaction, then the live `currentValues` win over the stale `values` and the result is `{ value: [20, 60, 70], thumbIndex: 2, didSwap: true }`. (base-ui: `packages/react/src/slider/utils/resolveThumbCollision.test.ts`: "resolveThumbCollision > uses current values when a controlled range grows during a swap interaction")
- Given `resolveThumbCollision('push', [20, 40], [20], [20, 40], 0, 30, 0, 100, 1, 0)` where the live values shrank to a single item mid-interaction, then the slider is no longer treated as a range and the result is the scalar `{ value: 30, thumbIndex: 0, didSwap: false }`. (base-ui: `packages/react/src/slider/utils/resolveThumbCollision.test.ts`: "resolveThumbCollision > returns a scalar when the live values shrink to one item during an interaction")

## number-field

### Roles and attributes

- Given `<NumberField disabled />` (Root wrapping Group with Input, Increment, Decrement, ScrubArea), when rendered, then the `role="textbox"` input has the `disabled` attribute. (base-ui: `packages/react/src/number-field/root/NumberFieldRoot.test.tsx`: "prop: disabled > should disable the input")
- Given `<NumberField readOnly />`, when rendered, then the textbox input has the `readonly` attribute. (base-ui: `packages/react/src/number-field/root/NumberFieldRoot.test.tsx`: "prop: readOnly > should mark the input as readOnly")
- Given `<Field.Root><NumberField.Root readOnly><NumberField.Input /></NumberField.Root></Field.Root>`, when the input is focused then blurred with `fireEvent.focus`/`fireEvent.blur`, then it gains `data-focused=""` on focus and loses it on blur even though the field is readOnly. (base-ui: `packages/react/src/number-field/root/NumberFieldRoot.test.tsx`: "prop: readOnly > keeps focus state in sync on a readOnly field")
- Given `<NumberField readOnly />`, when rendered, then the input has `readonly`, neither the `button` named "Increase" nor "Decrease" has `aria-readonly` (invalid on the button role), and both steppers instead expose `aria-disabled="true"`. (base-ui: `packages/react/src/number-field/root/NumberFieldRoot.test.tsx`: "prop: readOnly > does not render aria-readonly on stepper buttons")
- Given `<NumberField required />`, when rendered, then the textbox input has the `required` attribute. (base-ui: `packages/react/src/number-field/root/NumberFieldRoot.test.tsx`: "prop: required > should mark the input as required")
- Given `<Field.Root>` wrapping a NumberField Root and Input, when the input is focused and then blurred, then the input has `data-touched=""`. (base-ui: `packages/react/src/number-field/root/NumberFieldRoot.test.tsx`: "Field > [data-touched]")
- Given `<Field.Root>` wrapping a NumberField Root and Input, when the input value changes to `'1'`, then the input gains `data-dirty=""` (absent before the change). (base-ui: `packages/react/src/number-field/root/NumberFieldRoot.test.tsx`: "Field > [data-dirty]")
- Given `<Field.Root>` wrapping an empty NumberField, when the input changes to `'1'` and then back to `''`, then `data-filled=""` is added on the first change and removed when cleared. (base-ui: `packages/react/src/number-field/root/NumberFieldRoot.test.tsx`: "Field > [data-filled] > adds [data-filled] attribute when filled")
- Given `<Field.Root>` wrapping `<NumberField.Root defaultValue={1}>`, when rendered, then the input already has `data-filled`, and clearing it to `''` removes the attribute. (base-ui: `packages/react/src/number-field/root/NumberFieldRoot.test.tsx`: "Field > [data-filled] > has [data-filled] attribute when already filled")
- Given `<Field.Root>` wrapping a NumberField, when the input is focused and blurred, then the input carries `data-focused=""` only while focused (test is named "[data-filled]" but asserts `data-focused`). (base-ui: `packages/react/src/number-field/root/NumberFieldRoot.test.tsx`: "Field > [data-filled]")
- Given `<Field.Root>` wrapping a NumberField, when focus/blur/focus happen in sequence, then `data-focused=""` is re-added on the second focus, so the attribute is not one-shot. (base-ui: `packages/react/src/number-field/root/NumberFieldRoot.test.tsx`: "Field > adds [data-focused] attribute on every focus")
- Given `<Field.Root>` with a NumberField and `<Field.Label />`, when rendered, then the label's `for` attribute equals the textbox input's `id`. (base-ui: `packages/react/src/number-field/root/NumberFieldRoot.test.tsx`: "Field > Field.Label")
- Given `<Field.Root>` with `<NumberField.Input aria-describedby="external-description" />` and `<Field.Description />`, when rendered, then the input's `aria-describedby` is `"external-description <description id>"`, merging the consumer value with the generated one. (base-ui: `packages/react/src/number-field/root/NumberFieldRoot.test.tsx`: "Field > Field.Description")
- Given `<NumberField />`, when rendered, then the input has `inputmode="numeric"`. (base-ui: `packages/react/src/number-field/root/NumberFieldRoot.test.tsx`: "prop: inputMode > should set the inputMode to numeric")
- Given `<NumberField.Root min={0}><NumberField.Input /></NumberField.Root>` with `platform.os.ios`/`platform.os.apple` mocked to `true`, when rendered, then the textbox has `inputmode="decimal"` because negative values are impossible and the iOS numeric keypad lacks a decimal key (`.iOS.test.tsx`). - Given `<NumberField.Root min={-5}><NumberField.Input /></NumberField.Root>` with iOS mocked, when rendered, then the textbox has `inputmode="text"` because the iOS numeric keypad has no minus key (`.iOS.test.tsx`). - Given `<NumberField.Root readOnly>` with `<NumberField.Increment />` and `<NumberField.Input />`, when rendered, then the button's `aria-controls` equals the input's `id`. (base-ui: `packages/react/src/number-field/increment/NumberFieldIncrement.test.tsx`: "disabled state > exposes aria-controls on the stepper")
- Given `<NumberField.Root disabled>` with `<NumberField.Increment className={spy} />`, when rendered, then the className function's state argument has `disabled: true`. (base-ui: `packages/react/src/number-field/increment/NumberFieldIncrement.test.tsx`: "disabled state > prop: className > when root is disabled")
- Given `<NumberField.Root>` with `<NumberField.Increment disabled className={spy} />`, when rendered, then the className function's state argument has `disabled: true`. (base-ui: `packages/react/src/number-field/increment/NumberFieldIncrement.test.tsx`: "disabled state > prop: className > when button is disabled")
- Given `<NumberField.Root><NumberField.Decrement /></NumberField.Root>`, when rendered, then an element labelled `'Decrease'` exists (default `aria-label`). (base-ui: `packages/react/src/number-field/decrement/NumberFieldDecrement.test.tsx`: "has decrease label")
- Given `<NumberField.Root disabled>` with `<NumberField.Decrement className={spy} />`, when rendered, then the className function's state argument has `disabled: true`. - Given `<NumberField.Root>` with `<NumberField.Decrement disabled className={spy} />`, when rendered, then the className function's state argument has `disabled: true`.
