### Keyboard

- Given `<NumberField defaultValue={12.3} locale="en-US" />` with the input focused and a selection from index 1 through the character after the decimal separator, when `keyDown` with key `'.'` fires, then the event is not canceled (`fireEvent` returns `true`), so a decimal separator can be typed over a selection. (base-ui: `packages/react/src/number-field/root/NumberFieldRoot.test.tsx`: "typing behavior (parseable changes) > allows typing a decimal while replacing a selection")
- Given `<NumberField defaultValue={12.34} locale="de-DE" format={{ style: 'currency', currency: 'EUR', minimumFractionDigits: 2, maximumFractionDigits: 2 }} />` with the input focused, when `Backspace` is pressed (not canceled) and the value changes to the formatted string minus its last character, then the input shows that string and `onValueChange` fires once with `12.34`, so the trailing currency symbol after a locale literal can be deleted. (base-ui: `packages/react/src/number-field/root/NumberFieldRoot.test.tsx`: "typing behavior (parseable changes) > allows backspace to remove trailing currency symbol that follows a locale literal")
- Given `<NumberField defaultValue={0} min={-10} max={10} onValueCommitted={fn} />` with the input focused, when `ArrowUp`, `ArrowDown`, `Home`, `End` are pressed in order, then `onValueCommitted` fires once per key with `1`, `0`, `-10` (Home jumps to min) and `10` (End jumps to max). (base-ui: `packages/react/src/number-field/root/NumberFieldRoot.test.tsx`: "prop: onValueCommitted > fires on keyboard interactions (ArrowUp/Down/Home/End)")
- Given `<NumberField defaultValue={5} min={0} max={5} onValueCommitted={fn} />` with the input focused, when `ArrowUp` and then `End` are pressed (both no-ops at max), then `onValueCommitted` is not called; a following `ArrowDown` commits once with `4`. (base-ui: `packages/react/src/number-field/root/NumberFieldRoot.test.tsx`: "prop: onValueCommitted > does not fire on keyboard steps that do not change the value")
- Given `<NumberField min={0} allowOutOfRange />` with the input focused, when `keyDown` with key `'-'` fires, then `preventDefault` is never called and a subsequent change to `'-1'` leaves the input showing `'-1'`, so native underflow validation stays reachable. (base-ui: `packages/react/src/number-field/root/NumberFieldRoot.test.tsx`: "prop: allowOutOfRange > allows typing a negative value via keyboard when min is 0")
- Given `<NumberField />` with the input focused, when `keyDown` fires with `which: 229` (the IME composition key code), then `preventDefault` is not called. (base-ui: `packages/react/src/number-field/root/NumberFieldRoot.test.tsx`: "integration: exotic inputs and IME > allows composition key events (IME) without preventing default")
- Given `<NumberField />` whose input is focused and holds `'123'`, when `Backspace`, `Delete`, `ArrowLeft`, `ArrowRight`, `Tab` and `Enter` are each pressed, then `preventDefault` is never called for any of them. (base-ui: `packages/react/src/number-field/root/NumberFieldRoot.test.tsx`: "should allow navigation keys and not prevent their default behavior")
- Given `<NumberField defaultValue={5} />` with no `min`/`max` and the input focused, when `Home` and `End` are pressed, then `preventDefault` is not called, leaving native caret movement intact. (base-ui: `packages/react/src/number-field/root/NumberFieldRoot.test.tsx`: "does not prevent native caret movement for Home/End without min/max")
- Given `<NumberField defaultValue={5} />` with the input focused, when `PageUp`, `PageDown`, `Insert` and `F5` are pressed, then `preventDefault` is not called for any of them. (base-ui: `packages/react/src/number-field/root/NumberFieldRoot.test.tsx`: "does not swallow non-printing keys it does not handle")
- Given `<NumberField.Root><NumberField.Input /></NumberField.Root>` with the input focused, when `keyDown` with key `'a'` fires, then the input value stays `''`. (base-ui: `packages/react/src/number-field/input/NumberFieldInput.test.tsx`: "should not allow non-numeric characters on keydown")
- Given `<NumberField.Root defaultValue={0}>` with the input focused, when `ArrowUp` is pressed, then the input shows `'1'`. (base-ui: `packages/react/src/number-field/input/NumberFieldInput.test.tsx`: "should increment on keydown ArrowUp")
- Given `<NumberField.Root defaultValue={0}>` with the input focused, when `ArrowDown` is pressed, then the input shows `'-1'`. (base-ui: `packages/react/src/number-field/input/NumberFieldInput.test.tsx`: "should decrement on keydown ArrowDown")
- Given `<NumberField.Root min={-10} max={10}>` with the input focused, when `Home` is pressed, then the input shows `'-10'`. (base-ui: `packages/react/src/number-field/input/NumberFieldInput.test.tsx`: "should set the value to min on keydown Home")
- Given `<NumberField.Root min={-10} max={10}>` with the input focused, when `End` is pressed, then the input shows `'10'`. (base-ui: `packages/react/src/number-field/input/NumberFieldInput.test.tsx`: "should set the value to max on keydown End")
- Given `<NumberField.Root defaultValue={0.15} smallStep={0.1} snapOnStep>` with the input focused, when `ArrowUp` with `altKey: true` then `ArrowDown` with `altKey: true` are pressed, then the input shows `Intl.NumberFormat().format(0.3)` and then `format(0.2)`, snapping to multiples of the small step. (base-ui: `packages/react/src/number-field/input/NumberFieldInput.test.tsx`: "uses smallStep and snapOnStep when holding Alt with ArrowUp/ArrowDown")
- Given a controlled `<NumberField.Root value={0} smallStep={0.0001}>` with the input focused, when `ArrowUp` with `altKey: true` is pressed, then `onValueChange` last reports `0.0001` while the displayed text rounds to `'0'`. (base-ui: `packages/react/src/number-field/input/NumberFieldInput.test.tsx`: "advances by a smallStep finer than 3 fraction digits")
- Given `<NumberField.Root defaultValue={1.23456} onValueChange>` whose display rounds to `(1.23456).toLocaleString()`, when the input is focused and `ArrowUp` is pressed, then `onValueChange` last reports `2.23456`, stepping the full-precision numeric state rather than the rounded display text. (base-ui: `packages/react/src/number-field/input/NumberFieldInput.test.tsx`: "increments with keyboard from numeric state, not rounded display text")
- Given `<NumberField.Root defaultValue={1.23456} onValueChange>`, when the input is focused and `ArrowDown` is pressed, then `onValueChange` last reports `0.23456`, not the `0.235` the rounded display would give. (base-ui: `packages/react/src/number-field/input/NumberFieldInput.test.tsx`: "decrements with keyboard from numeric state, not rounded display text")
- Given a controlled NumberField starting at `null`, when the user types `1.23456`, blurs (display becomes `(1.23456).toLocaleString()`), refocuses and presses `ArrowUp`, then `onValueChange` last reports `2.23456`. (base-ui: `packages/react/src/number-field/input/NumberFieldInput.test.tsx`: "increments with keyboard from numeric state after a no-edit blur cycle")
- Given `<NumberField.Root value={0} onValueChange>` whose parent never mirrors the reported value back into `value`, when the input is focused, changed to `'1.5'` (reported as `1.5`) and `ArrowUp` is pressed, then `onValueChange` last reports `2.5`, stepping from the dirty text rather than the stale numeric state (which would give `1`). (base-ui: `packages/react/src/number-field/input/NumberFieldInput.test.tsx`: "steps keyboard from dirty input text when the controlled value lags onValueChange")
- Given `<NumberField.Root value={0} onValueChange>` with never-mirrored dirty text `'1.5'`, when `ArrowLeft` (a non-mutating navigation key) is pressed and then `ArrowUp`, then `onValueChange` last reports `2.5`: the navigation key must not mark the input as synced. (base-ui: `packages/react/src/number-field/input/NumberFieldInput.test.tsx`: "keeps dirty-input authority after a non-mutating key so the next keyboard step uses dirty text")
- Given `<NumberField.Root format={{ style: 'percent' }}><NumberField.Input /></NumberField.Root>` with the input focused, when native `keydown` events are dispatched for `'−'` (U+2212 MINUS SIGN), `'＋'` (U+FF0B FULLWIDTH PLUS), `'‰'` and `'１'`, then none is canceled (`dispatchEvent` returns `true`). (base-ui: `packages/react/src/number-field/input/NumberFieldInput.test.tsx`: "allows unicode plus/minus, permille and fullwidth digits on keydown when formatted as percent")
- Given `<NumberField.Root>` with no `format` and the input focused, when native `keydown` events are dispatched for `'%'` and `'‰'`, then both are canceled (`dispatchEvent` returns `false`). (base-ui: `packages/react/src/number-field/input/NumberFieldInput.test.tsx`: "blocks percent and permille symbols on keydown when not formatted as percent")
- Given `<NumberField.Root locale="de-DE">` (decimal `','`, group `'.'`) with the input focused, when a first `','` keydown is dispatched it is allowed (`true`); after the value becomes `'1,'` a second `','` keydown is canceled (`false`); `'.'` keydowns stay allowed (`true`) repeatedly, including after the value becomes `'1.,'`. (base-ui: `packages/react/src/number-field/input/NumberFieldInput.test.tsx`: "applies locale-aware decimal/group gating (de-DE)")
- Given `<NumberField.Root locale="pl-PL">` (space-like group separator) with the input focused, when a `' '` (plain space) keydown is dispatched it is allowed (`true`), and a change to `'1 234'` is kept in the input. (base-ui: `packages/react/src/number-field/input/NumberFieldInput.test.tsx`: "allows space key when locale uses space-like grouping (pl-PL)")
- Given `<NumberField.Root min={-10} max={10} defaultValue={-5}>` showing `'-5'` with the input focused and the caret collapsed at index 2, when a `'-'` keydown is dispatched, then it is canceled (`false`), blocking a second minus sign. (base-ui: `packages/react/src/number-field/input/NumberFieldInput.test.tsx`: "single sign character > blocks a second minus sign when the existing one is not selected")
- Given `<NumberField.Root min={-10} max={10} defaultValue={-5}>` showing `'-5'` with the selection range `(0, 1)` covering the existing sign, when a `'-'` keydown is dispatched, then it is allowed (`true`). (base-ui: `packages/react/src/number-field/input/NumberFieldInput.test.tsx`: "single sign character > allows a minus sign that replaces the selected existing sign")
- Given `<NumberField.Root min={-10} max={10} defaultValue={-5}>` with the whole value selected `(0, value.length)`, when a `'-'` keydown is dispatched, then it is allowed (`true`). (base-ui: `packages/react/src/number-field/input/NumberFieldInput.test.tsx`: "single sign character > allows a minus sign when the whole value is selected")

### Pointer

- Given `<NumberField defaultValue={0} onValueCommitted={fn} />`, when the "Increase" button is clicked and then the "Decrease" button, then `onValueCommitted` fires once per click with `1` then `0` and the input shows `'1'` then `'0'`. (base-ui: `packages/react/src/number-field/root/NumberFieldRoot.test.tsx`: "prop: onValueCommitted > fires once per press-release even after mouseleave/mouseenter during a hold")
- Given `<NumberField defaultValue={5} />` with no `step` prop, when "Increase" is clicked, then the input shows `'6'`, so `step` defaults to 1. (base-ui: `packages/react/src/number-field/root/NumberFieldRoot.test.tsx`: "prop: step > defaults to 1")
- Given `<NumberField defaultValue={4} step={2} />`, when "Increase" is clicked, then the input shows `'6'`. (base-ui: `packages/react/src/number-field/root/NumberFieldRoot.test.tsx`: "prop: step > should increment the value by the `step` prop")
- Given `<NumberField defaultValue={5} step={2} snapOnStep />`, when "Increase" is clicked, then the input shows `'6'`, the nearest multiple of the step above 5. (base-ui: `packages/react/src/number-field/root/NumberFieldRoot.test.tsx`: "prop: step > should snap when incrementing to the nearest multiple of the `step` prop")
- Given `<NumberField defaultValue={6} step={2} />`, when "Decrease" is clicked, then the input shows `'4'`. (base-ui: `packages/react/src/number-field/root/NumberFieldRoot.test.tsx`: "prop: step > should decrement the value by the `step` prop")
- Given `<NumberField defaultValue={5} step={2} snapOnStep />`, when "Decrease" is clicked, then the input shows `'4'`, the nearest multiple of the step below 5. ### Positioning

- Given `<NumberField.Root defaultValue={0}>` with `<NumberField.ScrubArea teleportDistance={100} style={{ position: 'fixed', left: 100, top: 100, width: 20, height: 20 }}>` containing a cursor, and `requestPointerLock` stubbed to resolve, when scrubbing starts the bare cursor has `offsetWidth` 0; a `movementX: 5000` past the right bound (120 + 100/2) wraps its `style.transform` to contain `translate3d(50px,`, and a following `movementX: -5000` past the left bound (100 - 100/2) wraps it to contain `translate3d(170px,`. (base-ui: `packages/react/src/number-field/scrub-area/NumberFieldScrubArea.test.tsx`: "prop: teleportDistance > wraps the virtual cursor around the allowed bounds") (browser-mode only; Chromium/Firefox only)

### Notes and edge cases

- Given `<NumberField.Root />`, the shared `describeConformance` suite runs with `{ refInstanceof: window.HTMLDivElement, render }` and no skips, so the root is asserted to forward props, forward refs, support the `render` prop and merge classNames on a `div`. (base-ui: `packages/react/src/number-field/root/NumberFieldRoot.test.tsx`: "describeConformance")
- Given `<NumberField />`, when `'123'` is pasted via a real `DataTransfer` with `text/plain` and the change is applied, then the input shows `'123'`. (base-ui: `packages/react/src/number-field/root/NumberFieldRoot.test.tsx`: "pasting > should allow pasting a valid number") (browser-mode only)
- Given `<NumberField />`, when `'abc'` is pasted via a real `DataTransfer` and a change to `'abc'` follows, then the input stays `''` and remains `''` after `blur`. (base-ui: `packages/react/src/number-field/root/NumberFieldRoot.test.tsx`: "pasting > should not allow pasting an invalid number") (browser-mode only)
- Given `<NumberField defaultValue={1} onValueChange={fn} />` with the input focused and selected, when `'abc'` is pasted, then the input stays `'1'` and `onValueChange` is not called. (base-ui: `packages/react/src/number-field/root/NumberFieldRoot.test.tsx`: "pasting at the caret > ignores a paste that does not parse to a number")
- Given `<NumberField defaultValue={1} readOnly />` with the input focused and selected, when `'9'` is pasted, then the input stays `'1'`. (base-ui: `packages/react/src/number-field/root/NumberFieldRoot.test.tsx`: "pasting at the caret > does not paste into a readOnly field")
- Given `<NumberField defaultValue={123} onValueChange={fn} />` with the caret at index 3 (collapsed), when `'5'` is pasted, then the input shows `'1235'` and `onValueChange` last reports `1235`, so the paste inserts at the caret instead of replacing everything. (base-ui: `packages/react/src/number-field/root/NumberFieldRoot.test.tsx`: "pasting at the caret > inserts pasted text at the caret instead of replacing the whole value")
- Given `<NumberField defaultValue={123} />` with the selection range `(1, 2)`, when `'9'` is pasted, then the input shows `'193'`. (base-ui: `packages/react/src/number-field/root/NumberFieldRoot.test.tsx`: "pasting at the caret > replaces the selected range when pasting over a selection")
- Given `<NumberField defaultValue={123} />` with the selection range `(1, 2)`, when `'9'` is pasted, then the input shows `'193'` and both `selectionStart` and `selectionEnd` are `2`, just after the pasted text. (base-ui: `packages/react/src/number-field/root/NumberFieldRoot.test.tsx`: "pasting at the caret > keeps the caret just after the pasted text")
- Given `<NumberField defaultValue={12} onValueChange={fn} />` with the input focused and selected, when `'abc'` is pasted, then the value contract is untouched: the input keeps `'12'` and `onValueChange` is never called. - Given the type of `NumberField.Root.Props['onValueChange']`, the value parameter is exactly `number | null` and the `details` union narrows by `reason`: `REASONS.wheel` gives `event: WheelEvent` (assigning it to `PointerEvent` is a `@ts-expect-error`), `REASONS.incrementPress` gives `PointerEvent | MouseEvent | TouchEvent`, and `REASONS.inputClear` gives `InputEvent | FocusEvent | Event` (assigning it to `KeyboardEvent` is a `@ts-expect-error`) — type-only assertions, no runtime. (base-ui: `packages/react/src/number-field/root/NumberFieldRoot.spec.tsx`: "assertNumberFieldChange")
- Given the type of `NumberField.Root.Props['onValueCommitted']`, the value parameter is exactly `number | null` and the `details` union narrows by `reason`: `REASONS.wheel` gives `event: WheelEvent`, `REASONS.scrub` gives `event: PointerEvent`, and `REASONS.inputClear` gives `InputEvent | FocusEvent | Event`; both handlers typecheck when passed to `<NumberField.Root defaultValue={0} onValueChange onValueCommitted />` — type-only assertions, no runtime. (base-ui: `packages/react/src/number-field/root/NumberFieldRoot.spec.tsx`: "assertNumberFieldCommit")
- Given `<NumberField.Input render={(props) => ...} />`, the render callback's props are typed as native `<input>` props: `props.disabled` and `props.readOnly` are each `boolean | undefined` — type-only assertion, no runtime. ## tabs

### Roles and attributes

- Given `<Tabs.Root defaultValue="one" asChild>` wrapping an `<article>` that contains a `<Tabs.List />`, when rendered, then the element is an `ARTICLE` with `data-orientation="horizontal"`, keeps `className="custom-class"` and the inline `outlineColor: rgb(1, 2, 3)`, the ref resolves to it, and clicking fires the author `onClick`. (radix: `packages/react/tabs/src/tabs.test.tsx`: "Tabs.Root > forwards props to the child element when `asChild` is set")
- Given `<Tabs.List asChild>` wrapping an `<article>` with one trigger, when rendered, then the element is an `ARTICLE` with `role="tablist"` and `aria-orientation="horizontal"`, keeps the className and inline `outlineColor`, the ref resolves to it, and clicking fires the author `onClick`. (radix: `packages/react/tabs/src/tabs.test.tsx`: "Tabs.List > forwards props to the child element when `asChild` is set")
- Given `<Tabs.Trigger value="one" asChild>` wrapping `<button type="button">` inside a root defaulted to `"one"`, when rendered, then the element is a `BUTTON` with `role="tab"`, `aria-selected="true"` and `data-state="active"`, keeps the className and inline `outlineColor`, the ref resolves to it, and clicking fires the author `onClick`. (radix: `packages/react/tabs/src/tabs.test.tsx`: "Tabs.Trigger > forwards props to the child element when `asChild` is set")
- Given `<Tabs.Content value="one" asChild>` wrapping an `<article>` inside a root defaulted to `"one"`, when rendered, then the element is an `ARTICLE` with `role="tabpanel"` and `data-state="active"`, keeps the className and inline `outlineColor`, the ref resolves to it, and clicking fires the author `onClick`. (radix: `packages/react/tabs/src/tabs.test.tsx`: "Tabs.Content > forwards props to the child element when `asChild` is set")
- Given `<Tabs.Root defaultValue="tab-0">` with four `<Tabs.Tab>` (two with explicit `id`) and four `<Tabs.Panel keepMounted>` declared in a different order than the tabs, when rendered, then each panel's `aria-labelledby` equals the `id` of the tab with the matching `value`, not the tab at the same DOM index. (base-ui: `packages/react/src/tabs/root/TabsRoot.test.tsx`: "prop: children > sets the aria-labelledby attribute on tab panels to the corresponding tab id")
- Given the same out-of-order tabs/panels tree, when rendered, then each tab's `aria-controls` equals the `id` of the panel with the matching `value`. (base-ui: `packages/react/src/tabs/root/TabsRoot.test.tsx`: "prop: children > sets the aria-controls attribute on tabs to the corresponding tab panel id")
- Given `<Tabs.Root>` with no `value`/`defaultValue` and two tabs plus two `keepMounted` panels, when rendered, then tab 0 gets `aria-controls` pointing at panel 0, tab 1 at panel 1, and each panel gets `aria-labelledby` pointing back at its tab. (base-ui: `packages/react/src/tabs/root/TabsRoot.test.tsx`: "prop: children > sets aria-controls on the first tab when no value is provided")
- Given panels WITHOUT `keepMounted` (only the selected panel is mounted), when the second tab is clicked, then `aria-controls` is removed from the previously selected tab and set on the newly selected tab pointing at the freshly mounted panel's `id`; a tab whose panel is not mounted has no `aria-controls` at all. (base-ui: `packages/react/src/tabs/root/TabsRoot.test.tsx`: "prop: children > syncs aria-controls to the mounted tab panel when keepMounted is false")
- Given `<Tabs.Root value={1}>` with tabs `0` and `1`, when rendered, then tab 0 has `aria-selected="false"` and tab 1 has `aria-selected="true"`. (base-ui: `packages/react/src/tabs/root/TabsRoot.test.tsx`: "prop: value > should pass selected prop to children")
- Given `<Tabs.Root value={0}>` with a `<Tabs.List>`, when rendered with the default horizontal orientation, then the `tablist` element has NO `aria-orientation` attribute. (base-ui: `packages/react/src/tabs/root/TabsRoot.test.tsx`: "prop: orientation > does not add aria-orientation by default")
- Given `<Tabs.Root value={0} orientation="vertical">`, when rendered, then the `tablist` element has `aria-orientation="vertical"`. (base-ui: `packages/react/src/tabs/root/TabsRoot.test.tsx`: "prop: orientation > adds the proper aria-orientation when vertical")

### Positioning

- Given `<Tabs.Root value={2}>` with three tabs and a `<Tabs.Indicator>`, when `value` is changed to 3 and then to 1, then the indicator's `--active-tab-left`/`--active-tab-right`/`--active-tab-top`/`--active-tab-bottom`/`--active-tab-width`/`--active-tab-height` are recomputed for each new active tab. (base-ui: `packages/react/src/tabs/indicator/TabsIndicator.test.tsx`: "rendering > should update the position variables when the tab list is resized") (browser-mode only)

- Given the last of three 80x32 tabs selected inside a wrapper with `transform: rotate(40deg)`, when the indicator is positioned via `--active-tab-width`/`--active-tab-height`/`translate(var(--active-tab-left), var(--active-tab-top))`, then its on-screen rect coincides with the active tab's on all four edges within 1px and it has no `hidden` attribute. - Given the same server render, when inspected, then the emitted `<script>`'s `innerHTML` is non-empty (the real minified script is inlined, not a browser stub). (base-ui: `packages/react/src/tabs/indicator/TabsIndicator.test.tsx`: "pre-hydration rendering > inlines the script contents during server-side rendering") (jsdom only)
- Given `<CSPProvider nonce="test-nonce">` wrapping a server-rendered `<Tabs.Indicator renderBeforeHydration />`, when rendered to string, then the pre-hydration `<script>` carries `nonce="test-nonce"`. (base-ui: `packages/react/src/tabs/indicator/TabsIndicator.test.tsx`: "pre-hydration rendering > applies the CSP nonce to the pre-hydration script")
- Given server markup containing the pre-hydration `<script>`, when the tree is hydrated, then the script element survives hydration (only its body is stubbed on the client, avoiding a recoverable hydration error) and is removed from the DOM once hydration completes. (base-ui: `packages/react/src/tabs/indicator/TabsIndicator.test.tsx`: "pre-hydration rendering > keeps the script during hydration and removes it afterwards") (jsdom only)
- Given hand-built server markup (a `role="tablist"` with a `[data-active]` button, a sibling button and a `hidden` `<span>` indicator) inside a host with `display: none`, with the real generated pre-hydration script executed inline, when the host becomes visible, then the script removes `hidden` from the indicator and sets `--active-tab-width` to the active tab's `offsetWidth` in px. (base-ui: `packages/react/src/tabs/indicator/TabsIndicator.test.tsx`: "pre-hydration script execution > positions the indicator once a hidden streamed segment becomes visible") (browser-mode only)
- Given the same hidden server markup, when `data-active` is removed from the captured tab (simulating hydration selecting a value with no matching tab) before the host is revealed, then after 100ms the indicator still has `hidden` — the script must not resurrect it. (base-ui: `packages/react/src/tabs/indicator/TabsIndicator.test.tsx`: "pre-hydration script execution > does not resurrect the indicator when the captured tab is no longer active") (browser-mode only)
- Given the same hidden server markup, when hydration takes ownership first (the indicator's `hidden` is removed and `--active-tab-width` is set to `55px`) and the host is then revealed, then after 100ms `--active-tab-width` is still `55px`, and resizing the tab list to 500px leaves it at `55px` — the script's `ResizeObserver` has disconnected. (base-ui: `packages/react/src/tabs/indicator/TabsIndicator.test.tsx`: "pre-hydration script execution > stops once hydration has revealed the indicator") (browser-mode only)
- Given server markup whose active tab has width but `height: 0` (styles/images still loading), when 100ms pass, then the indicator stays `hidden`, and once the tab's height becomes `40px` the script reveals it — the observer keeps waiting until the tab is fully measurable. (base-ui: `packages/react/src/tabs/indicator/TabsIndicator.test.tsx`: "pre-hydration script execution > keeps observing until the active tab is fully measurable") (browser-mode only)

- Given `<Collapsible.Trigger>` with `ref`, `data-testid`, `className`, inline `style` and `onClick` inside an open root, when rendered, then the unconsumed props land on the rendered element, the ref resolves to it, and clicking fires the author `onClick` composed with the trigger's own handler rather than replaced by it. (radix: `packages/react/collapsible/src/collapsible.test.tsx`: "Collapsible.Trigger > spreads props it does not consume onto the element it renders")
- Given `<Collapsible.Content>` with `ref`, `data-testid`, `className`, inline `style` and `onClick` inside an open root, when rendered, then the author inline `outlineColor: rgb(1, 2, 3)` survives alongside the content's own `--radix-collapsible-content-*` custom properties, the className applies, the ref resolves to the element, and clicking fires the author `onClick`. - Given `<Collapsible.Root />`, the shared `describeConformance` suite runs with `{ refInstanceof: window.HTMLDivElement }`, so the part is asserted to forward props, forward refs, support the `render` prop and merge classNames. - Given the same dialog, when the trigger is clicked open, then the content has a truthy `id`, the trigger's `aria-controls` equals that id, and `document.getElementById(id)` resolves to the content element. (radix: `packages/react/dialog/src/dialog.test.tsx`: "aria-controls > should reference the rendered content while open")
- Given `<Dialog.Root defaultOpen>` whose content renders `<Dialog.Title>Title</Dialog.Title>` and `<Dialog.Description>Description</Dialog.Description>`, when rendered, then the content's `aria-labelledby` and `aria-describedby` are both set and each id resolves to an element whose text content is "Title" and "Description" respectively. ### Dismissal and layering

- Given a default dialog opened by clicking its trigger with focus inside, when `Escape` is pressed on `document.activeElement`, then the content unmounts and the close button is removed from the document. (radix: `packages/react/dialog/src/dialog.test.tsx`: "given a default Dialog > after clicking the trigger > when pressing escape > should close the content")
- Given a modal dialog, when it is opened by trigger click and then closed via the `Close` button, then `document.body.style.pointerEvents` goes from `""` to `"none"` while open and back to `""` after closing. (radix: `packages/react/dialog/src/dialog.test.tsx`: "given a modal Dialog > should restore `body` pointer-events after closing")
- Given an open modal dialog rendered with `<Dialog.Content asChild>` wrapping an `<article>` and a controlled `onOpenChange`, when `Escape` is pressed on the active element, then `onOpenChange` is called with `false`, so slotting the content does not break dismissal. (radix: `packages/react/dialog/src/dialog.test.tsx`: "given a Dialog with `asChild` on the Content > still dismisses on escape when slotted")
- Given two modal `<Dialog.Root>`s both open with `<Dialog.Portal forceMount>` and `<Dialog.Content forceMount>` (mirroring exit animations), when both are closed in turn by their own buttons, then `document.body.style.pointerEvents` returns to `""` instead of leaking `"none"`. (radix: `packages/react/dialog/src/dialog.test.tsx`: "given two overlapping modal Dialogs (forceMount) > should restore `body` pointer-events after both close")
- Given a controlled open modal dialog containing a nested `<DismissableLayer disableOutsidePointerEvents>` opened as the top-most layer (with a 0ms `setTimeout` flush for the layer's document `pointerdown` listener), when an outside button receives the full `pointerdown`/`mousedown`/`pointerup`/`mouseup`/`click` sequence with `pointerType: 'mouse'`, then only the nested layer's `onDismiss` fires (once), the dialog's `onOpenChange` is never called, and the dialog content stays mounted. (radix: `packages/react/dialog/src/dialog.test.tsx`: "given a modal Dialog containing a nested modal layer (eg. a DropdownMenu) > does not call `onOpenChange(false)` on a controlled dialog when the nested layer is dismissed by an outside interaction")
- Given the `dialog--with-dropdown-menu` story with the dialog open and a nested modal DropdownMenu open (after a 150ms settle), when the dialog overlay is clicked at position 5,5 (inside the dialog, outside the dropdown), then the menu item unmounts and `[data-testid="dialog-state"]` still reads "open". (radix: `e2e/dialog.spec.ts`: "Dialog with a nested DropdownMenu > dismissing the dropdown does not close the dialog")
- Given the same story with dialog and nested dropdown both open, when `Escape` is pressed, then only the dropdown closes (menu item count 0) and `[data-testid="dialog-state"]` still reads "open". (radix: `e2e/dialog.spec.ts`: "Dialog with a nested DropdownMenu > pressing Escape closes only the dropdown")
- Given the `dialog--with-extension-overlay` story with the dialog open, when a button living inside a shadow root under `[data-testid="inside-shadow-host"]` is clicked, then `[data-testid="dialog-state"]` still reads "open", so shadow-DOM descendants count as inside the layer. (radix: `e2e/dialog.spec.ts`: "Dialog extension overlay interactions > keeps the dialog open when interacting with a shadow tree inside the dialog")
- Given the same story with the dialog open and an external overlay attached that swallows later mouse events, when `[data-testid="external-overlay-button"]` is clicked, then `[data-testid="dialog-state"]` still reads "open". (radix: `e2e/dialog.spec.ts`: "Dialog extension overlay interactions > keeps the dialog open when an outside overlay stops later mouse events")
- Given a `modal={false}` dialog in each of the three trigger arrangements, when the trigger opens it, `Escape` closes it, the trigger reopens it, and `click` fires on `document.body`, then the dialog closes again, so the dismiss interactions are rewired after the first close. (base-ui: `packages/react/src/dialog/root/DialogRoot.test.tsx`: "when using $name > rewires dismiss interactions after closing and reopening")
- Given `defaultOpen` with `modal: true`, then an element with role `presentation` (queried with `hidden: true`) is present, marking the rest of the page inert. ### SSR and hydration

- Given `<Dialog.Root handle defaultOpen defaultTriggerId="trigger" />` and a detached `<Dialog.Trigger handle id="trigger">` server-rendered with `renderToString`, then the trigger has `aria-expanded="false"` and no `data-popup-open` before hydration, and after `hydrate()` it becomes `aria-expanded="true"` with `data-popup-open`. (base-ui: `packages/react/src/dialog/root/DialogRoot.detached-triggers.test.tsx`: "handle-backed root ownership > hydrates a detached trigger from the stable fallback store")
- Given a server-rendered `<Dialog.Root handle defaultOpen defaultTriggerId="trigger" />` whose detached trigger is behind a `React.Suspense` boundary that throws a promise during hydration, when hydration starts (`handle.isOpen` becomes `true`), `handle.close()` runs while the trigger is still suspended, and the boundary then resolves, then the trigger reads `aria-expanded="false"` throughout and after hydration completes. (base-ui: `packages/react/src/dialog/root/DialogRoot.detached-triggers.test.tsx`: "handle-backed root ownership > keeps the server snapshot stable when the root closes before a delayed trigger hydrates")

## alert-dialog

### Roles and attributes

- Given `<AlertDialog.Trigger asChild>` wrapping a `<button type="button">` with `className`, `style` and `onClick` in a closed root, when rendered, then the element is a `BUTTON` with `aria-haspopup="dialog"` and `aria-expanded="false"`, the custom class and inline `outlineColor`, the ref resolves to it, and clicking fires `onClick`. (radix: `packages/react/alert-dialog/src/alert-dialog.test.tsx`: "AlertDialog.Trigger > forwards props to the child element when `asChild` is set")
- Given `<AlertDialog.Overlay asChild>` wrapping an `<article>` inside `<AlertDialog.Root defaultOpen>`'s portal, when rendered, then the element is an `ARTICLE` with `data-state="open"`, the author class, inline style and ref, and clicking fires `onClick`. (radix: `packages/react/alert-dialog/src/alert-dialog.test.tsx`: "AlertDialog.Overlay > forwards props to the child element when `asChild` is set")
- Given `<AlertDialog.Content asChild>` wrapping an `<article>` containing a `Title`, when rendered open, then the element is an `ARTICLE` with `role="alertdialog"` (not `dialog`), `data-state="open"` and `aria-labelledby` equal to the Title's id, plus the author class, inline style and ref, and clicking fires `onClick`. (radix: `packages/react/alert-dialog/src/alert-dialog.test.tsx`: "AlertDialog.Content > forwards props to the child element when `asChild` is set")
- Given `<AlertDialog.Root open>` with a trigger, backdrop, `AlertDialog.Title>title text` and `AlertDialog.Description>description text` in the popup, then an element with role `alertdialog` exists whose `aria-labelledby` is the title's `id` and whose `aria-describedby` is the description's `id`. (base-ui: `packages/react/src/alert-dialog/root/AlertDialogRoot.test.tsx`: "ARIA attributes")
- Given `<AlertDialog.Root open triggerId="trigger-2">` with triggers `trigger-1` and `trigger-2`, then `trigger-1` has `aria-expanded="false"` and no `aria-controls`, while `trigger-2` has `aria-expanded="true"` and `aria-controls` equal to the popup's `id`. (base-ui: `packages/react/src/alert-dialog/root/AlertDialogRoot.test.tsx`: "synchronizes trigger ARIA attributes in controlled mode")
- Given `<AlertDialog.Root handle defaultOpen defaultTriggerId="trigger">` containing `<AlertDialog.Trigger id="trigger">`, then on first render the trigger has `aria-expanded="true"` and `aria-controls` equal to the popup's `id`. (base-ui: `packages/react/src/alert-dialog/root/AlertDialogRoot.test.tsx`: "synchronizes trigger ARIA attributes when initially open with a handle")
- Given a detached `<AlertDialog.Trigger handle id="trigger">` declared before `<AlertDialog.Root handle defaultOpen defaultTriggerId="trigger">`, then on first render the trigger has `aria-expanded="true"`, `aria-controls` equal to the popup's `id`, and `handle.isOpen` is `true`. (base-ui: `packages/react/src/alert-dialog/root/AlertDialogRoot.test.tsx`: "synchronizes detached trigger ARIA attributes when initially open with a handle")
- Given `<AlertDialog.Root open>` with an `AlertDialog.Viewport` wrapping the popup inside the portal, then the viewport element contains the element with role `alertdialog`. (base-ui: `packages/react/src/alert-dialog/root/AlertDialogRoot.test.tsx`: "renders a viewport")
- Given an `AlertDialog.Root` with two contained triggers, then both start at `aria-expanded="false"`; when the first is clicked, then it gets a non-null `aria-controls` equal to the `alertdialog` element's `id` and `aria-expanded="true"`, while the second stays `aria-expanded="false"`. (base-ui: `packages/react/src/alert-dialog/root/AlertDialogRoot.test.tsx`: "multiple triggers within Root > synchronizes ARIA attributes on the active trigger") (browser-mode only)

## drawer

### Roles and attributes

- Given `<Drawer.Provider>` wrapping `<Drawer.IndentBackground data-testid="bg" />` and `<Drawer.Indent data-testid="indent">` containing a `<Drawer.Root open={false}>` with a `<Drawer.Trigger>`, when `open` flips to `true`, then the indent element switches from `data-inactive=""` (no `data-active`) to `data-active=""` (no `data-inactive`), and the sibling `Drawer.IndentBackground` also gains `data-active=""`. (base-ui: `packages/react/src/drawer/indent/DrawerIndent.test.tsx`: "sets data-active when any drawer is open")
- Given `<Drawer.Provider>` wrapping `<Drawer.IndentBackground data-testid="bg" />` and a sibling `<Drawer.Root open={false}>`, when `open` flips to `true`, then the background's `data-inactive` attribute (initially `""`) becomes `null` and `data-active` becomes `""`. (base-ui: `packages/react/src/drawer/indent-background/DrawerIndentBackground.test.tsx`: "sets data-active when any drawer is open")
- Given `<Drawer.Content data-testid="content">` rendered inside `<Drawer.Root open>` / `Portal` / `Viewport` / `Popup`, when it mounts, then it carries neither `data-swipe-ignore` nor `data-base-ui-swipe-ignore` (those swipe-ignore markers stay private). (base-ui: `packages/react/src/drawer/content/DrawerContent.test.tsx`: "does not add public swipe-ignore attributes")
- Given `<Drawer.Provider>` with a `Drawer.Indent` and a control that calls `context.visualStateStore.set(...)`, when the store is set to `{ swipeProgress: 0.5, frontmostHeight: 120 }`, then the indent's inline style sets `--drawer-swipe-progress: 0.5` and `--drawer-height: 120px`; setting `swipeProgress: 0` leaves `--drawer-swipe-progress` as `'0'` while `--drawer-height` stays `120px`; setting `frontmostHeight: 0` clears `--drawer-height` to `''`; setting `{ swipeProgress: NaN, frontmostHeight: Infinity }` yields `--drawer-swipe-progress: '0'` and `--drawer-height: ''`; and unmounting the indent (`showIndent: false`) after a non-zero set resets both custom properties to `'0'` and `''`. (base-ui: `packages/react/src/drawer/provider/DrawerProvider.test.tsx`: "synchronizes and restores visual state on Drawer.Indent")
- Given `<Drawer.Indent>` and `<Drawer.IndentBackground>` rendered with no `Drawer.Provider` ancestor, when they mount, then both render and carry `data-inactive=""`. (base-ui: `packages/react/src/drawer/provider/DrawerProvider.test.tsx`: "allows indent parts to render without a provider")
- Given `<Drawer.Root defaultSnapPoint="100px" open modal={false} snapPoints={['100px','300px']} swipeDirection="up">` with a viewport of `offsetHeight` 400 and a popup of `offsetHeight` 300, when it settles, then the popup's inline `--drawer-snap-point-offset` is `-200px` (negative for upward drawers) and the popup has `data-swipe-direction="up"`. (base-ui: `packages/react/src/drawer/popup/DrawerPopup.test.tsx`: "applies a negative snap point offset to upward drawers")
- Given a `Drawer.Root` popup containing a nested `Drawer.Root` popup styled `height: 100px` with `border-top: 2px solid` and `border-bottom: 2px solid` around a 10px child, when the nested drawer is open, then the nested popup's `offsetHeight` exceeds its `scrollHeight` and the parent popup's `--drawer-frontmost-height` equals the nested popup's full `offsetHeight` including borders. (base-ui: `packages/react/src/drawer/popup/DrawerPopup.test.tsx`: "includes border size in frontmost height CSS variable for nested drawers") (browser-mode only)
- Given a parent `Drawer.Popup` containing a nested `Drawer.Root` whose popup has `offsetHeight` 100, rendered under `React.StrictMode` with the child's `Drawer.Portal keepMounted`, when the child opens, then `notifyParentFrontmostHeight` and `notifyParentHasNestedDrawer` both fire before React passive effects flush, and the parent popup ends with `--nested-drawers: 1`, `data-nested-drawer-open=""` and `--drawer-frontmost-height: 100px`. (base-ui: `packages/react/src/drawer/popup/DrawerPopup.test.tsx`: "reports nested presence and frontmost height before passive effects")
- Given a parent drawer popup containing a nested drawer popup which itself contains a non-modal `Dialog.Root`, when the inner dialog is opened, then the parent popup's `--nested-drawers` stays `'1'` (a MutationObserver on `style` never records `'2'`), and the child popup keeps `--nested-drawers: 0` with no `data-nested-drawer-open`. (base-ui: `packages/react/src/drawer/popup/DrawerPopup.test.tsx`: "does not treat dialogs inside nested drawers as nested drawers")
- Given a parent drawer popup containing a nested drawer popup which itself contains an `AlertDialog.Root`, when the alert dialog is opened, then the parent popup's `--nested-drawers` stays `'1'` (never observed as `'2'`) and the child popup keeps `--nested-drawers: 0` with no `data-nested-drawer-open`. - Given `<Drawer.Root>` with `<Drawer.Trigger>Open</Drawer.Trigger>` and a portalled `<Drawer.Viewport><Drawer.Popup data-testid="popup">`, when the trigger is clicked and the `role="dialog"` popup appears, then the trigger's `aria-controls` equals the popup element's `id`. - Given `<Drawer.Root><Drawer.SwipeArea data-testid="swipe-area" /></Drawer.Root>`, when an upward pointer swipe from `clientY` 120 to 40 is in flight (checked in `beforeRelease`) then the swipe area has `data-swiping=""`, and after the release the attribute is gone. - Given `<Drawer.Root open modal={false}>` wrapped in `<Drawer.VirtualKeyboardProvider>` with a `<Drawer.Content>` scroller (`height: 420`, `overflowY: 'auto'`, `overflowAnchor: 'auto'`, `paddingBottom: 20`, `clientHeight` 420, `scrollHeight` 1200, rect top 300/bottom 720) holding an input at y 650, `window.innerHeight` 800 and `visualViewport.height` 800, when the input is focused and the visual viewport resizes to 500, then the scroller's `paddingBottom` grows above 20px, `scrollPaddingBottom` becomes non-empty, `overflowAnchor` becomes `none`, and the input's vertical center lands on the center of the band between the scroller top (300) and the 500px keyboard viewport; and when the input blurs, `paddingBottom` returns to `20px`, `scrollPaddingBottom` to empty and `overflowAnchor` to `auto`. (base-ui: `packages/react/src/drawer/popup/DrawerPopup.test.tsx`: "stops composite navigation keys from escaping the popup")

### Pointer

- Given animations enabled (`BASE_UI_ANIMATIONS_DISABLED = false`) and a nested drawer popup with a 100ms `animation` bound to `[data-ending-style]`, when the nested `Drawer.Close` is clicked, then while the child popup still has `data-ending-style` the parent popup already reports `--nested-drawers: 0` and has lost `data-nested-drawer-open`, and the child later unmounts. (base-ui: `packages/react/src/drawer/popup/DrawerPopup.test.tsx`: "clears parent nested drawer state when a nested drawer starts closing before unmount") (browser-mode only)
- Given animations enabled, a parent popup styled `height: var(--drawer-height, auto)` with `height: var(--drawer-frontmost-height, var(--drawer-height))` under `[data-nested-drawer-open]` and a `height 100ms linear` transition, and a nested drawer with a 100ms exit animation, when the nested drawer is opened then closed, then a MutationObserver on `data-nested-drawer-open`/`style` records at least one state where `data-nested-drawer-open` is absent while `--drawer-height` is still non-empty, so the parent keeps a fixed height through the nested exit animation before the child unmounts. (base-ui: `packages/react/src/drawer/popup/DrawerPopup.test.tsx`: "keeps a fixed height applied while a nested drawer closes") (browser-mode only)

(base-ui: `packages/react/src/drawer/popup/DrawerPopup.test.tsx`: "restores a fixed height before nested state when reopening a nested drawer") (browser-mode only)

### Notes and edge cases

- Given `<Drawer.Content />`, the shared `describeConformance` suite runs with `{ refInstanceof: window.HTMLDivElement }` and a custom `render` that wraps the node in `<Drawer.Root open><Drawer.Portal><Drawer.Viewport><Drawer.Popup>`, so the part is asserted to forward props, forward refs, support the `render` prop and merge classNames. (base-ui: `packages/react/src/drawer/content/DrawerContent.test.tsx`: "describeConformance")
- Given a `React.Profiler` wrapping `Drawer.Provider`, when `setDrawerOpen(manualDrawer, false)` is called for a drawer that was never registered open, then no re-render is recorded (closed drawers are not retained in the registry). (base-ui: `packages/react/src/drawer/provider/DrawerProvider.test.tsx`: "does not retain closed drawer registrations")
- Given the pure helper `getSnapPointSwipeMovement(currentOffset, movement)`, when the drag does not overshoot the open edge, then the raw movement is returned: `getSnapPointSwipeMovement(100, -50) === -50` and `getSnapPointSwipeMovement(0, 20) === 20`. (base-ui: `packages/react/src/drawer/root/useDrawerSnapPoints.test.ts`: "getSnapPointSwipeMovement > returns the raw movement when the drag does not overshoot the open edge")
- Given `getSnapPointSwipeMovement`, when the drag lands exactly on the open edge (`nextOffset === 0`), then the raw movement is returned: `getSnapPointSwipeMovement(100, -100) === -100`. (base-ui: `packages/react/src/drawer/root/useDrawerSnapPoints.test.ts`: "getSnapPointSwipeMovement > returns the raw movement at the open edge (nextOffset === 0)")
- Given `getSnapPointSwipeMovement`, when the drag overshoots past the open edge, then the overshoot is damped by a square root: `getSnapPointSwipeMovement(0, -150) ≈ -Math.sqrt(150)` and `getSnapPointSwipeMovement(100, -250) ≈ -Math.sqrt(150) - 100`. (base-ui: `packages/react/src/drawer/root/useDrawerSnapPoints.test.ts`: "getSnapPointSwipeMovement > damps the movement with a square root once the drag overshoots the open edge")
- Given the pure helper `closestSnapPointIndex(values, target)`, when called, then it returns the index of the nearest value and keeps the first on a tie: `closestSnapPointIndex([100,200,300], 240) === 1` and `closestSnapPointIndex([100,200], 150) === 0`. (base-ui: `packages/react/src/drawer/root/useDrawerSnapPoints.test.ts`: "closestSnapPointIndex > returns the closest value and keeps the first value on ties")
- Given `closestSnapPointIndex([], 100)`, when called with an empty list, then it returns `-1`. (base-ui: `packages/react/src/drawer/root/useDrawerSnapPoints.test.ts`: "closestSnapPointIndex > returns -1 when there are no values")
- Given `<Drawer.Popup />`, the shared `describeConformance` suite runs with `{ refInstanceof: window.HTMLDivElement }` and a custom `render` wrapping the node in `<Drawer.Root open><Drawer.Portal><Drawer.Viewport>`, so the part is asserted to forward props, forward refs, support the `render` prop and merge classNames. (base-ui: `packages/react/src/drawer/popup/DrawerPopup.test.tsx`: "describeConformance")
- Given `<Drawer.Popup>` rendered inside `Drawer.Portal` with no `Drawer.Viewport` ancestor, when it mounts in development, then `console.error` receives a message containing `'Base UI: <Drawer.Popup> expected to be rendered within <Drawer.Viewport>.'`. (base-ui: `packages/react/src/drawer/popup/DrawerPopup.test.tsx`: "warns in development when not rendered within a viewport")
- Given `SafeReact.captureOwnerStack` stubbed to return `null`, when a `Drawer.Popup` renders without a `Drawer.Viewport`, then `console.error` is called with exactly `'Base UI: <Drawer.Popup> expected to be rendered within <Drawer.Viewport>. Omitting the viewport disables drawer swipe handling and touch scroll locking. Wrap <Drawer.Popup> in <Drawer.Viewport>.'`. (base-ui: `packages/react/src/drawer/popup/DrawerPopup.test.tsx`: "warns without relying on React owner-stack support")
- Given a stubbed `ResizeObserver` and a popup whose `offsetHeight` starts at 100, when `onNestedFrontmostHeightChange(200)` is called from context, the popup height grows to 150 and the resize callback fires, then the context's `popupHeight` stays `100` (the last measurement taken before nested content stretched it). (base-ui: `packages/react/src/drawer/popup/DrawerPopup.test.tsx`: "keeps the last measured popup height while nested content stretches it")
- Given `<Drawer.Popup render={() => null}>` inside an open non-modal root, when rendered, then the render resolves without throwing. (base-ui: `packages/react/src/drawer/popup/DrawerPopup.test.tsx`: "does not throw when a popup render function produces no element")
- Given a stubbed `ResizeObserver` capturing callbacks and a popup that is conditionally rendered, when the popup is unmounted and the captured resize callbacks are then invoked, then no error is thrown (queued measurements after unmount are ignored). (base-ui: `packages/react/src/drawer/popup/DrawerPopup.test.tsx`: "ignores a queued measurement after the popup unmounts")
- Given a component that calls `useDrawerRootContext()` outside any `<Drawer.Root>`, when it renders, then rendering rejects with the error "Base UI: DrawerRootContext is missing. Drawer parts must be placed within <Drawer.Root>." (base-ui: `packages/react/src/drawer/root/DrawerRoot.test.tsx`: "throws a descriptive error when the root context is missing")
- Given `<Drawer.Provider>` wrapping a `<Drawer.Root modal={false}>` plus `<Drawer.IndentBackground data-testid="background">`, for the three cases "a controlled drawer" (`open`), "a default-open drawer in Strict Mode" (`defaultOpen` + `StrictMode`) and "the React 17 id fallback" (`defaultOpen` + `StrictMode` + `useId` mocked to return `undefined`), when the root mounts then `setDrawerOpen` on the provider context is called before any passive `useEffect` has flushed and the background has `data-active=""`; when the root unmounts then `removeDrawer` is called before the passive effect teardown has flushed and the background has `data-inactive=""`. (base-ui: `packages/react/src/drawer/root/DrawerRoot.test.tsx`: "reports and unregisters $label before passive effects")
- Given a `directions: ['down']` swipe box that captures `getDragStyles` from any render where `swipe.swiping` is still `false`, when a gesture reaches `clientY` 40 so the transform is written imperatively and `style.transition` is `none`, then calling the captured lagging `getDragStyles()` still returns `transition: 'none'` and a `transform` matching `translate3d(0px, 40px, 0)`, so a render committing mid-gesture cannot reconcile the drag transform away. (base-ui: `packages/react/src/utils/useSwipeDismiss.test.tsx`: "keeps the drag transform on a render that lags behind the swiping state")
- Given `<Drawer.SwipeArea />` rendered inside `<Drawer.Root>`, the shared `describeConformance` suite runs with `{ refInstanceof: window.HTMLDivElement }` and a custom `render` that wraps the node in `<Drawer.Root>`, so the part is asserted to forward props, forward refs, support the `render` prop and merge classNames. (base-ui: `packages/react/src/drawer/swipe-area/DrawerSwipeArea.test.tsx`: "describeConformance")
- Given `<Drawer.Viewport />` rendered inside `<Drawer.Root open><Drawer.Portal>`, the shared `describeConformance` suite runs with `{ refInstanceof: window.HTMLDivElement }` and a custom `render` that wraps the node in an open root and portal, so the part is asserted to forward props, forward refs, support the `render` prop and merge classNames. (base-ui: `packages/react/src/drawer/viewport/DrawerViewport.test.tsx`: "describeConformance")
- Given an open drawer whose backdrop has gained `data-swiping=""` from a `touchstart` on an inner button, when the whole tree is unmounted mid-swipe, then the detached backdrop node no longer carries `data-swiping`, i.e. teardown removes it. (base-ui: `packages/react/src/drawer/viewport/DrawerViewport.test.tsx`: "clears the backdrop data-swiping attribute when the drawer unmounts mid-swipe")
- Given `<Drawer.Root open snapPoints={['100px', '200px']} swipeDirection="down">` whose popup is removed via props mid-drag, when a drag to `clientY` 20 has set `data-swiping=""` on the backdrop, the popup then unmounts, a further `pointermove` to `clientY` 30 keeps `data-swiping=""`, and `pointerup` follows, then the backdrop ends without `data-swiping` and `onOpenChange` is never called. (base-ui: `packages/react/src/drawer/viewport/DrawerViewport.test.tsx`: "cleans up when the popup unmounts during an active swipe")
- Given `<Drawer.Root open modal={false} snapPoints={['100px', '200px']} snapPoint="100px">` with viewport and popup `offsetHeight` 200 and a probe tracking layout vs passive effect phases, when the `snapPoint` prop changes to `'200px'`, then the backdrop's `--drawer-swipe-progress` is set to `'0'` before the descendant passive effect has flushed, and it ends at `'0'`. (base-ui: `packages/react/src/drawer/viewport/DrawerViewport.test.tsx`: "publishes resting snap progress before descendant layout effects")
- Given a closed `<Drawer.Root modal={false}>` with `<Drawer.Portal keepMounted>` whose popup has been manually given `--drawer-swipe-movement-y: 50px` and `data-swipe-dismiss`, when `open` flips to `true`, then `popup.toggleAttribute('data-swipe-dismiss', false)` runs before the descendant passive effect flushes, `--drawer-swipe-movement-y` ends at `0px` and `data-swipe-dismiss` is gone. (base-ui: `packages/react/src/drawer/viewport/DrawerViewport.test.tsx`: "clears kept-mounted swipe state before descendant layout effects on reopen")
- Given a parent drawer whose popup holds a nested `keepMounted` child drawer, where `onNestedSwipeProgressChange(0.5)` has set the parent popup's `--drawer-swipe-progress` to `'0.5'`, when the child's `open` prop flips to `false`, then the parent popup's `--drawer-swipe-progress` is set to `'0'` before the child's passive effect teardown has flushed, and ends at `'0'`. (base-ui: `packages/react/src/drawer/viewport/DrawerViewport.test.tsx`: "clears nested progress before descendant layout effects when the child closes")
- Given `<Drawer.Provider>` with `<Drawer.Indent>` and an open non-modal drawer, where `visualStateStore.set({ swipeProgress: 0.5, frontmostHeight: 100 })` has put `--drawer-swipe-progress: 0.5` and `--drawer-height: 100px` on the indent and the backdrop has been given `data-swiping`, when the `<Drawer.Viewport>` subtree unmounts, then the indent's `--drawer-swipe-progress` is set to `'0'` before the passive effect teardown flushes, `--drawer-height` ends empty and the backdrop loses `data-swiping`. (base-ui: `packages/react/src/drawer/viewport/DrawerViewport.test.tsx`: "clears provider and backdrop swipe state during layout teardown")

## popover

### Roles and attributes

- Given `<Popover.Root>` with `Trigger` and a portalled `Content` while closed, when rendered, then the content is not in the document, the trigger has `aria-expanded="false"` and the trigger has no `aria-controls` attribute at all. (radix: `packages/react/popover/src/popover.test.tsx`: "aria-controls > should not reference a non-existent element while closed")
- Given the same popover, when the trigger is clicked, then the content has a truthy `id`, the trigger flips to `aria-expanded="true"`, `aria-controls` equals the content's id, and `document.getElementById(id)` resolves to the content. (radix: `packages/react/popover/src/popover.test.tsx`: "aria-controls > should reference the rendered content while open")
- Given an open `<Popover.Content>` with no `Title` and no `Description`, when the trigger is clicked and the `dialog` role element is inspected, then it has neither `aria-labelledby` nor `aria-describedby`. (radix: `packages/react/popover/src/popover.test.tsx`: "Title and Description > should not reference a title or description when none are rendered")
- Given `<Popover.Content>` containing `<Popover.Title>Title</Popover.Title>`, when opened, then the title has a truthy `id`, the content's `aria-labelledby` equals it, and `aria-describedby` is absent. (radix: `packages/react/popover/src/popover.test.tsx`: "Title and Description > should label the content via aria-labelledby when a Title is rendered")
- Given `<Popover.Content>` containing `<Popover.Description>Description</Popover.Description>`, when opened, then the description has a truthy `id`, the content's `aria-describedby` equals it, and `aria-labelledby` is absent. (radix: `packages/react/popover/src/popover.test.tsx`: "Title and Description > should describe the content via aria-describedby when a Description is rendered")
- Given `<Popover.Content>` containing both a `Title` and a `Description`, when opened, then `aria-labelledby` equals the title's id and `aria-describedby` equals the description's id. (radix: `packages/react/popover/src/popover.test.tsx`: "Title and Description > should reference both Title and Description when rendered together")
- Given `<Popover.Content asChild className="content" onClick ref>` wrapping an `<article>` in a portal, for both `modal: true` and `modal: false`, when rendered with `defaultOpen`, then the element is an `ARTICLE` with `role="dialog"` and `data-state="open"`, the `content` class, the ref pointing at it, and clicking fires `onClick` once. (radix: `packages/react/popover/src/popover.test.tsx`: "given a Popover with `asChild` on the Content > forwards content props and the ref to the child (modal: $modal)")
- Given `<Popover.Trigger asChild>` wrapping a `<button type="button">` (the trigger is additionally wrapped in a slotted `Popper.Anchor`, so props must survive two nested `Slot`s), when rendered closed, then the element is a `BUTTON` with `aria-haspopup="dialog"`, `aria-expanded="false"` and `data-state="closed"`, plus the author class, inline style and ref, and clicking fires `onClick`. (radix: `packages/react/popover/src/popover.test.tsx`: "Popover.Trigger > forwards props to the child element when `asChild` is set")
- Given `<Popover.Content asChild>` wrapping an `<article>` containing a `Title` in a non-modal open popover, when rendered, then the element is an `ARTICLE` with `role="dialog"`, `data-state="open"` and `aria-labelledby` equal to the Title's id, plus the author class, inline style and ref, and clicking fires `onClick`. (radix: `packages/react/popover/src/popover.test.tsx`: "Popover.Content > forwards props to the child element when `asChild` is set")
- Given `<Popover.Root defaultOpen modal>` with `<Popover.Content asChild>` wrapping an `<article>` containing a `Title`, when rendered, then the element is an `ARTICLE` with `role="dialog"`, `data-state="open"` and `aria-labelledby` equal to the Title's id, plus the author class, inline style and ref, and clicking fires `onClick`. (radix: `packages/react/popover/src/popover.test.tsx`: "Popover.Content > forwards props to the child element when `asChild` is set on a modal popover")
- Given the shared Popover tree (`Popover.Root` > `Popover.Trigger` "Toggle" + `Popover.Portal` > `Popover.Positioner data-testid="positioner"` > `Popover.Popup data-testid="popover-popup"` "Content"), run for contained / detached (`Popover.createHandle()` + `handle`) / multiple detached triggers, when it renders closed, then the trigger's children text "Toggle" is in the document. (base-ui: `packages/react/src/popover/root/PopoverRoot.test.tsx`: "when using $name > should render the children")
- Given `<Popover.Root open triggerId="trigger-2">` with two `Popover.Trigger`s `id="trigger-1"`/`id="trigger-2"`, when it renders open, then `trigger-1` has `aria-expanded="false"` and no `aria-controls`, while `trigger-2` has `aria-expanded="true"` and an `aria-controls` equal to the `role="dialog"` popup's `id`. (base-ui: `packages/react/src/popover/root/PopoverRoot.detached-triggers.test.tsx`: "multiple triggers within Root > synchronizes ARIA attributes in controlled mode") (browser-mode only)
- Given `<Popover.Root open>` with a single `Popover.Trigger` and no `triggerId`, when it renders open, then the trigger's `aria-controls` equals the `role="dialog"` popup's `id`. (base-ui: `packages/react/src/popover/root/PopoverRoot.detached-triggers.test.tsx`: "multiple triggers within Root > synchronizes ARIA attributes for a controlled open single trigger without triggerId") (browser-mode only)
- Given `<Popover.Root open>` with `Popover.Trigger`, `Popover.Portal`, `Popover.Positioner` and `<Popover.Popup>Content</Popover.Popup>`, when it renders, then the text "Content" is in the document. (base-ui: `packages/react/src/popover/popup/PopoverPopup.test.tsx`: "should render the children")
- Given `<Popover.Trigger disabled />` inside a closed `Popover.Root`, then the trigger has both the native `disabled` attribute and `data-disabled`, and when it is clicked "Content" never appears and `[Tab]` does not move focus onto it. (base-ui: `packages/react/src/popover/trigger/PopoverTrigger.test.tsx`: "prop: disabled > disables the popover")
- Given `<Popover.Trigger disabled render={<span />} nativeButton={false} />`, then the trigger has no native `disabled` attribute but does have `data-disabled` and `aria-disabled="true"`, and when it is clicked "Content" never appears and `[Tab]` does not focus it. (base-ui: `packages/react/src/popover/trigger/PopoverTrigger.test.tsx`: "prop: disabled > custom element")
- Given `<Popover.Root>` with a bare `<Popover.Trigger />`, when the trigger is clicked, then it has both `data-popup-open` and `data-pressed`. (base-ui: `packages/react/src/popover/trigger/PopoverTrigger.test.tsx`: "style hooks > should have the data-popup-open and data-pressed attributes when open by clicking")
- Given `<Popover.Trigger openOnHover delay={0} />`, when the trigger is hovered, then it has `data-popup-open` but not `data-pressed`. (base-ui: `packages/react/src/popover/trigger/PopoverTrigger.test.tsx`: "style hooks > should have the data-popup-open but not the data-pressed attribute when open by hover")
- Given `<Popover.Trigger delay={0} openOnHover />`, when the trigger is hovered and then clicked, then it still has `data-popup-open`. (base-ui: `packages/react/src/popover/trigger/PopoverTrigger.test.tsx`: "style hooks > should not have the data-popup-open and data-pressed attributes when open by click when `openOnHover=true` and `delay=0`")
- Given `<Popover.Trigger openOnHover />` (default delay), when the trigger is hovered and then clicked, then it has both `data-popup-open` and `data-pressed`. (base-ui: `packages/react/src/popover/trigger/PopoverTrigger.test.tsx`: "style hooks > should have the data-popup-open and data-pressed attributes when open by click when `openOnHover=true`")
- Given an open popover whose popup wraps `<div data-testid="content">Content</div>` in `Popover.Viewport`, when it renders, then the content's closest `[data-current]` ancestor exists and its `textContent` is exactly "Content". (base-ui: `packages/react/src/popover/viewport/PopoverViewport.test.tsx`: "should render children in the `current` container by default")
- Given two absolutely positioned `Popover.Trigger`s with payloads `0`/`1`, a `Popover.Viewport data-testid="viewport"` and CSS animations on `[data-transitioning] [data-previous]`/`[data-current]`, when trigger 1 opens the popup and trigger 2 is clicked, then the viewport gains `data-activation-direction` whose space-separated tokens match the geometric move: `right down` (10,10 → 200,100), `left up` (200,100 → 10,10), `right` only (horizontal move with a 2px vertical delta), `down` only (vertical move with a 2px horizontal delta), empty (both deltas within the 5px tolerance), `left down` (200,10 → 10,100), and `right up` (10,100 → 200,10). (base-ui: `packages/react/src/popover/viewport/PopoverViewport.test.tsx`: "morphing containers with multiple triggers and payloads > $name") (browser-mode only)
- Given `<Popover.Root>` (closed) containing only `<Popover.Close aria-label="Close popover" />`, when it renders, then a `role="button"` named "Close popover" is in the document — the close part renders even while the popover is closed. (base-ui: `packages/react/src/popover/close/PopoverClose.test.tsx`: "renders when popover is closed")
- Given `<Popover.Root open>` whose popup contains `<Popover.Title>Title</Popover.Title>`, when it renders, then the `role="dialog"` popup has `aria-labelledby` equal to the rendered `<h2>`'s `id`. (base-ui: `packages/react/src/popover/title/PopoverTitle.test.tsx`: "labels the popup element with its id")
- Given `<Popover.Root open>` whose popup contains `<Popover.Description>Title</Popover.Description>`, when it renders, then the `role="dialog"` popup has `aria-describedby` equal to the rendered `<p>`'s `id`. (base-ui: `packages/react/src/popover/description/PopoverDescription.test.tsx`: "describes the popup element with its id")

### Keyboard

- Given a `Toolbar.Root` containing `First`, a `Toolbar.Button render={<Popover.Trigger />}` "Open", and `Last`, with an "Inside" button in the portaled popup, when `[Tab]` focuses `First`, `[ArrowRight]` moves the roving highlight to the trigger, `[Enter]` opens the popup (focus on "Inside"), and `[ArrowRight]` is pressed, then focus stays on "Inside" and `Last` is not focused — composite keys from the popup are not relayed to the toolbar. (base-ui: `packages/react/src/popover/popup/PopoverPopup.test.tsx`: "inside a toolbar > does not relay composite keys from the popup to the toolbar")
- Given the same toolbar-hosted popover whose popup contains `<input defaultValue="ab" />`, when the trigger is clicked, the focused input's caret is set to 0 and `[ArrowRight]` is pressed, then `input.selectionStart` is `1` and the `Last` toolbar button is not focused — only propagation is stopped, not the key itself. (base-ui: `packages/react/src/popover/popup/PopoverPopup.test.tsx`: "inside a toolbar > keeps composite keys working inside the popup content")
- Given `<Popover.Trigger render={<div />} nativeButton={false} data-testid="div-trigger">` plus an unrelated button, rendered through `vitest-browser-react`, when the trigger is focused and `[Enter]` is pressed "Content" appears; Shift+Tab returns focus to the trigger and `[Enter]` closes it, `[Enter]` reopens it; likewise `[Space]` closes and reopens it and a final `[Space]` closes it — a non-native-button trigger toggles on both Enter and Space. (base-ui: `packages/react/src/popover/trigger/PopoverTrigger.test.tsx`: "should toggle closed with Enter or Space when rendering a <div>") (browser-mode only)

### Pointer

- Given the shared Popover tree with controlled `open`/`onOpenChange` and `Popover.Trigger openOnHover delay={0}`, when an external "Show" button opens the popover and then `mouseEnter`/`mouseLeave` fire on the positioner, then the `role="dialog"` popup stays mounted (hover-out only closes hover-opened popups). (base-ui: `packages/react/src/popover/root/PopoverRoot.test.tsx`: "when using $name > controlled open > does not close after hovering out of a popup opened externally")
- Given the shared Popover tree with controlled `open`/`onOpenChange` and `Popover.Trigger openOnHover delay={0}`, when `mouseEnter`+`mouseMove` on the trigger open it and then `mouseEnter`/`mouseLeave` fire on the positioner, then the `role="dialog"` popup unmounts. (base-ui: `packages/react/src/popover/root/PopoverRoot.test.tsx`: "when using $name > controlled open > closes after hovering out of a popup opened by its trigger")
- Given the shared Popover tree with `modal: false` and `Popover.Trigger openOnHover delay={0} closeDelay={0}`, when the popup is hover-opened, the pointer crosses from trigger to positioner (registering a `document` `'mousemove'` safe-polygon listener), the trigger is then clicked to make the open click-sticky, and `mouseLeave` fires on the positioner, then the popup stays open and `document.removeEventListener` was called with `'mousemove'` and that same handler. (base-ui: `packages/react/src/popover/root/PopoverRoot.test.tsx`: "when using $name > controlled open > cleans up the safe polygon handler after a hover-opened popup becomes click-sticky")
- Given the shared Popover tree with `defaultOpen: true` and `Popover.Trigger openOnHover`, when `mouseEnter`/`mouseLeave` fire on the positioner, then "Content" stays in the document because the open was not caused by trigger hover. (base-ui: `packages/react/src/popover/root/PopoverRoot.test.tsx`: "when using $name > prop: defaultOpen > does not close after hovering out of a popup opened without trigger hover")
- Given the shared Popover tree with `Popover.Trigger openOnHover delay={100}` and fake timers, when `mouseEnter`+`mouseMove` fire on the trigger, then "Content" is absent until `clock.tick(100)` elapses (the `delay` is a rest delay), after which it is present. (base-ui: `packages/react/src/popover/root/PopoverRoot.test.tsx`: "when using $name > prop: delay > should open after delay with rest type by default")

### Animation and presence

- Given the shared Popover tree with `Popover.Portal keepMounted`, `Popover.Trigger openOnHover delay={1}` and a popup class animating `opacity` over 50ms only while `[data-ending-style]` is set, when the trigger is hovered to set `data-open`, unhovered until the popup has `data-ending-style`, and re-entered with only `pointerEnter` (`pointerType: 'mouse'`) + `mouseEnter` and no follow-up `mousemove`, then the popup regains `data-open` and has no `data-closed` — the close-transition fast path reopens from `onMouseEnter`. (base-ui: `packages/react/src/popover/root/PopoverRoot.test.tsx`: "when using $name > hover close transitions > reopens immediately when re-hovering the trigger during a hover close transition") (browser-mode only)
- Given the shared Popover tree open with controlled `open` and `onOpenChangeComplete`, no exit animation defined, when an external "Close" button closes it, then `popover-popup` unmounts, the first `onOpenChangeComplete` call received `true` and the last received `false`. (base-ui: `packages/react/src/popover/root/PopoverRoot.test.tsx`: "when using $name > prop: onOpenChangeComplete > is called on close when there is no exit animation defined") (browser-mode only)

(base-ui: `packages/react/src/popover/root/PopoverRoot.test.tsx`: "when using $name > prop: onOpenChangeComplete > is called on close when the exit animation finishes") (browser-mode only)
- Given the shared Popover tree closed with controlled `open` and `onOpenChangeComplete` and no enter animation, when an external "Open" button opens it, then `popover-popup` mounts, `onOpenChangeComplete` has been called twice and its first argument was `true`. (base-ui: `packages/react/src/popover/root/PopoverRoot.test.tsx`: "when using $name > prop: onOpenChangeComplete > is called on open when there is no enter animation defined") (browser-mode only)
- Given the shared Popover tree closed with `onOpenChangeComplete` and a popup whose `[data-starting-style]` runs a 1ms `test-anim` keyframe animation (with `BASE_UI_ANIMATIONS_DISABLED = false`), when the "Open" button opens it, then `onOpenChangeComplete` is first called with `true` after the enter animation finishes and `popover-popup` is present. (base-ui: `packages/react/src/popover/root/PopoverRoot.test.tsx`: "when using $name > prop: onOpenChangeComplete > is called on open when the enter animation finishes") (browser-mode only)

(base-ui: `packages/react/src/popover/root/PopoverRoot.test.tsx`: "when using $name > prop: onOpenChangeComplete > does not get called on mount when not open") (browser-mode only)

### Notes and edge cases

- Given `<Popover.Anchor>` with `ref`, `data-testid`, `className="custom-class"`, `style={{ outlineColor: 'rgb(1, 2, 3)' }}` and `onClick`, when rendered, then the props land on the anchor element, the ref resolves to it, and clicking fires `onClick`. (radix: `packages/react/popover/src/popover.test.tsx`: "Popover.Anchor > spreads props it does not consume onto the element it renders")

## hover-card

### Roles and attributes

- Given `<HoverCard.Trigger asChild>` wrapping an `<article>Trigger</article>` in a closed root, when rendered, then the element is an `ARTICLE` with `data-state="closed"`, the author class, inline style and ref, and clicking fires `onClick`. (radix: `packages/react/hover-card/src/hover-card.test.tsx`: "HoverCard.Trigger > forwards props to the child element when `asChild` is set")
- Given `<HoverCard.Root open>` with `<HoverCard.Content asChild>` wrapping an `<article>` in a portal, when rendered, then the element is an `ARTICLE` with `data-state="open"` and `data-side="bottom"`, plus the author class, inline style and ref, and clicking fires `onClick`. (radix: `packages/react/hover-card/src/hover-card.test.tsx`: "HoverCard.Content > forwards props to the child element when `asChild` is set")
- Given `<PreviewCard.Backdrop data-testid="backdrop">` inside the portal of a `<PreviewCard.Trigger delay={0} closeDelay={0}>` card, when the trigger is hovered open, then the backdrop's inline `style.pointerEvents` is `"none"`. (base-ui: `packages/react/src/preview-card/backdrop/PreviewCardBackdrop.test.tsx`: "sets `pointer-events: none` style")
- Given `<PreviewCard.Viewport>` wrapping `<div data-testid="content">Content</div>` inside an open card's popup, then the content's nearest `[data-current]` ancestor exists and its `textContent` is "Content". (base-ui: `packages/react/src/preview-card/viewport/PreviewCardViewport.test.tsx`: "should render children in the `current` container by default")

### Pointer

- Given `<HoverCard.Root openDelay={700} closeDelay={300}>` with fake timers, when `pointerEnter` with `pointerType: 'mouse'` is fired on the trigger, timers advance 300ms, `pointerLeave` fires, and timers then advance a further 1000ms, then the content never mounts and the trigger keeps `data-state="closed"`. (radix: `packages/react/hover-card/src/hover-card.test.tsx`: "HoverCard > does not open when leaving the trigger before the open delay elapses")
- Given the same hover card, when `pointerEnter` (mouse) is fired on the trigger, then the content is still absent immediately, and after advancing timers by exactly 700ms the content is visible. (radix: `packages/react/hover-card/src/hover-card.test.tsx`: "HoverCard > opens after the open delay when the trigger stays hovered")
- Given the hover card opened by hovering the trigger for 700ms, when `pointerLeave` (mouse) fires and timers advance 300ms, then the content unmounts. (radix: `packages/react/hover-card/src/hover-card.test.tsx`: "HoverCard > closes after the close delay when leaving an open trigger")
- Given three sibling `<HoverCard.Root openDelay={700} closeDelay={300}>` instances with triggers A, B and C, when the pointer enters and leaves each trigger with only 200ms in between (less than the open delay) and timers then advance 1000ms, then none of "Content A", "Content B" or "Content C" is in the document, so sweeping across a list leaves no card lingering open. (radix: `packages/react/hover-card/src/hover-card.test.tsx`: "HoverCard > does not leave a card open when sweeping across a list of triggers")
- Given each of the three trigger layouts (contained `<PreviewCard.Trigger href="#">` inside `<PreviewCard.Root>`, a detached trigger paired with `<PreviewCard.Root handle>`, and two detached triggers sharing one handle), when `pointerdown` with `pointerType: 'mouse'`, `mouseenter` and `mousemove` fire on the `link`-role trigger and the clock advances the default `OPEN_DELAY` of 600ms, then "Content" is in the DOM. (base-ui: `packages/react/src/preview-card/root/PreviewCardRoot.test.tsx`: "when using $name > uncontrolled open > should open when the trigger is hovered")
- Given a preview card opened by a 600ms hover (run for contained, detached and multiple detached triggers), when `mouseleave` fires on the trigger and the default `CLOSE_DELAY` of 300ms elapses, then "Content" is removed. - Given a controlled preview card opened by hovering its trigger for 600ms (run for contained, detached and multiple detached triggers), when the pointer enters and then leaves the positioner and 300ms elapses, then "Content" is removed. (base-ui: `packages/react/src/preview-card/root/PreviewCardRoot.test.tsx`: "when using $name > prop: onOpenChange > closes after hovering out of a popup opened by its trigger")
- Given `<PreviewCard.Root defaultOpen>` (run for contained, detached and multiple detached triggers), when the pointer enters and leaves the positioner and 300ms elapses, then "Content" stays in the DOM because the card was not opened by trigger hover. - Given `<PreviewCard.Trigger delay={100}>` (run for contained, detached and multiple detached triggers), when `mouseenter` plus `mousemove` fire, then "Content" is absent immediately and present after 100ms. - Given three detached `<PreviewCard.Trigger handle delay={0} closeDelay={0}>` links sharing one handle and one `<PreviewCard.Root handle>`, when each is hovered (`mouseenter` plus `mousemove`) and then left, then the shared popup becomes visible for each and unmounts after each leave. ### Positioning

- Given `<HoverCard.Arrow asChild>` wrapping an `<svg>` inside the content of an open hover card, when rendered, then the element's `tagName` is the lower-case `svg` and it carries `viewBox="0 0 30 10"`, plus the author class, inline style and ref, and clicking fires `onClick`. ### Animation and presence

- Given a controlled `<PreviewCard.Root open onOpenChangeComplete>` with no exit animation (run for contained, detached and multiple detached triggers), when a "Close" button sets `open` to `false`, then the popup unmounts, the first `onOpenChangeComplete` call received `true` and the last received `false`. (base-ui: `packages/react/src/preview-card/root/PreviewCardRoot.test.tsx`: "when using $name > prop: onOpenChangeComplete > is called on close when there is no exit animation defined") (browser-mode only)

(base-ui: `packages/react/src/preview-card/root/PreviewCardRoot.test.tsx`: "when using $name > prop: onOpenChangeComplete > is called on close when the exit animation finishes") (browser-mode only)
- Given a controlled `<PreviewCard.Root open={false} onOpenChangeComplete>` with no enter animation (run for contained, detached and multiple detached triggers), when "Open" is clicked, then the popup mounts and `onOpenChangeComplete` has been called twice with the first call receiving `true`. (base-ui: `packages/react/src/preview-card/root/PreviewCardRoot.test.tsx`: "when using $name > prop: onOpenChangeComplete > is called on open when there is no enter animation defined") (browser-mode only)
- Given `BASE_UI_ANIMATIONS_DISABLED = false` and a popup whose `.animation-test-indicator[data-starting-style]` runs a 1ms `test-anim` animation (run for contained, detached and multiple detached triggers), when "Open" is clicked, then `onOpenChangeComplete` first fires with `true` once the enter animation finishes and the popup is present. (base-ui: `packages/react/src/preview-card/root/PreviewCardRoot.test.tsx`: "when using $name > prop: onOpenChangeComplete > is called on open when the enter animation finishes") (browser-mode only)
- Given a closed `<PreviewCard.Root onOpenChangeComplete>` (run for contained, detached and multiple detached triggers), when it mounts, then `onOpenChangeComplete` is never called.
