- Given `BASE_UI_ANIMATIONS_DISABLED = false` and two detached `delay={0}` triggers feeding one `<PreviewCard.Root handle>` whose popup wraps a `<PreviewCard.Viewport>`, when the pointer moves from trigger 1 to trigger 2 so the content switches from `1` to `2`, then the popup's inline `style.scale` is the empty string. - Given `<HoverCard.Trigger>` with an `HTMLAnchorElement` `ref`, `data-testid`, `className="custom-class"`, `style={{ outlineColor: 'rgb(1, 2, 3)' }}` and `onClick`, when rendered, then the props land on the rendered trigger, the ref resolves to it, and clicking fires `onClick`. (radix: `packages/react/hover-card/src/hover-card.test.tsx`: "HoverCard.Trigger > spreads props it does not consume onto the element it renders")
- Given `<HoverCard.Content>` with `ref`, `data-testid`, `className`, inline `style` and `onClick` inside `<HoverCard.Root open>`, when rendered, then the props land on the content element, the ref resolves to it, and clicking fires `onClick`. (radix: `packages/react/hover-card/src/hover-card.test.tsx`: "HoverCard.Content > spreads props it does not consume onto the element it renders")
- Given `<HoverCard.Arrow>` with an `SVGSVGElement` `ref`, `data-testid`, `className`, inline `style` and `onClick` inside open content, when rendered, then the props land on the arrow element, the ref resolves to it, and clicking fires `onClick`. (radix: `packages/react/hover-card/src/hover-card.test.tsx`: "HoverCard.Arrow > spreads props it does not consume onto the element it renders")

## tooltip

### Roles and attributes

- Given `<Tooltip.Provider>` wrapping `<Tooltip.Root>` with a trigger and portalled content containing an `Arrow`, when rendered without interaction, then the trigger text is in the document and the content text is not. (radix: `packages/react/tooltip/src/tooltip.test.tsx`: "Tooltip rendering > renders tooltip trigger")
- Given `<Tooltip.Root delayDuration={0}>` whose trigger already has `aria-describedby="existing-description"` and whose content has `id="tooltip-description"`, when the trigger is hovered, then `aria-describedby` becomes `"existing-description tooltip-description"`, and after clicking the trigger to dismiss it reverts to `"existing-description"`. (radix: `packages/react/tooltip/src/tooltip.test.tsx`: "Tooltip rendering > appends the tooltip id to an existing aria-describedby")
- Given a trigger with `aria-describedby=" existing-description\texisting-description tooltip-description "` and content `id="tooltip-description"`, when the tooltip opens on hover, then `aria-describedby` is normalized and de-duplicated to exactly `"existing-description tooltip-description"`. (radix: `packages/react/tooltip/src/tooltip.test.tsx`: "Tooltip rendering > normalizes and deduplicates aria-describedby ids when the tooltip opens")
- Given `<Tooltip.Trigger asChild>` wrapping a `<button aria-describedby="existing-description">` and content `id="tooltip-description"`, when the trigger is hovered then clicked, then `aria-describedby` becomes `"existing-description tooltip-description"` while open and returns to `"existing-description"` after dismissal. (radix: `packages/react/tooltip/src/tooltip.test.tsx`: "Tooltip rendering > appends the tooltip id to aria-describedby on an asChild trigger")
- Given `<Tooltip.Content id="custom-id">`, when the trigger is hovered, then the trigger's `aria-describedby` is `"custom-id"` and the element with `role="tooltip"` has `id="custom-id"`. (radix: `packages/react/tooltip/src/tooltip.test.tsx`: "Tooltip rendering > keeps aria-describedby in sync with a custom content id")
- Given `<Tooltip.Content aria-label="Accessible label" id="custom-id">Tooltip Content</Tooltip.Content>`, when the tooltip is opened by hover, then exactly one element matches `#custom-id`, the trigger's `aria-describedby` is `"custom-id"`, and that element has `role="tooltip"` with text content "Accessible label" and NOT "Tooltip Content", so the description resolves to the label rather than the visible children. (radix: `packages/react/tooltip/src/tooltip.test.tsx`: "Tooltip rendering > keeps a custom id unique when combined with aria-label")

- Given `<Tooltip.Trigger delay={0} closeDelay={0}>` (run for contained, detached and multiple detached triggers), when the trigger is focused the popup carries `data-instant="focus"`, and when it is later opened by `pointerdown`/`mouseenter`/`mousemove` the popup has no `data-instant` attribute. (base-ui: `packages/react/src/tooltip/root/TooltipRoot.test.tsx`: "when using $name > instant animations > marks the popup as instant when opened by focus, but not when opened by hover") (browser-mode only)
- Given a closed `<Tooltip.Root>` with `<Tooltip.Portal keepMounted>`, then the popup element exists in the DOM but is inaccessible (`toBeInaccessible`) rather than unmounted. (base-ui: `packages/react/src/tooltip/portal/TooltipPortal.test.tsx`: "prop: keepMounted > renders the closed popup as hidden instead of unmounting it")
- Given a closed `<Tooltip.Root>` with `<Tooltip.Portal>` and no `keepMounted`, then the popup element is not in the DOM. (base-ui: `packages/react/src/tooltip/portal/TooltipPortal.test.tsx`: "prop: keepMounted > unmounts the closed popup by default")
- Given `BASE_UI_ANIMATIONS_DISABLED = false` and two detached `delay={0}` triggers feeding one `<Tooltip.Root handle>` whose popup wraps a `<Tooltip.Viewport>`, when the pointer moves from trigger 1 to trigger 2 so the content switches from `1` to `2`, then the popup's inline `style.scale` is the empty string, so no inline scale overrides the user's CSS transitions. (base-ui: `packages/react/src/tooltip/root/TooltipRoot.detached-triggers.test.tsx`: "multiple detached triggers > should not have inline scale style after switching triggers") (browser-mode only)
- Given `<Tooltip.Viewport data-testid="viewport">` inside a `delay={0} closeDelay={0}` tooltip, when the trigger is focused, then the viewport carries `data-instant="focus"`, mirroring the tooltip's instant type. (base-ui: `packages/react/src/tooltip/viewport/TooltipViewport.test.tsx`: "should mirror the instant animation type of the tooltip") (browser-mode only)
- Given `<Tooltip.Root>` whose children function renders a different `<img>` per payload inside `<Tooltip.Viewport>`, with two `delay={0}` triggers, when focus moves from trigger 1 to trigger 2, then the second image's `[data-current]` container is a different element from the first's, so the current container remounts on trigger change. (base-ui: `packages/react/src/tooltip/viewport/TooltipViewport.test.tsx`: "should remount the `current` container when the active trigger changes")
- Given `BASE_UI_ANIMATIONS_DISABLED = false` and CSS that animates `[data-transitioning] [data-previous]` and `[data-transitioning] [data-current]` over 0.3s, when focus moves between two absolutely positioned `delay={0}` triggers with payloads 0 and 1, then a `[data-previous]` container appears carrying the `inert` attribute and the old text "Content 0" while `[data-current]` holds "Content 1"; after the animation the `[data-previous]` container is removed and `[data-current]` stays visible. (base-ui: `packages/react/src/tooltip/viewport/TooltipViewport.test.tsx`: "morphing containers with multiple triggers and payloads > should create morphing containers during transitions") (browser-mode only)
- Given the same morphing setup with 10s slide animations and three `delay={0}` triggers, when focus goes trigger 1, trigger 2, then trigger 3 within single frames, then the `[data-current]` container for "Content 3" has exactly one running animation, the viewport still has `data-transitioning`, and `[data-previous]` holds "Content 2". (base-ui: `packages/react/src/tooltip/viewport/TooltipViewport.test.tsx`: "morphing containers with multiple triggers and payloads > keeps the latest transition active during rapid trigger changes") (browser-mode only)
- Given a morph driven by 10s `transform`/`opacity` transitions with `[data-current][data-starting-style]` and `[data-previous][data-ending-style]` rules, when the payload for the already-active trigger arrives a render later and remounts the current container mid-morph, then the new `[data-current]` container restarts its entry transition with at least one running animation, `[data-previous]` survives the next four frames instead of being torn down, and once all animations are finished `[data-previous]` is removed and the viewport loses `data-transitioning`. (base-ui: `packages/react/src/tooltip/viewport/TooltipViewport.test.tsx`: "morphing containers with multiple triggers and payloads > cleans up the transition when a lagging payload remounts the current container") (browser-mode only)

### SSR and hydration

- Given a server-rendered `<Tooltip.Root handle defaultOpen defaultTriggerId="trigger">` plus a detached `<Tooltip.Trigger handle id="trigger">` inside `<React.Suspense>` whose render throws a promise during hydration, then the server markup's trigger has no `data-popup-open`, `handle.isOpen` stays `true` throughout the suspended hydration, and once the promise resolves the trigger gains `data-popup-open`. (base-ui: `packages/react/src/tooltip/root/TooltipRoot.detached-triggers.test.tsx`: "keeps a default-open root open until its detached trigger hydrates") (jsdom only)
- Given a server-rendered controlled `<Tooltip.Root handle open triggerId="trigger-a" onOpenChange>` with trigger A in the same tree and trigger B server-rendered into a separate container that has not hydrated, when the app switches `triggerId` to `"trigger-b"`, then `onOpenChange` is never called and `handle.isOpen` stays `true`; once `ReactDOMClient.hydrateRoot` hydrates trigger B, that button gains `data-popup-open`. (base-ui: `packages/react/src/tooltip/root/TooltipRoot.detached-triggers.test.tsx`: "keeps an open root open when ownership moves to a trigger that has not hydrated") (jsdom only)

### Notes and edge cases

- Given `<Tooltip.Content>` whose single child component counts its own mounts in a `useEffect`, when the tooltip opens on hover, then exactly one element matches the content text and the child mounted once, so the children are not rendered twice. (radix: `packages/react/tooltip/src/tooltip.test.tsx`: "Tooltip rendering > does not duplicate content children")
- Given `<Tooltip.Content aria-label="Accessible label">` wrapping a mount-counting child, when the tooltip opens on hover, then the content text appears exactly once, the child mounted once, and the element with `role="tooltip"` has text content "Accessible label". (radix: `packages/react/tooltip/src/tooltip.test.tsx`: "Tooltip rendering > uses aria-label without duplicating content children")
- Given three sibling `<Tooltip.Root delayDuration={0}>` instances each wrapped in a `React.Profiler` counting commits, when trigger "a" is hovered until its content is visible, then tooltip "a"'s commit count increases while "b" and "c" record zero additional commits. (radix: `packages/react/tooltip/src/tooltip.test.tsx`: "Tooltip behavior > hovering one tooltip does not re-render sibling tooltips")
- Given `<Tooltip.Trigger>` with `ref`, `data-testid`, `className="custom-class"`, `style={{ outlineColor: 'rgb(1, 2, 3)' }}` and `onClick`, when rendered, then the props land on the rendered trigger, the ref resolves to it, and clicking fires the author `onClick` composed with the trigger's own handler. (radix: `packages/react/tooltip/src/tooltip.test.tsx`: "Tooltip.Trigger > spreads props it does not consume onto the element it renders")
- Given `<Tooltip.Content>` with `ref`, `data-testid`, `className`, inline `style` and `onClick` inside `<Tooltip.Root open>`, when rendered, then the props land on the content element, the ref resolves to it, and clicking fires `onClick`. (radix: `packages/react/tooltip/src/tooltip.test.tsx`: "Tooltip.Content > spreads props it does not consume onto the element it renders")
- Given `<Tooltip.Arrow>` with an `SVGSVGElement` `ref`, `data-testid`, `className`, inline `style` and `onClick` inside open content, when rendered, then the props land on the arrow element, the ref resolves to it, and clicking fires `onClick`. (radix: `packages/react/tooltip/src/tooltip.test.tsx`: "Tooltip.Arrow > spreads props it does not consume onto the element it renders")
- Given a `<Tooltip.Root>`/`<Tooltip.Trigger>`/`<Tooltip.Portal>`/`<Tooltip.Positioner>`/`<Tooltip.Popup>` tree, the shared `popupConformanceTests` suite runs with `{ triggerMouseAction: 'hover' }`, so the tooltip is asserted against the harness's shared trigger, portal and popup contract using hover rather than click to open. (base-ui: `packages/react/src/tooltip/root/TooltipRoot.test.tsx`: "popupConformanceTests")
- Given an outer trigger containing a nested tooltip trigger, when a `mouseover` event is dispatched on the inner trigger whose `composedPath()` is stubbed, then the outer popup stays closed for both stubbed paths: one that "starts with a ShadowRoot" and one that "is empty". (base-ui: `packages/react/src/tooltip/root/TooltipRoot.test.tsx`: "nested tooltips > handles a composed path that $name")
- Given `<Tooltip.Arrow />`, the shared `describeConformance` suite runs with `{ refInstanceof: window.Element }` and a custom `render` that mounts it inside `<Tooltip.Root open><Tooltip.Portal><Tooltip.Positioner><Tooltip.Popup>`, so the part is asserted to forward props, forward refs, support the `render` prop and merge classNames. (base-ui: `packages/react/src/tooltip/arrow/TooltipArrow.test.tsx`: "describeConformance")
- Given `<Tooltip.Portal />`, the shared `describeConformance` suite runs with `{ refInstanceof: window.HTMLDivElement }` and a custom `render` that mounts it inside `<Tooltip.Root open>`. (base-ui: `packages/react/src/tooltip/portal/TooltipPortal.test.tsx`: "describeConformance")
- Given `<Tooltip.Popup />`, the shared `describeConformance` suite runs with `{ refInstanceof: window.HTMLDivElement }` and a custom `render` that mounts it inside `<Tooltip.Root open><Tooltip.Portal><Tooltip.Positioner>`. (base-ui: `packages/react/src/tooltip/popup/TooltipPopup.test.tsx`: "describeConformance")

## toast

### Roles and attributes

- Given a `<Toast.Provider>` wrapping a `<Toast.Viewport>` whose list renders `<Toast.Root data-testid="root">` with `<Toast.Title data-testid="title" />`, when a toast is added via `useToastManager().add({ title: 'title', description: 'description', actionProps: { id: 'action', children: 'action' } })`, then the root element's `aria-labelledby` equals the rendered title element's `id`. (base-ui: `packages/react/src/toast/title/ToastTitle.test.tsx`: "adds aria-labelledby to the root element")
- Given a toast added with `title: 'title'`, when `<Toast.Title />` renders with no children of its own, then it renders the toast object's `title` as its text content (`textContent === 'title'`). (base-ui: `packages/react/src/toast/title/ToastTitle.test.tsx`: "renders the title by default")
- Given `<Toast.Title render={<div>render prop title</div>} />` inside `<Toast.Root toast={{ id: 'test' }} data-testid="root">`, when rendered, then the root's `aria-labelledby` equals the render-prop element's generated `id`. (base-ui: `packages/react/src/toast/title/ToastTitle.test.tsx`: "wires aria-labelledby to a title rendered through the render prop")
- Given `<Toast.Title>{title}</Toast.Title>` with `title` initially `'Toast title'` so the root has a non-null `aria-labelledby`, when a button sets the title state to `null`, then the title text is gone and the root's `aria-labelledby` attribute is removed (`getAttribute('aria-labelledby') === null`). (base-ui: `packages/react/src/toast/title/ToastTitle.test.tsx`: "clears aria-labelledby from the root when the title content is removed")
- Given a `<Toast.Root data-testid="root">` rendering `<Toast.Title key="old" id="old-title">Old</Toast.Title>`, when rerendered to show both titles and then only `<Toast.Title key="new" id="new-title">New</Toast.Title>`, then `aria-labelledby` moves to `"new-title"` when both are present and stays `"new-title"` after the old title unmounts, i.e. the older title's cleanup must not clear the newer registration. (base-ui: `packages/react/src/toast/title/ToastTitle.test.tsx`: "does not let an older title cleanup clear a newer title")
- Given a `<Toast.Provider>`/`<Toast.Viewport>` list rendering `<Toast.Root data-testid="root">` with `<Toast.Description data-testid="description" />`, when a toast is added with a `description`, then the root's `aria-describedby` equals the description element's `id`. (base-ui: `packages/react/src/toast/description/ToastDescription.test.tsx`: "adds aria-describedby to the root element")
- Given a toast added with `description: 'description'`, when `<Toast.Description />` renders with no children, then it renders the toast object's `description` as its text content (`textContent === 'description'`). (base-ui: `packages/react/src/toast/description/ToastDescription.test.tsx`: "renders the description by default")
- Given `<Toast.Description render={<div>render prop description</div>} />` inside `<Toast.Root toast={{ id: 'test' }} data-testid="root">`, when rendered, then the root's `aria-describedby` equals the render-prop element's generated `id`. (base-ui: `packages/react/src/toast/description/ToastDescription.test.tsx`: "wires aria-describedby to a description rendered through the render prop")
- Given a toast added with `actionProps: { id: 'action', children: 'action' }` and a list rendering `<Toast.Action data-testid="action" />`, when the toast is added, then the action element receives `id="action"` from `actionProps`. (base-ui: `packages/react/src/toast/action/ToastAction.test.tsx`: "performs an action when clicked")
- Given two toasts added in sequence (`toast-1` then `toast-2`), each rendering `<Toast.Content data-testid={`content-${title}`}>`, when both are mounted, then the frontmost (newest) toast's content has no `data-behind` attribute and the older toast's content has `data-behind`. (base-ui: `packages/react/src/toast/content/ToastContent.test.tsx`: "marks content behind the frontmost toast with data-behind")
- Given `<Toast.Viewport data-testid="viewport">` with one toast added, when the toast mounts and is measured, then the viewport's inline style sets `--toast-frontmost-height` to a non-empty value. (base-ui: `packages/react/src/toast/viewport/ToastViewport.test.tsx`: "sets the measured frontmost toast height CSS variable") (browser-mode only)
- Given a `<Toast.Root data-testid="root">` list inside `<Toast.Viewport>`, when a toast is added, then the root's inline style sets `--toast-offset-y` to a non-empty value. (base-ui: `packages/react/src/toast/root/ToastRoot.test.tsx`: "sets the vertical offset CSS variable")
- Given a `<Toast.Root toast={{ id: 'test', title: 'Toast title', description: 'Toast description' }} data-testid="root">` whose `<Toast.Title data-testid="title">`/`<Toast.Description data-testid="description">` children switch between deriving their text from the toast object, explicit children, and being unmounted, when the mode changes to `'explicit'`, then `aria-labelledby`/`aria-describedby` still point at the mounted parts and the text reads `'Explicit title'`/`'Explicit description'`; when both parts unmount (`'none'`), then the root has neither `aria-labelledby` nor `aria-describedby`; when they are restored, then both attributes point at the new part ids and the text falls back to the toast object's `'Toast title'`/`'Toast description'`. (base-ui: `packages/react/src/toast/root/ToastRoot.test.tsx`: "keeps dynamic title and description ids synchronized with mounted label parts")
- Given a toast `{ id: 'resizable-toast', title: 'Loading', description: 'Short' }` rendered in a `<Toast.Root style={{ width: 30 }}>` with `<Toast.Content>`, when `update(toastId, { title: 'Success', description: <longer text> })` grows the content, then the root's `--toast-height` CSS variable increases above its initial measured value. (base-ui: `packages/react/src/toast/root/ToastRoot.test.tsx`: "recalculates height when content mutates") (browser-mode only)
- Given a custom list rendering `<Toast.Title data-testid="title">{t.title}</Toast.Title>`, when `add({ title: 'title', description: 'description' })` is called, then the title element's text content is `'title'`. (base-ui: `packages/react/src/toast/useToastManager.test.tsx`: "useToast > add > option: title > renders the title") (jsdom only)
- Given a custom list rendering `<Toast.Description data-testid="description">{t.description}</Toast.Description>`, when `add({ title: 'title', description: 'description' })` is called, then the description element's text content is `'description'`. (base-ui: `packages/react/src/toast/useToastManager.test.tsx`: "useToast > add > option: description > renders the description") (jsdom only)
- Given a custom list rendering `{t.type}` inside the toast root, when `add({ title: 'test', type: 'success' })` is called, then the title reads `'test'` and the text `'success'` is present, i.e. the `type` option is exposed on the toast object. (base-ui: `packages/react/src/toast/useToastManager.test.tsx`: "useToast > add > option: type > renders the type") (jsdom only)

### Keyboard

- Given three `Toast.Root` elements all `open` with `duration={Infinity}` inside a `Toast.Provider` plus a `Toast.Viewport`, when the second toast's `li` is focused and `Escape` is pressed on it, then only that toast's `onOpenChange` is called with `false` and the first and third toasts' `onOpenChange` are never called. (radix: `packages/react/toast/src/toast.test.tsx`: "escape key removal > closes only the focused (non-topmost) toast on Escape")
- Given three `Toast.Root` elements all `open` with `duration={Infinity}`, when `Escape` is pressed on `document.body` (focus outside any toast), then only the topmost (third/most recent) toast's `onOpenChange` is called with `false` and the other two are never called. (radix: `packages/react/toast/src/toast.test.tsx`: "escape key removal > closes the topmost toast on Escape when focus is outside any toast")

### Pointer

- Given a toast added with `<Toast.Close aria-label="close-press" />` in the list and the viewport focused via `viewport.focus()`, when the close button is clicked, then the toast is removed from the DOM (`queryByTestId('title') === null`). (base-ui: `packages/react/src/toast/close/ToastClose.test.tsx`: "closes the toast when clicked")
- Given one toast rendered inside `<Toast.Viewport data-testid="viewport">` with `<Toast.Content>`, when `mouseEnter` fires on the viewport, then the content element gains `data-expanded` (it has no `data-expanded` before the hover). (base-ui: `packages/react/src/toast/content/ToastContent.test.tsx`: "reflects the expanded state when the viewport is hovered")
- Given one toast rendered in `<Toast.Viewport data-testid="viewport">`, when `mouseEnter` then `mouseLeave` fire on the toast root and no element inside is focus-visible, then the viewport gains `data-expanded` on enter and loses it on leave. (base-ui: `packages/react/src/toast/viewport/ToastViewport.test.tsx`: "removes expanded on mouseleave when focus-visible not inside")
- Given one toast where `{F6}` then `{Tab}` have moved focus-visible into the viewport, when `mouseEnter` then `mouseLeave` fire on the toast root, then the viewport keeps `data-expanded` after the pointer leaves. (base-ui: `packages/react/src/toast/viewport/ToastViewport.test.tsx`: "keeps expanded on mouseleave when focus-visible is inside")
- Given one toast whose root has stubbed `setPointerCapture`/`releasePointerCapture`, when `pointerDown` at `(100, 100)` with `pointerType: 'touch'` and `pointerId: 1` is followed by `pointerMove` to `(100, 120)`, then the viewport has `data-expanded`; a `mouseLeave` on the viewport during the swipe does not remove it, and it is only removed after `pointerUp`. (base-ui: `packages/react/src/toast/viewport/ToastViewport.test.tsx`: "keeps expanded during an active touch swipe even if mouseleave fires")
- Given a touch swipe in progress (`pointerDown` at `(100, 100)` then `pointerMove` to `(100, 120)`, `pointerType: 'touch'`), then the root has `data-swiping` and the viewport `data-expanded`; when `pointerCancel` fires without any `mouseLeave`, then `data-swiping` is removed from the root while the viewport keeps `data-expanded`. (base-ui: `packages/react/src/toast/viewport/ToastViewport.test.tsx`: "keeps expanded when a touch swipe is canceled without leaving the viewport")
- Given a touch swipe in progress (`pointerDown` at `(100, 100)` then `pointerMove` to `(100, 120)`, `pointerType: 'touch'`), when `mouseLeave` fires on the viewport and then `pointerCancel` fires, then the root loses `data-swiping` and the viewport loses `data-expanded` (the deferred collapse runs). (base-ui: `packages/react/src/toast/viewport/ToastViewport.test.tsx`: "collapses after a touch swipe is canceled if mouseleave already fired")
- Given one toast with fake timers and the default 5000ms timeout, when `mouseEnter` fires on the toast root and the clock ticks 5001ms, then the toast is still in the DOM (hover pauses the auto-dismiss timer). (base-ui: `packages/react/src/toast/viewport/ToastViewport.test.tsx`: "timers > pauses timers when hovering")
- Given one toast paused by `mouseEnter` and a 5000ms tick while hovered, when `mouseLeave` fires and the clock ticks 4999ms, then the toast is still present; after 2ms more it is removed — the timer resumes from the full remaining delay. (base-ui: `packages/react/src/toast/viewport/ToastViewport.test.tsx`: "timers > resumes timers when not hovering")
- Given a hovered viewport with `data-expanded` and timers paused past 5001ms, when `pointerDown` with `pointerType: 'touch'` fires on `document.body` (outside the viewport), then `data-expanded` is removed and the toast is dismissed after a further 5001ms tick. (base-ui: `packages/react/src/toast/viewport/ToastViewport.test.tsx`: "timers > collapses and resumes timers on a touch outside the viewport")
- Given a hovered viewport, when `pointerDown` with `pointerType: 'touch'` fires on the viewport itself, then it keeps `data-expanded` and the toast survives a 5001ms tick. (base-ui: `packages/react/src/toast/viewport/ToastViewport.test.tsx`: "timers > stays expanded on a touch inside the viewport")

### Focus management

- Given a toast story with a focusable element before and after an empty `Toast.Viewport` and zero toasts, when focus is on "Focusable before viewport" and `Tab` is pressed, then focus moves to "Focusable after viewport", and `Shift+Tab` moves it back — the empty viewport does not interrupt natural document tab order. (radix: `e2e/toast.spec.ts`: "Toast > given zero toasts > should not interrupt natural tab order in the document")
- Given two toasts added to the viewport (each with two buttons), when tabbing forward from "Focusable before viewport", then focus visits toast 2, button 2.1, button 2.2, toast 1, button 1.1, button 1.2, then "Focusable after viewport" — most recent toast first — and `Shift+Tab` walks the exact reverse order back to "Focusable before viewport". (radix: `e2e/toast.spec.ts`: "Toast > given multiple toasts > should reverse tab order from most recent to least")
- Given two toasts in the viewport, when the `F8` viewport hotkey is pressed and then `Tab`, then focus lands on the latest toast (toast 2); when `F8` then `Shift+Tab` is pressed, then focus leaves the viewport backwards onto "Focusable before viewport". (radix: `e2e/toast.spec.ts`: "Toast > given multiple toasts > should tab forwards from viewport to latest toast or backwards into the document")
- Given a toast added into `<Toast.Viewport data-testid="viewport">`, when `{F6}` is pressed, then the viewport element receives focus. (base-ui: `packages/react/src/toast/viewport/ToastViewport.test.tsx`: "gets focused when F6 is pressed")

### State and controlled/uncontrolled

- Given a `Toast.Root` that is `open` with `duration={Infinity}`, when `blur` fires on `window` (pausing the toast), the component is re-rendered with `duration={3000}`, `focus` fires on `window` (resuming), and timers advance by 3000ms, then `onOpenChange` is called with `false` — a duration changed from `Infinity` to a finite value while paused takes effect on resume (fake timers). (radix: `packages/react/toast/src/toast.test.tsx`: "pause/resume with changing duration > closes after resume when duration changes from Infinity to a finite value while paused")
- Given `<Toast.Provider timeout={5000}>` whose child adds `{ id: 'toast', title: 'Toast', onClose }` from a `useIsoLayoutEffect`, when props change to `timeout={1000}` in the same commit that runs the effect, then the new timeout is already in effect for that toast: `onClose` has not fired after ticking 999ms and has fired once after ticking 2ms more (fake timers). (base-ui: `packages/react/src/toast/provider/ToastProvider.test.tsx`: "syncs a changed timeout before descendant layout effects")
- Given `<Toast.Provider limit={3}>` whose children add `{ id: 'first', timeout: 0 }` and `{ id: 'second', timeout: 0 }` from a `useIsoLayoutEffect` and then observe `store.state.toasts` from another layout effect, when props change to `limit={1}` in the commit that runs those effects, then the observer sees `[{ id: 'second', limited: false }, { id: 'first', limited: true }]`, i.e. the new limit is applied before descendant layout effects run and the newest toast wins. ### Dismissal and layering

- Given a toast added from a focused button, when `{F6}` then `{Tab}` move focus into the toast (requires a real `:focus-visible` check) and `{Escape}` is pressed, then the toast is removed from the DOM. (base-ui: `packages/react/src/toast/root/ToastRoot.test.tsx`: "closes when pressing escape") (browser-mode only)
- Given a `<Toast.Root>` whose React children include a button portalled to `document.body` via `ReactDOM.createPortal`, when that portalled button is focused and `{Escape}` is pressed, then the toast stays mounted — the key event bubbles through React to the toast but the DOM-outside element owns Escape. (base-ui: `packages/react/src/toast/root/ToastRoot.test.tsx`: "ignores Escape when focus is in portaled content")

### Positioning

- Given a toast added with `positionerProps: { anchor: anchorRef.current, side: 'bottom', sideOffset: 8 }` against an absolutely positioned button at `top: 200, left: 100, width: 80, height: 20`, when the anchor is clicked, then the `<Toast.Positioner>` gets `data-side="bottom"` and its bounding rect `top` is within 0 decimal places of `anchorRect.bottom + 8`. (base-ui: `packages/react/src/toast/positioner/ToastPositioner.test.tsx`: "positions an anchored toast against its anchor element") (browser-mode only)
- Given a toast added with no `positionerProps.anchor`, when it renders inside `<Toast.Viewport>`, then the positioner still renders with the defaults `data-side="top"` and `data-align="center"` and shows the toast title text. (base-ui: `packages/react/src/toast/positioner/ToastPositioner.test.tsx`: "falls back to the viewport when no anchor is provided")
- Given a toast added with `positionerProps: { side: 'bottom', align: 'end' }` rendered through `<Toast.Positioner side="left">`, when it mounts, then the element prop wins for side (`data-side="left"`) while the unset prop still comes from the toast object (`data-align="end"`). (base-ui: `packages/react/src/toast/positioner/ToastPositioner.test.tsx`: "lets positioner props override the ones carried on the toast")
- Given a `<Toast.Arrow data-testid="arrow" />` inside a `<Toast.Positioner>` for a toast added with `positionerProps: { anchor: anchorRef.current, side: 'bottom' }`, when the anchor button is clicked, then the arrow gets `data-side="bottom"` and `aria-hidden="true"`. (base-ui: `packages/react/src/toast/arrow/ToastArrow.test.tsx`: "mirrors the resolved side of its positioner") (browser-mode only)

### Animation and presence

- Given `<Toast.Provider toastManager={manager} timeout={0}>` with fake timers and two toasts added via `manager.add({ id: 'oldest' })` then `manager.add({ id: 'newest' })`, so `--toast-index` is `'0'` on `newest` and `'1'` on `oldest`, when `manager.close('newest')` runs, then the closing toast keeps a real index (`--toast-index` stays `'0'` rather than collapsing to `-1`) while it animates out and `oldest` becomes `'0'`. (base-ui: `packages/react/src/toast/positioner/ToastPositioner.test.tsx`: "--toast-index > keeps the DOM index while a toast animates out")
- Given two toasts with `globalThis.BASE_UI_ANIMATIONS_DISABLED = false`, the viewport hovered (`data-expanded`), and the newest root's `getAnimations` stubbed to return one animation with a controllable `finished` promise, when the newest toast is closed (gaining `data-ending-style`), then `mouseLeave` fires on the viewport, then the window `blur` listener (registered with capture, `composedPath() === [window]`) runs, and finally the clock ticks 20ms and the animation's `finished` promise resolves, then only one toast root remains and the viewport no longer has `data-expanded` — the deferred mouseleave collapse runs once the closing toast is removed. (base-ui: `packages/react/src/toast/viewport/ToastViewport.test.tsx`: "timers > collapses a deferred mouseleave after a closing toast is removed while blurred") (jsdom only)
- Given `BASE_UI_ANIMATIONS_DISABLED = false`, a 10s `opacity` transition with `[data-ending-style] { opacity: 0 }`, and a toast `{ id: 'save', title: 'Saved', timeout: 0 }`, when the toast is closed (gaining `data-ending-style` and `--toast-height` cleared to `''`) and then re-added under the same id while still animating out, then the same DOM element is reused, it never gains `data-starting-style`, and `--toast-height` is restored to its original measured value. (base-ui: `packages/react/src/toast/root/ToastRoot.test.tsx`: "clears the starting state and restores the height when re-adding an ending toast") (browser-mode only)
- Given `BASE_UI_ANIMATIONS_DISABLED = false` with a 10s ending opacity transition and two toasts `t1` and `t2` added with `timeout: 0`, when `t1` is closed (gaining `data-ending-style`) and re-added under the same id, then `t1` never gains `data-starting-style`, regains a non-empty `--toast-height`, becomes frontmost with `--toast-index: 0` and its `<Toast.Content>` has no `data-behind`, while `t2` keeps no `data-ending-style`, sits at `--toast-index: 1` and its content has `data-behind`. (base-ui: `packages/react/src/toast/root/ToastRoot.test.tsx`: "keeps stacking intact when re-adding an ending toast among other toasts") (browser-mode only)
- Given `BASE_UI_ANIMATIONS_DISABLED = false`, a 10s ending opacity transition and a `<Toast.Root swipeDirection="right">` for toast `{ id: 'save', timeout: 0 }` with stubbed pointer capture, when it is swipe-dismissed from `(100, 100)` to `(160, 100)` (gaining `data-ending-style` and `data-swipe-direction="right"`) and then re-added under the same id, then the same element is reused, it never gains `data-starting-style`, `data-swipe-direction` is removed, and both `--toast-swipe-movement-x` and `--toast-swipe-movement-y` reset to `'0px'`. (base-ui: `packages/react/src/toast/root/ToastRoot.test.tsx`: "clears swipe state when re-adding a swipe-dismissed toast") (browser-mode only)

### Accessibility tooling

- Given two toasts added to the viewport, when axe-core analyzes the subtree matching `[aria-label="Notifications (F8)"]`, then it reports zero violations. (radix: `e2e/toast.spec.ts`: "Toast > given multiple toasts > should have no acessibility issues")
- Given the default toast story with no custom announcer container, when a toast is added, then a `[role="status"]` announcement is rendered directly in `document.body` containing "Notification", "Toast 1 title" and "Toast 1 description", and after ~1100ms the `body [role="status"]` node count returns to 0. (radix: `e2e/toast.spec.ts`: "Toast > given multiple toasts > should render announcements in document body by default")
- Given the `toast--custom-announcer-container` story, when the open-toast button is clicked, then the toast becomes visible and the `[role="status"]` announcement is rendered inside `[data-testid="custom-announcer-container"]` containing "Notification", "Custom Container Toast" and "This toast's announcements are rendered in a custom container", while `body > [role="status"]` has count 0. (radix: `e2e/toast.spec.ts`: "Toast > given custom announcer container > should render announcements in the custom container")
- Given the `toast--custom-announcer-container` story with a toast opened, when ~1100ms elapse (the 1000ms announcement timeout), then the `[role="status"]` count inside the custom container drops from 1 back to 0. (radix: `e2e/toast.spec.ts`: "Toast > given custom announcer container > should clean up announcements after timeout")
- Given a toast added with `priority: 'high'` rendered through the standard list, then its root has `role="alertdialog"` and `aria-modal="false"`, an element with `role="alert"` exists and carries `aria-atomic="true"`; when the toast's `close-press` button is clicked, then no `role="alert"` element remains. (base-ui: `packages/react/src/toast/useToastManager.test.tsx`: "useToast > add > option: priority > applies correct ARIA attributes for high priority toasts") (jsdom only)
- Given an open `<Dialog.Root>` with `<Dialog.Backdrop>`/`<Dialog.Popup>` and a `<Toast.Viewport>` outside it, when a normal-priority toast `{ title: 'Toast in dialog', description: 'This toast is in a dialog' }` is added from inside the dialog, then the dialog is present and the toast root renders with its title and description readable (not hidden by the dialog's `aria-hidden` treatment of siblings). (base-ui: `packages/react/src/toast/useToastManager.test.tsx`: "useToast > in dialog > toasts in dialogs are accessible and not aria-hidden") (jsdom only)
- Given an open `<Dialog.Root>` and a toast added from inside it with `priority: 'high'`, then the toast root itself has `aria-hidden="true"` while a `role="alert"` live region still exists to announce it. (base-ui: `packages/react/src/toast/useToastManager.test.tsx`: "useToast > in dialog > high priority toasts in dialogs have correct accessibility structure") (jsdom only)

### Notes and edge cases

- Given a `Toast.Provider` wrapping an `open` `Toast.Root` with a ref and a `Toast.Viewport`, when the tree re-renders, then the composed ref on `Toast.Root` stays stable (asserted by the shared `assertStableComposedRef` helper from `@repo/test-utils/ref-stability`) — regression for issue #3963. (radix: `packages/react/toast/src/toast.test.tsx`: "ref stability > keeps a stable composed ref on the Toast root")
- Given a `Toast.Provider duration={5000}` with a `defaultOpen` `Toast.Root`, when timers advance 1000ms (short of auto-close) and the tree unmounts, then `window.clearTimeout` has been called — the pending close timer is cleared on unmount (fake timers). (radix: `packages/react/toast/src/toast.test.tsx`: "timer cleanup > should clear the close timer when the component unmounts before duration expires")
- Given a `Toast.Provider duration={5000}` with a `defaultOpen` `Toast.Root`, when timers advance 1000ms, the tree unmounts, and timers then advance a further 5000ms past the original duration, then nothing throws (no dangling timeout touching a torn-down `document`) (fake timers). (radix: `packages/react/toast/src/toast.test.tsx`: "timer cleanup > should not error when unmounting before time expires")
- Given `<Toast.Root open duration={Infinity}>` with `ref`, `data-testid`, `className="custom-class"`, `style={{ outlineColor: 'rgb(1, 2, 3)' }}` and `onClick`, then the rendered `li` carries the class and inline `outlineColor`, the ref points at it, and a click calls the supplied `onClick` (composed, not replaced). ### Roles and attributes

- Given a closed dropdown menu `<DropdownMenu.Root>` with `<DropdownMenu.Trigger>Open</DropdownMenu.Trigger>` and a portaled `<DropdownMenu.Content>` holding one `<DropdownMenu.Item>Item</DropdownMenu.Item>`, when rendered, then no element with `role="menu"` exists, the trigger carries `aria-expanded="false"`, and the trigger has no `aria-controls` attribute at all (rather than one pointing at a non-existent id). ### Pointer

- Given the open "dropdownmenu--submenus" story, when the pointer moves over the "Bookmarks →" submenu trigger, then the submenu opens but its first item "Inbox" is not focused. (radix: `e2e/dropdown-menu.spec.ts`: "DropdownMenu > given submenu user > when using pointer > should open submenu and not focus first item when moving pointer over trigger")
- Given the open "dropdownmenu--submenus" story, when the pointer moves over "Bookmarks →", then into the submenu onto "Inbox", then back onto "Bookmarks →", then the submenu stays open with "Inbox" visible. (radix: `e2e/dropdown-menu.spec.ts`: "DropdownMenu > given submenu user > when using pointer > should not close when moving pointer to submenu and back to parent trigger")
- Given the open "dropdownmenu--submenus" story at a 550x768 viewport, when the pointer exits the "Bookmarks →" trigger right-to-left (away from the submenu) the submenu closes, and when it exits left-to-right (towards the submenu) the submenu stays open; at the collision edge, where "WorkOS →" opens its submenu on the opposite side, the directions invert — exiting left-to-right closes and right-to-left keeps it open. This pins the safe-triangle/pointer-grace behavior. (radix: `e2e/dropdown-menu.spec.ts`: "DropdownMenu > given submenu user > when using pointer > at a narrow viewport > should close submenu when moving pointer away but remain open when moving towards")
- Given the open "dropdownmenu--submenus" story with the "Bookmarks →" submenu open and the pointer inside it on "Inbox", when the pointer moves to any item back in the parent menu — a plain item "New Tab", a disabled item "Print…", another submenu trigger "Tools →", or a disabled submenu trigger "History →" — then the open submenu closes in every case ("Inbox" leaves the DOM). (radix: `e2e/dropdown-menu.spec.ts`: "DropdownMenu > given submenu user > when using pointer > should close open submenu when moving pointer to any item in parent menu")
- Given the open "dropdownmenu--submenus" story with "Bookmarks →" and nested "WorkOS →" submenus both open and the pointer on the deep item "Radix", when the pointer moves back to the "Bookmarks →" trigger in the root menu, then the nested submenu closes ("Radix" leaves the DOM) while the "Bookmarks →" submenu stays open ("Inbox" visible). ### Dismissal and layering

- Given an open dropdown menu with an open submenu (root opened with `Enter` on the trigger, submenu opened with `ArrowRight` on the sub trigger), when a `FocusEvent('blur')` is dispatched on `window`, then both the sub item and the root item unmount and the trigger returns to `aria-expanded="false"`. (radix: `packages/react/dropdown-menu/src/dropdown-menu.test.tsx`: "closing on window blur > should close the menu and any open submenus when the window loses focus")
- Given the open "dropdownmenu--submenus" story, when a root item "New Tab" is clicked, when a submenu item "Inbox" is clicked after reopening and hovering "Bookmarks →", and when `body` is force-clicked outside the menu, then in all three cases every menu in the stack closes. (radix: `e2e/dropdown-menu.spec.ts`: "DropdownMenu > given submenu user > when using pointer > should close all menus when clicking item in any menu, or clicking outside")
- Given the "dropdownmenu--with-extension-overlay" story where an external overlay is opened first and then the dropdown menu, when the overlay's button is clicked — an outside press whose later mouse events the overlay stops — then the menu closes and "New Tab" leaves the DOM. (radix: `e2e/dropdown-menu.spec.ts`: "DropdownMenu extension overlay interactions > should close when an external overlay stops later mouse events")
- Given the "dropdownmenu--dismisses-only-menu-inside-dialog" story with a dialog open and a dropdown menu open inside it (state text reads "dialog: open | menu: open"), when the dialog's own heading is force-clicked (inside the dialog, outside the menu), then only the menu dismisses — the state text becomes "dialog: open | menu: closed", the dialog stays visible, and "Item one" leaves the DOM. (radix: `e2e/dropdown-menu.spec.ts`: "DropdownMenu nested in Dialog > dismisses only the menu when clicking inside dialog outside menu")
- Given a nested submenu whose first item is focused after keyboard navigation (contained and detached trigger variants), when Escape is pressed with default `closeParentOnEsc`, then only the submenu closes: exactly one visible `menu` remains and it is the root popup (`data-testid="menu"`). (base-ui: `packages/react/src/menu/root/MenuRoot.test.tsx`: "when using $name > prop: closeParentOnEsc > does not close the parent menu when the Escape key is pressed by default")
- Given a `Menu.SubmenuRoot` with `closeParentOnEsc: true` whose nested item "Item 4.1" is focused, when Escape is pressed, then no visible `menu` remains — the parent closes too. (base-ui: `packages/react/src/menu/root/MenuRoot.test.tsx`: "when using $name > prop: closeParentOnEsc > closes the parent menu when the Escape key is pressed  if `closeParentOnEsc=true`")
- Given `Menu.Root` with `modal: true` next to an outside button, when the trigger is clicked open, then the element immediately before the positioner is an internal backdrop with `role="presentation"`. - Given `Menu.Root` with `modal: false`, when the trigger is clicked open, then the positioner has no previous element sibling, i.e. no internal backdrop is rendered. (base-ui: `packages/react/src/menu/root/MenuRoot.test.tsx`: "when using $name > prop: modal > should not render an internal backdrop when `false`")
- Given a triggerless `<Menu.Root defaultOpen modal={false}>` whose positioner is anchored to `document.body` and which contains a `Menu.SubmenuRoot` (submenu trigger `openOnHover={false} delay={0}`), wrapped in a `DirectionProvider` (cases: `ltr` and `rtl`) with `Menu.Portal keepMounted` both `false` and `true`, when the direction-appropriate open key (ArrowRight in ltr, ArrowLeft in rtl) opens the submenu, then the nested "Leaf" item has focus, `onOpenChange` has not fired and the root popup has `data-open`; the first Escape closes only the submenu and returns focus to the "More" trigger without calling `onOpenChange`, and the second Escape closes the root calling `onOpenChange` exactly once with `(false, { reason: 'escape-key' })`, leaving the root element connected only when `keepMounted` is true. ### RTL and i18n

- Given the "dropdownmenu--submenus" story at a 550x768 viewport with "Right-to-left" toggled on (the menu is closed with `Escape` first so the toggle is clickable, since an open menu makes outside content `pointer-events: none`) and the menu reopened, when the pointer exits "Bookmarks →" left-to-right the submenu closes and right-to-left it stays open, with the directions inverted at the collision edge on "WorkOS →". (radix: `e2e/dropdown-menu.spec.ts`: "DropdownMenu > given submenu user > When using pointer in RTL > should close submenu when pointer moves away but remain open when moving towards")
- Given the "dropdownmenu--submenus" story with "Right-to-left" toggled on and the menu reopened, when `ArrowLeft` is dispatched on "Bookmarks →" then the submenu opens with focus on "Inbox", and when `ArrowRight` is dispatched on "Inbox" then the submenu closes while the root menu stays open ("New Tab" still visible) — the arrow roles swap under RTL. (radix: `e2e/dropdown-menu.spec.ts`: "DropdownMenu > given submenu user > When using keyboard in RTL > should open submenu and focus first item when pressing left arrow key but close when pressing right arrow key")

- Given `platform.screenReader.voiceOver` mocked to `true` (file suffix `.voiceOver.test.tsx`) and a menu opened by Tab+Enter with the submenu trigger focused at `aria-expanded="false"`, when ArrowRight opens the submenu and focus moves to its first item "Alpha", then the submenu trigger drops `aria-expanded` entirely (so VoiceOver does not talk over the item announcement) while keeping `aria-haspopup="menu"`. (base-ui: `packages/react/src/menu/submenu-trigger/MenuSubmenuTrigger.voiceOver.test.tsx`: "omits the expanded state when the submenu is opened with Enter")
- Given the VoiceOver platform mock (`.voiceOver.test.tsx`), when the submenu is opened by clicking its trigger (focus stays on the trigger, so there is no item announcement to interrupt), then the trigger keeps `aria-expanded="true"`. (base-ui: `packages/react/src/menu/submenu-trigger/MenuSubmenuTrigger.voiceOver.test.tsx`: "keeps the expanded state when the submenu is opened with a pointer")
- Given `platform.os.android` mocked to `true` (file suffix `.talkBack.test.tsx`) and an open menu, when a TalkBack-shaped synthetic press is fired on the submenu trigger (a `pointerdown` with `pointerType: 'mouse'`, `width: 1`, `height: 1`, `pressure: 0`, `detail: 0`, then `mousedown` with `detail: 0`, then `click` with `detail: 0`), then the submenu opens (the mousedown open path defers through a `requestAnimationFrame`). (browser-mode only — `isVirtualPointerEvent` returns false in jsdom) (base-ui: `packages/react/src/menu/submenu-trigger/MenuSubmenuTrigger.talkBack.test.tsx`: "opens the submenu on a TalkBack press with the default `openOnHover`")
- Given the Android/TalkBack platform mock (`.talkBack.test.tsx`) and `<Menu.SubmenuTrigger openOnHover={false}>`, when the TalkBack `pointerdown`+`mousedown` pair opens the submenu and the trailing `click` with `detail: 0` then fires, then after two animation frames the submenu is still open — the trailing click must not toggle it closed. - Given the Android/TalkBack platform mock (`.talkBack.test.tsx`) and the default `openOnHover`, when an ordinary mouse press is fired on the submenu trigger (`pointerdown` with `pressure: 0.5`, plain `mousedown`, `click` with `detail: 1`), then after two animation frames the submenu has not opened — a real pressed mouse is not treated as a virtual press. (browser-mode only) (base-ui: `packages/react/src/menu/submenu-trigger/MenuSubmenuTrigger.talkBack.test.tsx`: "ignores an ordinary mouse press with the default `openOnHover`")

## context-menu

### Roles and attributes

- Given `ContextMenu.Root` with a `Trigger` ("Right click here") and a portalled `Content` holding one `Item`, when nothing has happened, then the trigger has `data-state="closed"` and the item is not in the document. (radix: `packages/react/context-menu/src/context-menu.test.tsx`: "rendering and opening > keeps the content closed by default")
- Given a context menu whose `Content` holds a `ContextMenu.Group` containing a `ContextMenu.Label` ("Fruits") and two `Item`s, when the menu is opened by right click, then an element with `role="group"` exists, the label text renders, and `getAllByRole('menuitem')` has length 2. (radix: `packages/react/context-menu/src/context-menu.test.tsx`: "groups and labels > renders grouped items with a label")
- Given an open context menu containing `<ContextMenu.CheckboxItem disabled>`, then the item with `role="menuitemcheckbox"` has `aria-disabled="true"`. (radix: `packages/react/context-menu/src/context-menu.test.tsx`: "checkbox items > marks a disabled checkbox item as disabled")
- Given an open context menu with a `Sub`/`SubTrigger`/`SubContent`, when the submenu is closed the sub trigger has no `aria-controls` attribute; when `ArrowRight` opens it, then the sub trigger's `aria-controls` equals the non-empty `id` of the sub content element (`role="menu"`), and that id resolves via `document.getElementById` to the same element. (radix: `packages/react/context-menu/src/context-menu.test.tsx`: "submenus > associates the sub trigger with its content via `aria-controls` only while open")
- Given `<ContextMenu.Root defaultOpen>` with a `ContextMenu.Trigger`, when rendered, then the trigger has `data-popup-open=""`; after `Escape` closes the menu the attribute is removed. (base-ui: `packages/react/src/context-menu/trigger/ContextMenuTrigger.test.tsx`: "adds open state attributes")

### Roles and attributes

(base-ui: `packages/react/src/navigation-menu/root/NavigationMenuRoot.test.tsx`: "prop: onValueChange > preserves popup size when controlled value closes externally with keepMounted portal")
- Given a controlled `TestNavigationMenu` with `BASE_UI_ANIMATIONS_DISABLED = false` and trigger rects mocked so switching to `item-2` sets `data-activation-direction="right"` on `popup-2`, when the value is rerendered to `null` with a running animation, then the exiting content has `data-ending-style` and no longer has any `data-activation-direction` attribute. - Given `<TestNavigationMenuWithScopedPopupExitAnimation onOpenChangeComplete={spy} />` (350ms popup transitions, 150ms ending-style transitions, 175ms content transitions) with `BASE_UI_ANIMATIONS_DISABLED = false`, when "Product" is clicked open, "Learn" is clicked to switch content, all animations settle and `Escape` is pressed on the focused trigger, then `onOpenChangeComplete` is called exactly once with `false` and the close completes in under 325ms (the short exit path is taken after a content switch). ## select

### Roles and attributes

- Given a closed `<Select.Root>` with `<Select.Trigger aria-label="Choice">` wrapping `<Select.Value placeholder="Pick one" />` and a portaled `position="popper"` `<Select.Content>` holding two items, when rendered, then no element with `role="listbox"` exists, the `role="combobox"` trigger carries `aria-expanded="false"`, and it has no `aria-controls` attribute at all. (radix: `packages/react/select/src/select.test.tsx`: "aria-controls > should not reference a non-existent element while closed")
- Given the same Select rendered with `defaultOpen`, when the content mounts, then the `role="listbox"` element has a non-empty `id`, the combobox trigger carries `aria-expanded="true"` and `aria-controls` equal to that `id`, and `document.getElementById` on that id resolves to the listbox. (radix: `packages/react/select/src/select.test.tsx`: "aria-controls > should reference the rendered content while open")
- Given a Select whose items include one with `value=""` (text "None") rendered controlled with `value=""`, when closed, then the combobox trigger shows the placeholder text "Pick one" rather than the empty item's text "None", and it carries the bare `data-placeholder` attribute. (radix: `packages/react/select/src/select.test.tsx`: "clearing an optional value (#2706) > shows the placeholder (not the item text) when the empty value item is selected")
- Given `<Select.Trigger asChild>` wrapping `<button type="button">` around `<Select.Value placeholder="Pick one" />` on a closed Select, when rendered, then the element is a `BUTTON` carrying `role="combobox"` and `aria-expanded="false"`, keeps `className="custom-class"` and the inline `outlineColor: rgb(1, 2, 3)`, the ref resolves to it, and clicking fires the author `onClick`. ### Pointer

- Given an open Select whose second item is `<Select.Item value="banana" disabled onClick={fn}>`, when that disabled option is clicked, then the consumer's `onClick` still fires exactly once even though selection is blocked. (radix: `packages/react/select/src/select.test.tsx`: "disabled item > still calls a consumer-provided `onClick` on a disabled item")
- Given the "select--cypress-shadow-dom" story, where the select content is portaled into a shadow root, when the trigger is opened with a touch tap, the `[data-radix-select-viewport]` is touch-swiped 30px `toTop` via CDP touch events, and the "Grapes" option is then scrolled into view, polled until its bounding box is stable across two checks, and tapped, then the listbox stays attached through the swipe (no `preventDefault` on the following pointerup), closes on the tap, and the bound value updates to "food: grapes". ### Dismissal and layering

- Given the "select--with-extension-overlay" story where an external overlay is opened first and then the "choose a number" select, when the overlay's button is clicked — an outside press whose later mouse events the overlay stops — then the listbox unmounts. (radix: `e2e/select.spec.ts`: "Select extension overlay interactions > closes when an external overlay stops later mouse events")
- Given the "select--dismisses-only-select-inside-dialog" story with a dialog open and a select open inside it (state text "dialog: open | select: open"), when the dialog's own heading is force-clicked (inside the dialog, outside the select), then only the select dismisses — the state text becomes "dialog: open | select: closed", the dialog stays visible, and the option "One" leaves the DOM. (radix: `e2e/select.spec.ts`: "Select nested in Dialog > dismisses only the select when clicking inside dialog outside select")
- Given the "select--dismisses-only-select-in-popover" story with a popover open and its first select open (state text "popover: open | first: open | second: closed"), when the second select's trigger is force-clicked, then the first select closes (option "One" gone) while the popover stays open. (radix: `e2e/select.spec.ts`: "Select nested in Popover > dismisses only the open select when clicking another select trigger")
- Given `<Select.Root defaultOpen>` whose `<Select.Popup>` contains a `<Select.List>` plus a `ReactDOM.createPortal` child rendered into `document.body`, when that portalled content is clicked, then the `role="listbox"` stays mounted, i.e. React-portalled popup descendants do not count as an outside press. (base-ui: `packages/react/src/select/root/SelectRoot.test.tsx`: "does not dismiss when pressing portalled content inside the popup but outside the list")
- Given `<Select.Root modal>` (true) with a portalled positioner, when the trigger is clicked open, then an internal backdrop element with `role="presentation"` is rendered as the positioner's `previousElementSibling`. (base-ui: `packages/react/src/select/root/SelectRoot.test.tsx`: "prop: modal > should render an internal backdrop when `true`")
- Given `<Select.Root modal={false}>`, when the trigger is clicked open, then the positioner has no `previousElementSibling`, i.e. no internal backdrop is rendered. (base-ui: `packages/react/src/select/root/SelectRoot.test.tsx`: "prop: modal > should not render an internal backdrop when `false`")
- Given `<Select.Root modal>` with animations enabled and a popup whose `[data-ending-style]` runs a 20ms close animation, with `requestAnimationFrame`/`cancelAnimationFrame` stubbed so frames can be flushed manually, when a touch press (`pointerDown` with `pointerType: 'touch'` + `mouseDown`) opens it, a second touch press closes it (`aria-expanded="false"`), and a third touch press reopens it while the close animation is still pending, then after 30ms the document is not scroll-locked (no `overflow: hidden` on `documentElement`/`body` and no `data-base-ui-scroll-locked` attribute), i.e. the touch open method survives the rapid reopen. (base-ui: `packages/react/src/select/root/SelectRoot.test.tsx`: "scroll locking > interaction type tracking (openMethod) > keeps touch interaction type when reopening quickly after close") (browser-mode only)
- Given `<Select.Root modal>` whose `<Select.Positioner>` is styled `width: calc(100vw - 10px)`, when a touch press (`pointerDown` `pointerType: 'touch'` + `mouseDown`) opens the listbox, then the document becomes scroll-locked (`documentElement`/`body` `overflow: hidden` or `data-base-ui-scroll-locked` present). (base-ui: `packages/react/src/select/root/SelectRoot.test.tsx`: "scroll locking > touch scroll lock > applies scroll lock when a touch-opened popup covers the viewport width") (browser-mode only)
- Given the same `<Select.Root modal>` with the positioner styled `width: 240px` (narrower than the viewport), when a touch press opens the listbox and one animation frame passes, then the document is not scroll-locked. - Given `<Select.Root actionsRef>` with `<Select.Positioner alignItemWithTrigger={false}>`, kept-mounted `<Select.ScrollUpArrow>`/`<Select.ScrollDownArrow>` (rendered "▲"/"▼") and a `<Select.List>` stubbed to `scrollTop: 20`, `scrollHeight: 100`, `clientHeight: 50`, run both non-strict and StrictMode (`it.each([false, true])`), when the select is opened and scrolled so both arrows have `data-visible`, then closed, and `actionsRef.current.unmount()` is called after one animation frame, then both arrows lose `data-visible`. - Given the same controlled select with animations enabled and a popup whose `[data-ending-style]` runs a 1ms `test-anim` animation, when the open animation has completed (`onOpenChangeComplete` called with `true`) and "Close" is clicked, then the listbox unmounts and `onOpenChangeComplete` is last called with `false` only after the exit animation finishes. ## combobox

### Roles and attributes

- Given a closed `<Combobox.Root>` with `<Combobox.Input />` and an empty portalled positioner, then the input has `role="combobox"`, `aria-expanded="false"`, `aria-autocomplete="list"`, `aria-haspopup="listbox"` and neither `aria-controls` nor `aria-activedescendant`. (base-ui: `packages/react/src/combobox/root/ComboboxRoot.test.tsx`: "aria attributes > sets all aria attributes on the input when closed")
- Given `<Combobox.Root defaultOpen>` with an empty `<Combobox.List />` in the popup, then the input has `role="combobox"`, `aria-expanded="true"`, `aria-autocomplete="list"`, `aria-haspopup="listbox"`, `aria-controls` equal to the `listbox` element's id, and no `aria-activedescendant`. (base-ui: `packages/react/src/combobox/root/ComboboxRoot.test.tsx`: "aria attributes > sets all aria attributes on the input when open")
- Given `<Combobox.Root inline open>` with an inline `<Combobox.List />`, then the input has `role="combobox"`, `aria-expanded="true"` and `aria-controls` equal to the `listbox` id. (base-ui: `packages/react/src/combobox/root/ComboboxRoot.test.tsx`: "aria attributes > sets aria-expanded on the input when rendered inline and open")
- Given `<Combobox.Root inline open grid>`, then the input has `aria-expanded="true"`, `aria-haspopup="grid"` and `aria-controls` equal to the `grid` element's id. (base-ui: `packages/react/src/combobox/root/ComboboxRoot.test.tsx`: "aria attributes > sets the popup type on the input when rendered inline as a grid")
- Given `<Combobox.Root inline items={['apple','banana']}>` with no `open` prop, then the input already reads `aria-expanded="true"` with `aria-controls` pointing at the `listbox`, and both stay unchanged after the input is clicked. (base-ui: `packages/react/src/combobox/root/ComboboxRoot.test.tsx`: "aria attributes > keeps the input expanded when rendered inline without the `open` prop")
- Given `<Combobox.Root defaultOpen>` with items `a` and `b`, when the input is clicked (no `aria-activedescendant`) and `ArrowDown` pressed, then both options stay `aria-selected="false"` while the input's `aria-activedescendant` points at option `a`; after `Enter` and reopening, option `a` reads `aria-selected="true"` and `b` stays `aria-selected="false"`. (base-ui: `packages/react/src/combobox/root/ComboboxRoot.test.tsx`: "aria attributes > sets correct attributes on the item when highlighted")
- Given `<Combobox.Root defaultOpen>` with a `<Combobox.Trigger>` and the input inside the popup, then the `dialog` popup has a non-empty `id`, the trigger (the `BUTTON` with `role="combobox"`) has `aria-controls` equal to that id and `aria-expanded="true"`; clicking the trigger to close sets `aria-expanded="false"` and removes `aria-controls`. (base-ui: `packages/react/src/combobox/root/ComboboxRoot.test.tsx`: "aria attributes > sets aria-controls to the dialog popup on trigger")
- Given `<Combobox.Popup id="custom-popup-id">` inside a `defaultOpen` combobox with a trigger, then the `dialog` id is `custom-popup-id` and the trigger's `aria-controls` is `custom-popup-id`. (base-ui: `packages/react/src/combobox/root/ComboboxRoot.test.tsx`: "aria attributes > points aria-controls at a custom popup id on the trigger")
- Given `<Combobox.Popup render={<div id="custom-render-id" />}>` inside a `defaultOpen` combobox with a trigger, then the `dialog` id is `custom-render-id` and the trigger's `aria-controls` is `custom-render-id`. (base-ui: `packages/react/src/combobox/root/ComboboxRoot.test.tsx`: "aria attributes > points aria-controls at a popup id supplied through the render prop")
- Given `<Combobox.Root id="test-id">` with the input outside the popup, then the input carries `id="test-id"`. (base-ui: `packages/react/src/combobox/root/ComboboxRoot.test.tsx`: "prop: id > sets the id on the input when it is outside the popup")
- Given `<Combobox.Root id="test-id" defaultOpen>` with a trigger and the input inside the popup, then the trigger has `id="test-id"` and the input does not. (base-ui: `packages/react/src/combobox/root/ComboboxRoot.test.tsx`: "prop: id > sets the id on the trigger when the input is inside the popup")
- Given `<Combobox.Root readOnly>` with `<Combobox.Input />`, then the input has `aria-readonly="true"` and the `readonly` attribute. (base-ui: `packages/react/src/combobox/root/ComboboxRoot.test.tsx`: "prop: readOnly > should render readOnly state on the input")
- Given `<Combobox.Root readOnly>`, then the input has `aria-autocomplete="none"`. (base-ui: `packages/react/src/combobox/root/ComboboxRoot.test.tsx`: "prop: readOnly > should expose aria-autocomplete=\"none\" when readOnly")
- Given `<Combobox.Root defaultOpen>` with an inline `<Combobox.List>` holding one item, then the `listbox` element has no `aria-orientation` attribute (listbox is implicitly vertical). (base-ui: `packages/react/src/combobox/root/ComboboxRoot.test.tsx`: "does not render aria-orientation on the listbox role")
- Given `<Combobox.Root grid defaultOpen>` with two `<Combobox.Row>`s of three `<Combobox.Item>`s each, then the list has `role="grid"` and there are 6 elements with `role="gridcell"`. (base-ui: `packages/react/src/combobox/root/ComboboxRoot.test.tsx`: "prop: grid > sets grid roles when grid is enabled and rows are used")
- Given `<Combobox.Root grid defaultOpen>` with one row of two items, then the `grid` element has no `aria-orientation` attribute (the `grid` role disallows it per axe `aria-allowed-attr`). (base-ui: `packages/react/src/combobox/root/ComboboxRoot.test.tsx`: "prop: grid > does not render aria-orientation on the grid role")
- Given `<Combobox.Root grid defaultOpen>` with a `<Combobox.Group>` containing a `<Combobox.GroupLabel>Fruits</Combobox.GroupLabel>` and a row, then no element has `role="group"` and the group renders as `role="rowgroup"` with accessible name `Fruits`. (base-ui: `packages/react/src/combobox/root/ComboboxRoot.test.tsx`: "prop: grid > renders groups with the rowgroup role")
- Given a `<Field.Root disabled>` wrapping a `<Combobox.Root>` with an input and trigger, when it renders, then both the input and the trigger have the `disabled` attribute. (base-ui: `packages/react/src/combobox/root/ComboboxRoot.test.tsx`: "Field > should receive disabled prop from Field.Root")
- Given a `<Field.Root name="field-combobox">` wrapping a `<Combobox.Root>`, when it renders, then the hidden textbox carries `name="field-combobox"`. (base-ui: `packages/react/src/combobox/root/ComboboxRoot.test.tsx`: "Field > should receive name prop from Field.Root")
- Given a `<Field.Root>` with `<Field.Label>Search</Field.Label>` and a `<Combobox.Root>` whose `<Combobox.Trigger id="x-id">` is outside the popup and whose input is inside it, when it renders, then the trigger keeps `id="x-id"` and gets `aria-labelledby` equal to the label's id. (base-ui: `packages/react/src/combobox/root/ComboboxRoot.test.tsx`: "Field > Field.Label links to Combobox.Trigger when input is inside popup and trigger has an explicit id")
- Given a `<Field.Root invalid>` with `<Field.Description>` and `<Field.Error match>` and a combobox whose input is inside the popup, when it renders, then the trigger has `aria-invalid="true"` and an `aria-describedby` containing both the description and error ids; after opening, the popup input has none of `aria-invalid`, `aria-describedby`, `data-valid`, `data-invalid`, `data-touched`, `data-dirty`, `data-filled` or `data-focused`. (base-ui: `packages/react/src/combobox/root/ComboboxRoot.test.tsx`: "Field > does not apply validation ARIA attributes to input inside popup")
- Given a `<Combobox.Root>` with `<Combobox.Label>Search</Combobox.Label>`, a `<Combobox.Trigger id="x-id">` and the input inside the popup, when it renders, then the trigger keeps `id="x-id"` and gets `aria-labelledby` equal to the label's id. (base-ui: `packages/react/src/combobox/root/ComboboxRoot.test.tsx`: "Field > Combobox.Label links to Combobox.Trigger when input is inside popup and trigger has an explicit id")
- Given a `<Field.Root>` wrapping a combobox with an input and trigger and items "" / "1", when `focus` then `blur` are fired on the input, then both the input and the trigger gain `data-touched=""`. (base-ui: `packages/react/src/combobox/root/ComboboxRoot.test.tsx`: "Field > [data-touched]")
- Given a `<Field.Root>` wrapping a combobox (fake timers with `shouldAdvanceTime`), when the user clicks the input, the clock advances 200ms, and `ArrowDown` plus a click select "Option 1", then both the input and the trigger gain `data-dirty=""` (neither had it initially). (base-ui: `packages/react/src/combobox/root/ComboboxRoot.test.tsx`: "Field > [data-dirty]")
- Given a `<Field.Root>` wrapping `<Combobox.Root multiple defaultOpen defaultValue={['a']}>`, when the user clicks option "b" (both input and trigger gain `data-dirty=""`) and clicks "b" again to return to `['a']`, then `data-dirty` is removed from both. (base-ui: `packages/react/src/combobox/root/ComboboxRoot.test.tsx`: "Field > removes [data-dirty] in multiple mode after returning to the initial value")
- Given a `<Field.Root>` wrapping `<Combobox.Root multiple defaultOpen items defaultValue={[{id:'a',label:'a'}]} isItemEqualToValue={(item, value) => item.id === value.id}>` where the default value is a different object reference than the rendered item, when the user deselects "a" (trigger gains `data-dirty=""`) and reselects it, then `data-dirty` is removed — the dirty check uses the comparator, not reference identity. ### Keyboard

- Given `<Combobox.Root items={['Apple','Banana','Cherry']}>` with `<Combobox.Trigger><Combobox.Value placeholder="Select a fruit" /></Combobox.Trigger>` and the `<Combobox.Input />` inside the popup, when the trigger is clicked, `ban` is typed, then `ArrowDown` and `Enter` are pressed, then the `dialog` popup unmounts, focus returns to the trigger, the trigger reads `Banana`, and reopening shows an empty input with the `Banana` option `aria-selected="true"` and carrying `data-highlighted`. (base-ui: `packages/react/src/combobox/root/ComboboxRoot.test.tsx`: "input inside popup composition > selects with the keyboard, restores focus, and resets the query on reopen")
- Given an input-inside-popup combobox with `defaultValue="Apple"` and an `onValueChange` spy, when the trigger is clicked, `ban` is typed and `Escape` is pressed, then the popup closes, focus returns to the trigger, the trigger still reads `Apple`, `onValueChange` is never called, and reopening shows an empty input with `Apple` still `aria-selected="true"` and `Banana` present again. (base-ui: `packages/react/src/combobox/root/ComboboxRoot.test.tsx`: "input inside popup composition > discards an uncommitted query on Escape and preserves the selection")
- Given `<Combobox.Root defaultOpen>` whose popup also renders a `ReactDOM.createPortal` button into `document.body`, when that portalled button is focused and `ArrowDown` is dispatched on it, then the store's `activeIndex` stays `null` (no list navigation). (base-ui: `packages/react/src/combobox/root/ComboboxRoot.test.tsx`: "does not navigate the list with arrow keys from portalled controls inside the popup")
- Given `MultiplePopupCombobox` (`multiple`, items `['apple','banana','cherry']`, trigger outside and input inside the popup) with `defaultValue={['banana','cherry']}`, when `Tab` focuses the trigger and `ArrowDown` opens the popup, then `banana` gets `data-highlighted` and `cherry` does not. (base-ui: `packages/react/src/combobox/root/ComboboxRoot.test.tsx`: "selection behavior > multiple > anchors to the first selected item when opened with the keyboard")
- Given the same multiple combobox with `defaultValue={['banana','cherry']}` opened by trigger click and the input focused, when `ArrowDown` is pressed, then `cherry` (the item after the anchor, not `apple` at the top) becomes `data-highlighted`, and `ArrowUp` returns the highlight to `banana`. (base-ui: `packages/react/src/combobox/root/ComboboxRoot.test.tsx`: "selection behavior > multiple > continues arrow navigation from the anchor rather than the top of the list")
- Given `MultiplePopupCombobox` with default value `['apple','banana']`, when the popup is opened, `cherry` is typed so `apple` is filtered out, `ArrowDown` highlights `cherry` and `Enter` toggles it, then the input clears to `''` and `cherry` keeps `data-highlighted` while `apple` does not. (base-ui: `packages/react/src/combobox/root/ComboboxRoot.test.tsx`: "selection behavior > multiple > keeps the toggled item highlighted when selecting with the keyboard while filtering")
- Given `<Combobox.Root>` with directly rendered `apple`/`banana`/`cherry` items and the input outside the popup, when the input is focused and `ArrowDown` is pressed, then `aria-activedescendant` points at `apple`; after `Escape` closes the popup, `ArrowUp` reopens it with `aria-activedescendant` on `cherry`. (base-ui: `packages/react/src/combobox/root/ComboboxRoot.test.tsx`: "keyboard interaction > focuses first item on ArrowDown and last item on ArrowUp")
- Given `<Combobox.Root items={['apple','banana','cherry']}>`, when the input is clicked to open, `ArrowDown` highlights the first item and `Enter` is pressed, then the `listbox` unmounts and the input value is `apple`. (base-ui: `packages/react/src/combobox/root/ComboboxRoot.test.tsx`: "keyboard interaction > opens, navigates with ArrowDown, and Enter selects")
- Given `<Combobox.Root items={['apple','banana','cherry']}>` whose list render function passes an explicit `index` prop to each `<Combobox.Item>`, when the input is clicked, `c` typed to filter to `cherry`, then `ArrowDown` and `Enter` pressed, then the input value becomes `cherry`. - Given `<Combobox.Root defaultOpen items={['a','b']}>`, when `Escape` is pressed with nothing highlighted, then the `listbox` unmounts and the input value stays `''`. ### Pointer

- Given a `<Combobox.Root defaultOpen>` (single mode) with items "a"/"b"/"c" and an input outside the popup, when the user clicks the option "b", then the listbox unmounts, the input value becomes `"b"`, and clicking the input again reopens the listbox with the option "b" carrying `aria-selected="true"`. (base-ui: `packages/react/src/combobox/root/ComboboxRoot.test.tsx`: "prop: multiple > \"single\" selects and closes, then reopens with selection focused")
- Given a `<Combobox.Root multiple defaultOpen>` whose `onInputValueChange` cancels any change with `details.isItemPress`, when the user types "app", hovers "apple" with `mouseMove` to highlight it, then fires `mouseUp` on it with `button: 0` (a drag-select release, no preceding mousedown on the item), then the selection commits on mouseup: the item gets `aria-selected="true"`, the input keeps `"app"`, and the last `onInputValueChange` details carry `isItemPress: true`.
