### Dismissal and layering

- Given `<Combobox.Root items={['apple','banana']}>` with `<Combobox.InputGroup>` wrapping the input and trigger outside the popup, when the input is clicked to open the `listbox`, then the input keeps focus and the input group is not given `aria-hidden="true"`. (base-ui: `packages/react/src/combobox/root/ComboboxRoot.test.tsx`: "does not aria-hide the input group when the input is outside the popup")
- Given a combobox whose input and trigger sit inside a plain `<div>` alongside a `<span data-testid="pad">padding</span>`, when the popup is opened from the trigger and the padding span is clicked, then the `listbox` closes (the plain wrapper is treated as outside). (base-ui: `packages/react/src/combobox/root/ComboboxRoot.test.tsx`: "dismisses the popup when clicking a plain wrapper around the input")
- Given `<Combobox.Root defaultOpen>` whose popup renders `ReactDOM.createPortal(<div>Portalled content</div>, document.body)`, when that portalled content is clicked, then the `listbox` stays open. (base-ui: `packages/react/src/combobox/root/ComboboxRoot.test.tsx`: "does not dismiss when pressing portalled content inside the popup but outside the list")
- Given `<Combobox.Root defaultOpen>` whose popup contains a nested `<Popover.Root>`, when the nested popover is opened and its `Nested focusable content` button is clicked, then the combobox `listbox` stays open. (base-ui: `packages/react/src/combobox/root/ComboboxRoot.test.tsx`: "does not dismiss when pressing content inside a nested popover")
- Given an outside `<button data-testid="outside">` and a combobox with the input outside the popup, when the input is clicked to open the `listbox`, then both the outside button and `<Combobox.Trigger>` end up inert, i.e. they or an ancestor carry `aria-hidden="true"`, `inert`, or `data-base-ui-inert`. (base-ui: `packages/react/src/combobox/root/ComboboxRoot.test.tsx`: "hides the trigger when popup is open with input outside the popup")
- Given a closed `<Combobox.Root items={['Apple','Banana']}>` with the input outside the popup, then no `button` named `Dismiss` is rendered. (base-ui: `packages/react/src/combobox/root/ComboboxRoot.test.tsx`: "does not render the start dismiss button while closed")
- Given `<Combobox.Root defaultOpen modal items={['Apple','Banana']}>` with the input inside the popup and an outside button, then two `Dismiss` buttons exist, the first is `input.previousElementSibling`, the second is `popup.nextElementSibling`, neither has a `tabindex` attribute, the outside button becomes inert, and clicking the end `Dismiss` button closes the `listbox`. (base-ui: `packages/react/src/combobox/root/ComboboxRoot.test.tsx`: "renders internal dismiss buttons before the input and after the popup")
- Given a combobox with the input outside the popup, when the input is clicked to open, then the start `Dismiss` button is `input.previousElementSibling`, the end one is `popup.nextElementSibling`, neither has `tabindex`, and clicking the start `Dismiss` button closes the `listbox`. (base-ui: `packages/react/src/combobox/root/ComboboxRoot.test.tsx`: "renders an internal dismiss button for the input-outside-popup pattern")
- Given `<Combobox.Root inline defaultOpen>` with an inline `<Combobox.List>` (no Positioner/Popup) inside a wrapper `<div onKeyDown>`, when the input is clicked and `Escape` pressed, then the outer `keydown` handler fires once (Escape is allowed to bubble). (base-ui: `packages/react/src/combobox/root/ComboboxRoot.test.tsx`: "keyboard interaction > bubbles Escape key when rendered inline without Positioner/Popup")
- Given `<Combobox.Root defaultOpen items={[]}>` with the positioner manually set to `display: none` and no `<Combobox.Empty>`, when the input is clicked and `Escape` pressed, then the wrapping `div`'s `keydown` handler fires once. (base-ui: `packages/react/src/combobox/root/ComboboxRoot.test.tsx`: "keyboard interaction > bubbles Escape key when list is empty and popup hidden with CSS")
- Given the same empty-list combobox but with `<Combobox.Empty>No results.</Combobox.Empty>` inside the popup and the positioner hidden via `display: none`, when `Escape` is pressed, then the outer `keydown` handler is never called (Escape is consumed). - Given `<Combobox.Root modal items={['Apple']}>` whose `<Combobox.Positioner>` is styled `width: calc(100vw - 10px)`, when the trigger receives `pointerdown` with `pointerType: 'touch'` followed by `mousedown` and the `listbox` opens, then the page is scroll-locked (`documentElement.style.overflow === 'hidden'`, or `data-base-ui-scroll-locked` on `documentElement`, or `body.style.overflow === 'hidden'`). - Given a `<Combobox.Root defaultOpen items={['apple']}>`, when the user types "a", clears the input and presses `Escape`, then the listbox unmounts. (base-ui: `packages/react/src/combobox/root/ComboboxRoot.test.tsx`: "coverage edge cases > handles closing after a changed query is cleared")

- Given `<Combobox.Root items={['apple','banana']} multiple defaultValue={['apple']}>` with a trigger, an input, a chip with `<Combobox.ChipRemove>`, and a popup, when the trigger is clicked to open the listbox and the remove button is then clicked, then the listbox is still present and the input has focus. ### Positioning

- Given `<Combobox.Root items={['apple']}>` with `<Combobox.Positioner side="right">`, then the closed trigger has no `data-popup-side`; when it is clicked open the trigger gains `data-popup-side="right"`, and after an outside click closes the popup the attribute is removed again. (base-ui: `packages/react/src/combobox/trigger/ComboboxTrigger.test.tsx`: "data state attributes > sets data-popup-side to the current popup side") (browser-mode only)
- Given `<Combobox.Root items={['apple']}>` with `<Combobox.Positioner side="right">`, then the closed input has no `data-popup-side`; clicking it open sets `data-popup-side="right"`, and an outside click that closes the popup removes the attribute. (base-ui: `packages/react/src/combobox/input/ComboboxInput.test.tsx`: "data state attributes > sets data-popup-side to the current popup side") (browser-mode only)
- Given `<Combobox.Root open items={[40 items]}>` anchored by a wrapper at `position: fixed; bottom: 120px; left: 100px` with `<Combobox.Positioner side="bottom" sideOffset={0}>` and a `<Combobox.List style={{ maxHeight: 'min(80px, var(--available-height))', overflowY: 'auto' }}>` of 30px items, when positioned, then the positioner keeps `data-side="bottom"` — `--available-height` must be seeded before `size()` runs so `min(80px, var(--available-height))` is valid on the first `flip()` pass (regression for mui/base-ui#5118). (base-ui: `packages/react/src/combobox/positioner/ComboboxPositioner.test.tsx`: "keeps the popup on the preferred side when its capped height fits below tall content") (browser-mode only)
- Given `<Combobox.Root open>` with a 120px-wide `<Combobox.Input>` and a 240px-wide `<Combobox.Trigger>` but no `<Combobox.InputGroup>`, when the positioner's `sideOffset` callback reads `data.anchor.width`, then it equals the input's measured width, not the trigger width. (base-ui: `packages/react/src/combobox/positioner/ComboboxPositioner.test.tsx`: "default anchor > uses the input when input group is absent") (browser-mode only)
- Given `<Combobox.Root open>` with a 240px-wide `<Combobox.InputGroup>` wrapping a 120px-wide `<Combobox.Input>` and a trigger, when the positioner's `sideOffset` callback reads `data.anchor.width`, then it equals 240 (the input group is the default anchor). (base-ui: `packages/react/src/combobox/positioner/ComboboxPositioner.test.tsx`: "default anchor > uses the input group when present") (browser-mode only)

### Animation and presence

- Given `<Combobox.Root items={['Apple','Banana']} defaultValue="Banana">` with the input inside a popup animated by a 100ms `data-ending-style` close keyframe and `BASE_UI_ANIMATIONS_DISABLED = false`, when `banana` is typed, `Escape` closes the popup, and the trigger is clicked again while `data-ending-style` is still applied, then the close animation is cancelled (`data-ending-style` removed), `selectedIndex` is restored to `1`, the input value is `''`, `Apple` is rendered again, and `Banana` gets `data-highlighted` with the input's `aria-activedescendant` pointing at its id. (browser-mode only) (base-ui: `packages/react/src/combobox/root/ComboboxRoot.test.tsx`: "input inside popup composition > clears a single-select query and restores the selection when reopening during the close animation")
- Given the same 100ms `data-ending-style` close animation on `<Combobox.Root items={['Apple','Banana']}>` with no selection, when `ap` is typed, `Escape` closes the popup, and `b` is typed into the still-animating input, then the popup reopens, the input value is `apb`, the `<Combobox.Empty>` region with `role="status"` reads `No matches`, and no `option` is rendered. (browser-mode only) (base-ui: `packages/react/src/combobox/root/ComboboxRoot.test.tsx`: "input inside popup composition > preserves a typed query when input reopens single-select during the close animation")
- Given a controlled-`open`, controlled-`inputValue` combobox with `items={['apple','apricot','banana']}`, a 400ms `data-ending-style` close animation, and an `onInputValueChange` that calls `eventDetails.cancel()` when `reason === REASONS.inputClear`, when `ap` is typed, `apple` is clicked (closing), and the external `Open` button reopens the popup mid-`data-ending-style`, then the input reads `apple` and all 3 options are shown. - Given a combobox with the input outside the popup, a 400ms close animation, and a `refetch` button that replaces the `items` array identity, when `app` is typed, `Escape` closes the popup, and the trigger reopens it mid-animation, then the input still reads `app`, and it still reads `app` after `refetch` produces a new `items` identity. - Given `<Combobox.Root items={['apple','apricot','banana']} defaultValue="apple">` with the input outside the popup and a 400ms close animation, when the input is clicked, `Backspace` narrows the list to 1 option, `Escape` starts the close, and typing `e` reopens the popup, then the input reads `apple` again and exactly 1 option is shown (the keystroke's query-changed flag survives the reopen). - Given `<Combobox.Root items defaultValue="apple">` whose `onInputValueChange` synchronously replaces the `items` array, with a 400ms close animation, when the input is emptied with five `Backspace` presses, `Escape` starts the close, and `a` is typed mid-animation, then the input reads `a` (the items resync does not undo the keystroke). - Given `<Combobox.Root items={Combobox.createItems(['Isparta', 'İzmir'], ...)} locale="tr" defaultOpen>`, when `i` is typed, then Turkish collation applies: `Isparta` is filtered out and `İzmir` remains an `option`. (base-ui: `packages/react/src/combobox/items/createItems.test.tsx`: "uses the root locale for filtering")
- Given `@base-ui/utils/platform` mocked so `platform.engine.gecko` is `true` and `<DirectionProvider direction="rtl">` wrapping `<Combobox.Root defaultInputValue="apple">` with a `<Combobox.Input />`, when the focused input receives `Home` then `End`, then Firefox/Gecko's inverted RTL caret behavior is honored: `Home` puts `selectionStart` at the value length and `End` puts it at `0`. Browser-quirk file `ComboboxInput.gecko.test.tsx`. (base-ui: `packages/react/src/combobox/input/ComboboxInput.gecko.test.tsx`: "uses Gecko RTL caret positions for Home and End")
- Given `<DirectionProvider direction="rtl">` wrapping `<Combobox.Root multiple defaultValue={['apple','banana']}>` with chips "apple"/"banana" then the input inside `<Combobox.Chips>`, when the input is focused with caret at 0 and ArrowRight is pressed repeatedly, focus moves banana -> apple -> input; and from the "apple" chip ArrowLeft moves focus to "banana" then to the input (directions are mirrored). (base-ui: `packages/react/src/combobox/chip/ComboboxChip.test.tsx`: "interaction behavior > mirrors chip keyboard navigation in RTL mode")

- Given `<Combobox.Root>` with `<Combobox.Input />` and a portalled positioner rendered with `renderToString`, then the input has `role="combobox"`, `aria-expanded="false"`, `aria-autocomplete="list"` and `aria-haspopup="listbox"` before hydration. (base-ui: `packages/react/src/combobox/root/ComboboxRoot.test.tsx`: "server-side rendering > sets combobox aria attributes on the input")
- Given `<Combobox.Root>` with only `<Combobox.Trigger />` (input inside popup pattern) rendered with `renderToString`, then the trigger has `role="combobox"`, `aria-expanded="false"` and `aria-haspopup="dialog"`. (base-ui: `packages/react/src/combobox/root/ComboboxRoot.test.tsx`: "server-side rendering > sets combobox aria attributes on the trigger when input is inside popup")
- Given `<Combobox.Root inline>` with `<Combobox.Label>`, `<Combobox.Trigger>` and `<Combobox.Input>` rendered with `renderToString`, then both label and trigger get non-empty `id`s but the trigger has no `aria-labelledby` until hydration. (base-ui: `packages/react/src/combobox/root/ComboboxRoot.test.tsx`: "server-side rendering > does not link Combobox.Label to trigger before hydration")
- Given a server render (`renderToString`) of `<Combobox.Root items={sharedPersonItems} filteredItems={[{ id: 'user-1', name: 'Alice' }]} defaultValue="user-1">` with `<Combobox.Input>`, then the serialized input value is `Alice`, so a `defaultValue` label resolves from the external window during SSR. (base-ui: `packages/react/src/combobox/items/createItems.test.tsx`: "resolves a server-rendered defaultValue label from the external window")
- Given `<Autocomplete.Root items={['alpha','beta']} name="search">` with `<Autocomplete.Input>` outside the popup, when server-rendered via `renderToString` and then hydrated, then in both phases the input has `role="combobox"` and is the single `[name="search"]` control (form-value ownership survives hydration). - Given `<Combobox.Root defaultOpen>` with `<Combobox.Status>Searching…</Combobox.Status>` under fake timers, when rendered the status element is the `role="status"` node with text `'Searching…⁠'`, and after advancing 200ms (`INITIAL_LIVE_REGION_TEXT_MUTATION_RESET_DELAY`) the text is `'Searching…'`. - Given `<Combobox.Root defaultOpen>` with an empty `<Combobox.Status>` (the `role="status"` node, text `''`) under fake timers, when it is rerendered with children "Searching…", then the live region immediately shows "Searching…". - Given `<Combobox.Status render={<p data-testid="custom-status" />}>Searching…</Combobox.Status>` in an open root under fake timers, when rendered the visible element is a `P` that is itself the `role="status"` node with text `'Searching…⁠'`, and after 200ms the text is `'Searching…'`. - Given `<Combobox.Root defaultOpen>` with `<Combobox.Status>Searching…</Combobox.Status>` under fake timers whose text is `'Searching…⁠'`, when the tree unmounts during the 200ms reset delay, then the detached node's text is restored to `'Searching…'`. - Given `<Combobox.Root items={[]} defaultOpen>`, when it is re-rendered with `items={undefined}`, then no infinite re-render loop occurs and the `combobox` element is still present. - Given `<Combobox.Root items={['apple','banana','cherry']} defaultValue="apple">`, when `apple` is selected so the input value equals the selection and the popup is reopened, then all three items are shown rather than only those matching the query. (base-ui: `packages/react/src/combobox/root/ComboboxRoot.test.tsx`: "selection behavior > single > should show all items when query matches current selection")
- Given a `<Combobox.Root items>` with 50 items ("alpha-0".."alpha-24", "beta-0".."beta-24") and `<Combobox.List style={{ maxHeight: 100, overflowY: 'auto' }}>`, when the list is opened, scrolled to `scrollTop = 40`, and the user types "b" to change the query, then the list `scrollTop` returns to `0`. (base-ui: `packages/react/src/combobox/root/ComboboxRoot.test.tsx`: "scroll reset on input value change > resets the list scroll position to the top when the query changes") (browser-mode only)

- Given `<Progress.Root min={5} max={5} value={5}>` (a zero-width range), when rendered, then `aria-valuenow="5"`, `aria-valuetext` is the 0% format, the value text matches and the indicator width is `"0%"` — no division-by-zero artifacts. ### Notes and edge cases

- Given an avatar with `Avatar.Image src="/test.png"` and spies on `Image.prototype.addEventListener`/`removeEventListener`, when the avatar is mounted and unmounted, then the number of `addEventListener` calls equals the number of `removeEventListener` calls — no leaked image listeners. (radix: `packages/react/avatar/src/avatar.test.tsx`: "given an Avatar with multiple images (development) > warns that multiple images are not supported")
- Given `NODE_ENV="development"` and an `Avatar.Root` containing exactly one `Avatar.Image`, then `console.warn` is never called. (radix: `packages/react/avatar/src/avatar.test.tsx`: "given an Avatar with multiple images (development) > does not warn for a single image")
- Given `<Avatar.Root>` with `ref`, `data-testid="root"`, `className="custom-class"`, `style={{ outlineColor: 'rgb(1, 2, 3)' }}` and `onClick`, then the rendered element keeps the class and inline `outlineColor`, the ref points at it, and a click calls `onClick`. (radix: `packages/react/avatar/src/avatar.test.tsx`: "Avatar.Image > spreads props it does not consume onto the element it renders")
- Given `<Avatar.Image src="/avatar.png" asChild>` wrapping an `<img alt="Avatar" />`, then the rendered element is `IMG` with `src="/avatar.png"`, keeps `custom-class` and inline `outlineColor`, receives the ref, and forwards `onClick`. - Given `<Avatar.Fallback>` with `ref`, `data-testid`, `className`, `style` and `onClick`, then the rendered element keeps the class and inline `outlineColor`, the ref points at it, and a click calls `onClick`. - Given `<Avatar.Fallback asChild>` wrapping an `<article>AB</article>`, then the rendered element is `ARTICLE`, keeps `custom-class` and inline `outlineColor`, receives the ref, and forwards `onClick`. - Given `<Avatar.Image keepMounted render={(props) => <img sizes src srcSet {...props} />} />` where the author's source props come BEFORE the spread, when rendered, then the author's `sizes`, `src` and `srcset` survive — the library does not override source props supplied through a render callback. ### Notes and edge cases

## scroll-area

### Roles and attributes

- Given `<ScrollArea.Viewport data-testid="viewport">Content</ScrollArea.Viewport>` inside `<ScrollArea.Root type="always">`, then the viewport's first element child is an implicit `HTMLDivElement` wrapper styled `display: table; min-width: 100%` and holding the text "Content". (radix: `packages/react/scroll-area/src/scroll-area.test.tsx`: "ScrollArea.Viewport > renders an implicit content element around its children by default")
- Given `<ScrollArea.Viewport disableImplicitContentElement>` wrapping a `<span data-testid="child">`, then the viewport's first element child is that span itself and it does not get `display: table` — no implicit wrapper is inserted. (radix: `packages/react/scroll-area/src/scroll-area.test.tsx`: "ScrollArea.Viewport > skips the implicit content element when `disableImplicitContentElement` is set")
- Given the `scrollarea--cypress` story where both scrollbars overflow, then the root's computed `--radix-scroll-area-corner-width` and `--radix-scroll-area-corner-height` are both `8px`; when the "toggle-horizontal-overflow" control removes the horizontal overflow so that scrollbar goes away, then both variables reset to `0px` so the remaining vertical scrollbar leaves no gap at the bottom — regression for issue #2383. (radix: `e2e/scroll-area.spec.ts`: "ScrollArea > given both scrollbars were visible and one becomes hidden > resets the corner size CSS variables back to zero")
- Given `<ScrollArea.Root data-testid="root" style={{ width: 200, height: 200 }}>` around a `<ScrollArea.Viewport>` holding a 1000x1000 child, with fake timers, when `pointerEnter` then `scroll` (`scrollTop: 1`) fire on the viewport, then the root gains `data-scrolling=""`, and after `SCROLL_TIMEOUT` (500ms) ticks it is removed; repeating with `scrollLeft: 1` adds and then removes `data-scrolling=""` the same way. (base-ui: `packages/react/src/scroll-area/root/ScrollAreaRoot.test.tsx`: "data-scrolling attribute > adds [data-scrolling] attribute when viewport is scrolled")
- Given a `<ScrollArea.Root>` (200x200 viewport, 1000x1000 content) inside a `display: none` wrapper with a vertical `<ScrollArea.Scrollbar style={{ display: 'flex' }}>` and `<ScrollArea.Thumb style={{ paddingBlock: 8 }} />`, when a "show" button flips the wrapper to `display: block`, then the thumb's `--scroll-area-thumb-height` is recomputed to something other than `'0px'` without any scroll happening. (base-ui: `packages/react/src/scroll-area/root/ScrollAreaRoot.test.tsx`: "sizing > recomputes thumb size when becoming visible without requiring scroll") (browser-mode only)
- Given a `<ScrollArea.Root>` (200x200) with both vertical (`width: 11`) and horizontal (`height: 13`) scrollbars plus `<ScrollArea.Corner data-testid="corner" />` and a mocked `ResizeObserver`, when content is 100x100 (non-overflowing) the corner is not rendered at all, and after rerendering with 1000x1000 content and firing the resize observer callback, then the corner renders with inline `style.width === '11px'` and `style.height === '13px'`. (base-ui: `packages/react/src/scroll-area/root/ScrollAreaRoot.test.tsx`: "sizing > recomputes corner size when content starts overflowing") (browser-mode only)
- Given a `<ScrollArea.Root>` (200x200) with 1000x1000 content, two `keepMounted` scrollbars (`width: 10` / `height: 10`), a `<ScrollArea.Corner>` and a mocked `ResizeObserver`, then the root initially has `data-has-overflow-x` and `data-has-overflow-y`, the corner exists, and the viewport's inline `--scroll-area-overflow-x-end` / `--scroll-area-overflow-y-end` are non-`'0px'`; when a "shrink" button drops content to 100x100 and the resize observer fires, then both `data-has-overflow-*` attributes are removed, the corner unmounts, and `--scroll-area-overflow-x-start`, `--scroll-area-overflow-x-end`, `--scroll-area-overflow-y-start` and `--scroll-area-overflow-y-end` are all `'0px'`. (base-ui: `packages/react/src/scroll-area/root/ScrollAreaRoot.test.tsx`: "sizing > clears corner, overflow attributes, and metrics when content stops overflowing") (browser-mode only)
- Given a 200x200 `<ScrollArea.Root>` with 1000x1000 content and vertical plus horizontal scrollbars each containing a thumb, when measured, then the vertical thumb's `--scroll-area-thumb-height` and the horizontal thumb's `--scroll-area-thumb-width` both equal `(200 / 1000) * 200` px, i.e. `40px`. (base-ui: `packages/react/src/scroll-area/root/ScrollAreaRoot.test.tsx`: "sizing > should correctly set thumb height and width based on scrollable content") (browser-mode only)
- Given a 200x200 `<ScrollArea.Root>` with 1000x1000 content and overlay scrollbars sized `width: 10` / `height: 10`, when rendered, then the viewport's first child (the content wrapper) has computed `padding-left`, `padding-right` and `padding-bottom` all `'0px'`, so overlay scrollbars add no padding. - Given a 200x200 `<ScrollArea.Root>` with 1000x1000 content, a vertical scrollbar with `paddingBlock: 8` and a horizontal scrollbar with `paddingInline: 8`, when measured, then each thumb's `--scroll-area-thumb-height` / `--scroll-area-thumb-width` equals `(200 - 8 * 2) * (200 / 1000)` px, so scrollbar padding shrinks the track used for thumb sizing. (base-ui: `packages/react/src/scroll-area/scrollbar/ScrollAreaScrollbar.test.tsx`: "track click by axis > scrolls into the negative RTL range when clicking a horizontal RTL track") (browser-mode only)
- Given an RTL 200x200 scroll area with viewport metrics mocked to `clientWidth` 200 / `scrollWidth` 1000 at `scrollLeft: 0` and a horizontal `keepMounted` scrollbar, when a `wheel` with `deltaX: -50` fires on the scrollbar, then `viewport.scrollLeft` becomes `-50`. (base-ui: `packages/react/src/scroll-area/scrollbar/ScrollAreaScrollbar.test.tsx`: "wheel > allows horizontal scrolling away from the RTL start edge")
- Given the same RTL mocked setup, when a `wheel` with `deltaX: 50` fires at `scrollLeft: 0`, then it stays `0`; from `-100` a `deltaX: 50` moves it to `-50`; from `-790` a `deltaX: -50` clamps to `-800` and a further `deltaX: -50` leaves it at `-800`; from `-10` a `deltaX: 50` clamps back to `0`. - Given `<ScrollArea.Root ref>` wrapping a `Viewport disableImplicitContentElement` and a `Content`, when the tree re-renders, then the composed ref on the root stays stable (shared `assertStableComposedRef` helper) — regression for issue #3963. - Given `<ScrollArea.Root type="always">` with a `<ScrollArea.Scrollbar orientation="vertical" ref>` containing a `Thumb`, when the tree re-renders, then the composed ref on the scrollbar stays stable. (radix: `packages/react/scroll-area/src/scroll-area.test.tsx`: "ScrollArea ref stability > keeps a stable composed ref on the scrollbar")
- Given `<ScrollArea.Root type="always">` with `ref`, `data-testid="root"`, `className="custom-class"`, `style={{ outlineColor: 'rgb(1, 2, 3)' }}` and `onClick`, then the rendered element keeps the class and inline `outlineColor`, the ref points at it, and a click calls `onClick`. ## toolbar

### Roles and attributes

- Given `<Toolbar.Root asChild>` wrapping an `<article>` containing a `Toolbar.Button`, when rendered, then the element is an `ARTICLE` with `role="toolbar"` and `aria-orientation="horizontal"`, keeps `className="custom-class"` and the inline `outlineColor: rgb(1, 2, 3)`, the ref resolves to it, and clicking fires the author `onClick`. (radix: `packages/react/toolbar/src/toolbar.test.tsx`: "Toolbar.Root > forwards props to the child element when `asChild` is set")
- Given `<Toolbar.Separator asChild>` wrapping an `<article />` inside a default horizontal `Toolbar.Root`, when rendered, then the element is an `ARTICLE` with `role="separator"` and `data-orientation="vertical"`, since a separator in a horizontal toolbar is itself vertical; it keeps the className and inline `outlineColor`, the ref resolves to it, and clicking fires the author `onClick`. (radix: `packages/react/toolbar/src/toolbar.test.tsx`: "Toolbar.Separator > forwards props to the child element when `asChild` is set")
- Given `<Toolbar.Button asChild>` wrapping `<button type="button">` inside `Toolbar.Root`, when rendered, then the element is a `BUTTON` carrying `data-orientation="horizontal"` contributed by the enclosing `RovingFocusGroup.Item`, keeps the className and inline `outlineColor`, the ref resolves to it, and clicking fires the author `onClick`. (radix: `packages/react/toolbar/src/toolbar.test.tsx`: "Toolbar.Button > forwards props to the child element when `asChild` is set")
- Given `<Toolbar.Link asChild>` wrapping `<a href="/">` inside `Toolbar.Root`, when rendered, then the element is an `A` carrying `data-orientation="horizontal"` from the enclosing `RovingFocusGroup.Item`, keeps the className and inline `outlineColor`, the ref resolves to it, and clicking fires the author `onClick`. (radix: `packages/react/toolbar/src/toolbar.test.tsx`: "Toolbar.Link > forwards props to the child element when `asChild` is set")
- Given `<Toolbar.ToggleGroup type="single" asChild>` wrapping an `<article>` with one toggle item, when rendered, then the element is an `ARTICLE` with `role="radiogroup"` and `data-orientation="horizontal"`, keeps the className and inline `outlineColor`, the ref resolves to it, and clicking fires the author `onClick`. (radix: `packages/react/toolbar/src/toolbar.test.tsx`: "Toolbar.ToggleGroup > forwards props to the child element when `asChild` is set")
- Given `<Toolbar.ToggleItem value="one" asChild>` wrapping `<button type="button">` inside `<Toolbar.ToggleGroup type="single">` with nothing selected, when rendered, then the element is a `BUTTON` with `role="radio"`, `aria-checked="false"` and `data-state="off"`, keeps the className and inline `outlineColor`, the ref resolves to it, and clicking fires the author `onClick`. (radix: `packages/react/toolbar/src/toolbar.test.tsx`: "Toolbar.ToggleItem > forwards props to the child element when `asChild` is set")
- Given `<Toolbar.Root />`, when rendered, then the root element carries `role="toolbar"`. (base-ui: `packages/react/src/toolbar/root/ToolbarRoot.test.tsx`: "ARIA attributes > has role=\"toolbar\"")
- Given `<Toolbar.Root><Toolbar.Button data-testid="button" /></Toolbar.Root>`, when rendered, then the element with `data-testid="button"` is the same element found by `getByRole('button')`. (base-ui: `packages/react/src/toolbar/button/ToolbarButton.test.tsx`: "ARIA attributes > renders a button")
- Given `<Toolbar.Root><Toolbar.Group data-testid="group" /></Toolbar.Root>`, when rendered, then the element with `data-testid="group"` is the same element found by `getByRole('group')`. (base-ui: `packages/react/src/toolbar/group/ToolbarGroup.test.tsx`: "ARIA attributes > renders a group")
- Given `<Toolbar.Root><Toolbar.Input data-testid="input" /></Toolbar.Root>`, when rendered, then the element with `data-testid="input"` is the same element found by `getByRole('textbox')`. (base-ui: `packages/react/src/toolbar/input/ToolbarInput.test.tsx`: "ARIA attributes > renders a textbox")
- Given `<Toolbar.Root><Toolbar.Link data-testid="link" href="https://base-ui.com" /></Toolbar.Root>`, when rendered, then the element with `data-testid="link"` is the same element found by `getByRole('link')`. (base-ui: `packages/react/src/toolbar/link/ToolbarLink.test.tsx`: "ARIA attributes > renders an anchor")
- Given `<Toolbar.Separator />` inside a `<Toolbar.Root orientation>`, when rendered, then the separator's `aria-orientation` is the perpendicular of the toolbar's: cases `orientation="horizontal"` toolbar produces `aria-orientation="vertical"`, and `orientation="vertical"` toolbar produces `aria-orientation="horizontal"`. (base-ui: `packages/react/src/toolbar/separator/ToolbarSeparator.test.tsx`: "uses a %s separator in a %s toolbar")
- Given `<Toolbar.Root orientation="horizontal"><Toolbar.Separator orientation="horizontal" /></Toolbar.Root>`, when rendered, then the explicit `orientation` prop wins and the separator has `aria-orientation="horizontal"` instead of the derived perpendicular value. (base-ui: `packages/react/src/toolbar/button/ToolbarButton.test.tsx`: "rendering other Base UI components > Menu > renders a menu trigger")
- Given `<Toolbar.Button data-testid="button" render={<Select.Trigger />} />` inside `<Select.Root defaultValue="a">`, when rendered, then the button is the `getByRole('combobox')` element and has `aria-haspopup="listbox"`. - Given `<Toolbar.Button render={<Dialog.Trigger data-testid="trigger" />} />` inside `<Dialog.Root modal={false}>`, when rendered, then the element with `data-testid="trigger"` is the same element found by `getByRole('button')`. - Given `<Toolbar.Button render={<AlertDialog.Trigger data-testid="trigger" />} />` inside `<AlertDialog.Root>`, when rendered, then the element with `data-testid="trigger"` is the same element found by `getByRole('button')`. - Given `<Toolbar.Button render={<Popover.Trigger data-testid="trigger" />} />` inside `<Popover.Root>`, when rendered, then the element with `data-testid="trigger"` is the `getByRole('button')` element and has `aria-haspopup="dialog"`. ### Keyboard

- Given `<Toolbar.Root>` with a `<Toolbar.Link href="#" onClick>` whose children include an `<input>` portaled to `document.body` via `ReactDOM.createPortal`, when the portaled input has focus and `keyDown` `" "` is fired on it, then the link's `onClick` is never called. Regression test for issue 3232. (radix: `packages/react/toolbar/src/toolbar.test.tsx`: "keys from focusable descendants > does not activate a ToolbarLink from Space typed into a portaled focusable descendant")
- Given `<Toolbar.Root>` with a `<Toolbar.Link href="#" onClick>`, when the link itself has focus and `keyDown` `" "` is fired on it, then `onClick` is called exactly once, so Space activates a toolbar link. (radix: `packages/react/toolbar/src/toolbar.test.tsx`: "keys from focusable descendants > still activates the ToolbarLink via Space when the link itself is focused")
- Given `<DirectionProvider direction="ltr">` wrapping `<Toolbar.Root dir="ltr" orientation="horizontal">` containing a `Toolbar.Button`, a `Toolbar.Link`, a `Toolbar.Group` of two buttons and a `Toolbar.Input`, when Tab focuses the first button and `ArrowRight` is pressed repeatedly, then focus advances button1 → link → grouped button1 → grouped button2 → input → wraps back to button1, and `ArrowLeft` walks back input → grouped button2. (base-ui: `packages/react/src/toolbar/root/ToolbarRoot.test.tsx`: "keyboard navigation > ltr > orientation: horizontal") (browser-mode only)
- Given the same toolbar with `orientation="vertical"` under `DirectionProvider direction="ltr"`, when Tab focuses the first button and `ArrowDown` is pressed repeatedly, then focus advances button1 → link → grouped button1 → grouped button2 → input → wraps to button1, and `ArrowUp` walks back input → grouped button2. (base-ui: `packages/react/src/toolbar/root/ToolbarRoot.test.tsx`: "keyboard navigation > ltr > orientation: vertical") (browser-mode only)
- Given the same toolbar with `orientation="horizontal"` under `DirectionProvider direction="rtl"` and `dir="rtl"`, when Tab focuses the first button and `ArrowLeft` is pressed repeatedly, then focus advances forward through button1 → link → grouped button1 → grouped button2 → input → wraps to button1, and `ArrowRight` walks backwards. (base-ui: `packages/react/src/toolbar/root/ToolbarRoot.test.tsx`: "keyboard navigation > rtl > orientation: horizontal") (browser-mode only)
- Given the same toolbar with `orientation="vertical"` under `DirectionProvider direction="rtl"` and `dir="rtl"`, when Tab focuses the first button and `ArrowDown` is pressed repeatedly, then focus advances forward and `ArrowUp` walks backwards, i.e. vertical keys are unaffected by RTL. (base-ui: `packages/react/src/toolbar/root/ToolbarRoot.test.tsx`: "keyboard navigation > rtl > orientation: vertical") (browser-mode only)
- Given `<Toolbar.Root loopFocus={false}>` with two buttons, when Tab focuses the first and `ArrowLeft` is pressed, then focus stays on the first; `ArrowRight` moves to the last and a further `ArrowRight` keeps focus on the last, so navigation does not wrap. (base-ui: `packages/react/src/toolbar/root/ToolbarRoot.test.tsx`: "keyboard navigation > does not wrap focus when loopFocus is false") (browser-mode only)

- Given `<Toolbar.Root>` with a disabled `Toolbar.Button`, a `Toolbar.Group` of two disabled buttons and a disabled `Toolbar.Input`, when Tab focuses the first button and `ArrowRight` is pressed repeatedly, then none of the items carry the native `disabled` attribute and each disabled item can take focus while showing `data-disabled` and `aria-disabled="true"`; wrapping past the input returns `tabindex="0"` to button1, and `ArrowLeft` walks back through input and grouped button2. ## one-time-password-field

### Roles and attributes

- Given `<OneTimePasswordField.Root type="password">` with one input, when `1` is typed, then the visible input's `type` is `"password"` while the sibling `HiddenInput` carries the real value `"1"`. (radix: `packages/react/one-time-password-field/src/one-time-password-field.test.tsx`: "should mask input value when type is password")
- Given `<OneTimePasswordField.Root asChild>` wrapping an `<article>`, when rendered, then the element is an `ARTICLE` that still carries the root's own `role="group"`. (radix: `packages/react/one-time-password-field/src/one-time-password-field.test.tsx`: "OneTimePasswordField.Root > forwards props to the child element when `asChild` is set")
- Given `<OneTimePasswordField.Input asChild>` wrapping an `<input>`, when rendered, then the element is an `INPUT` that carries the part's own attributes plus those contributed by the roving-focus group and collection: `data-radix-otp-input` and `data-radix-index="0"`. - Given `<OTPField.Root length={L} />` for each of `0`, `-1`, `3.7`, `NaN` and `Infinity`, when rendered, then exactly one `console.warn` fires containing "Base UI: <OTPField.Root> `length` must be a positive integer. Received `length={<L>}`." (base-ui: `packages/react/src/otp-field/root/OTPFieldRoot.test.tsx`: "warns when length is not a positive integer (%p)")
- Given the `OTPField.Root` type surface, `length` is a required prop (`<OTPField.Root />` is a type error), `<OTPField.Root length={6} form="verification-form" mask validationType="alphanumeric" normalizeValue={...} onValueChange onValueInvalid onValueComplete />` type-checks, `inputMode` may be combined with `validationType="none"` (`inputMode="numeric"`) or override a built-in type (`validationType="numeric"` with `inputMode="tel"`), and the removed `sanitizeValue` prop is a type error since it was renamed to `normalizeValue`. (base-ui: `packages/react/src/otp-field/root/OTPFieldRoot.spec.tsx`: type-only assertions)
- Given the `onValueChange`/`onValueInvalid`/`onValueComplete` handler types, the first argument is `string` and the details object narrows its `event` by `reason`: `"input-paste"` gives `ClipboardEvent`, `"keyboard"` gives `KeyboardEvent`, `"input-change"` gives `InputEvent | Event`, and `"input-clear"` gives `InputEvent | FocusEvent | Event` (never `KeyboardEvent`); `onValueInvalid` and `onValueComplete` details narrow only `"input-paste"` and `"input-change"`. (base-ui: `packages/react/src/otp-field/root/OTPFieldRoot.spec.tsx`: type-only assertions)
- Given `<OTPField.Input />`, the component accepts no explicit `index` prop (`<OTPField.Input index={0} />` is a type error) because slot order is inferred from render order, and its `render` callback receives native `<input>` props where `props.disabled` and `props.readOnly` are `boolean | undefined`. (base-ui: `packages/react/src/otp-field/input/OTPFieldInput.spec.tsx`: type-only assertions)

- Given `<Presence>` toggled from `present` to `present={false}` and back to `present`, when the final rerender lands, then the button is mounted again. (radix: `packages/react/presence/src/presence.test.tsx`: "mount/unmount behavior > keeps the child mounted when toggling present back to true")
- Given `<Presence present>` whose child is a render function `({ present }) => <button>{present ? 'visible' : 'hidden'}</button>`, when rerendered with `present={false}`, then the button stays in the DOM (the render-function variant force-mounts) and its text switches from "visible" to "hidden". (radix: `packages/react/presence/src/presence.test.tsx`: "render function children > always renders the child when using a render function")
- Given `<Presence present>` with a render-function child, when it is first rendered, then the function receives `present: true`. (radix: `packages/react/presence/src/presence.test.tsx`: "render function children > passes present=true to the render function when present prop is true")
- Given `useAnimationsFinished(ref)` with `BASE_UI_ANIMATIONS_DISABLED = false` and one running animation, when that animation is CANCELED (its `finished` promise rejects) and `getAnimations()` then returns a replacement animation, then the callback is not fired until the replacement animation finishes, at which point it fires exactly once. (base-ui: `packages/react/src/internals/useAnimationsFinished.test.tsx`: "waits for a replacement animation after an animation is canceled")
- Given one running animation that is canceled while `getAnimations()` then returns an empty list, when the cancellation settles, then the callback fires exactly once (no replacement means the wait is over). (base-ui: `packages/react/src/internals/useAnimationsFinished.test.tsx`: "finishes when a canceled animation has no replacement")
- Given two items each using `useAnimationsFinished(ref, false, /* batch */ true)` that unmount themselves on completion, when both animations finish inside the same microtask, then both items unmount and `React.Profiler` records exactly ONE additional commit (the batched callbacks coalesce into a single render). (base-ui: `packages/react/src/internals/useAnimationsFinished.test.tsx`: "batches opted-in callbacks that finish in the same microtask into a single commit")
- Given two batched callbacks where the first aborts the second's `AbortSignal` when it runs, when both animations finish in the same microtask, then the first callback runs once and the second never runs — an abort that happens mid-flush is honoured. (base-ui: `packages/react/src/internals/useAnimationsFinished.test.tsx`: "skips a callback whose signal aborts while the batch is flushing")
- Given two popups mirroring `useOpenChangeComplete` with default (non-batched) mode, where the first popup's close completion reopens the second, when both animations finish in the same microtask, then the second popup's queued completion sees the updated `open` state and does NOT unmount — each callback commits separately so later callbacks observe earlier updates. (base-ui: `packages/react/src/internals/useAnimationsFinished.test.tsx`: "commits each callback separately by default so later callbacks observe earlier updates")

### Notes and edge cases

- Given `<Presence present>` wrapping a button whose `ref` is a stable `useRef` object, when rendered, then rendering does not throw and the component commits in fewer than 25 renders (no ref-driven render loop). (radix: `packages/react/presence/src/presence.test.tsx`: "ref stability > does not loop when the child has a stable ref")
- Given `<Presence present>` wrapping a button with an inline callback ref (new identity each render) that calls `forceRender()` when attached, when rendered, then rendering does not throw and the render count stays under 25. (radix: `packages/react/presence/src/presence.test.tsx`: "ref stability > does not loop when the child has an unstable callback ref that triggers a render on attach")

(radix: `packages/react/presence/src/presence.test.tsx`: "ref stability > forwards the node to the child ref")

### Dismissal and layering

- Given `<DismissableLayer.Root onFocusOutside onInteractOutside onDismiss>`, when `focusin` fires on the outside button, then `onFocusOutside`, `onInteractOutside` and `onDismiss` each fire exactly once. (radix: `packages/react/dismissable-layer/src/dismissable-layer.test.tsx`: "DismissableLayer > dismisses on focus outside")
- Given the same layer, when `focusin` fires on the "inside" button, then `onDismiss` is never called. (radix: `packages/react/dismissable-layer/src/dismissable-layer.test.tsx`: "DismissableLayer > does not dismiss on focus inside")
- Given a layer rendered alongside a `<DismissableLayer.Branch>` containing a "branch" button, when `pointerdown` fires on the branch button, then `onDismiss` is never called. (radix: `packages/react/dismissable-layer/src/dismissable-layer.test.tsx`: "DismissableLayer > does not dismiss when interacting with a branch")
- Given a parent `<DismissableLayer.Root disableOutsidePointerEvents deferPointerDownOutside>` and a later child `<DismissableLayer.Root disableOutsidePointerEvents>`, when the outside button receives the full mouse click sequence, then only the child's `onDismiss` fires (once) and the parent's is never called. (radix: `packages/react/dismissable-layer/src/dismissable-layer.test.tsx`: "DismissableLayer > does not dismiss a deferred parent when a child layer dismisses first")
- Given the same deferred modal parent plus nested child layer, when the outside button receives `pointerdown` with `pointerType: 'touch'` followed by `touchstart`, `touchend` and `click`, then only the child's `onDismiss` fires (once) and the parent stays open. - Given `<DismissableLayer.Root onEscapeKeyDown={() => onEscapeKeyDown(count)}>` whose `count` state is incremented twice by clicking a button, when `keydown` with `key: 'Escape'` is fired on `document`, then the handler is called with the latest value `2`, not a stale closure. - Given `<DismissableLayer.Branch>` with `ref`, `data-testid`, `className`, inline `style` and `onClick` inside a layer, when rendered, then the element is a `DIV` carrying those props, the ref resolves to it, and clicking fires `onClick`. - Given `<FloatingPortal id="custom-portal">` wrapping a non-modal `FloatingFocusManager` over an open floating element, when it renders, then the element with `aria-owns` has `aria-owns="custom-portal"` — the supplied portal `id` is reused for the `aria-owns` relationship. - Given `<FloatingPortalLite data-testid="lite-portal">`, when it renders, then a portal element carrying that `data-testid` exists in the document. ### Notes and edge cases

- Given `<FloatingPortal container={customRoot}>` where `customRoot` is a `div#custom-root` appended to `document.body`, when the floating element opens, then its parent is an element with `data-base-ui-portal` whose own parent is `customRoot`. ## hover-interaction

### Roles and attributes

- Given a `<React.StrictMode>`-wrapped `FloatingDelayGroup delay={{ open: 1000, close: 0 }} timeoutMs={50}` with two `useDelayGroup` + `useHover` tooltips whose triggers get `data-instant-phase=""` while `isInstantPhase` is true, when the first trigger is hovered and timers advance 1000ms, then the second trigger is hovered and timers advance 1ms, then `reference-two` has the `data-instant-phase` attribute; after `mouseleave` on it and advancing the 50ms `timeoutMs`, the attribute is gone, so the instant phase resets even though Strict Mode replays the lifecycle effects. (base-ui: `packages/react/src/floating-ui-react/components/FloatingDelayGroup.test.tsx`: "resets the instant phase after Strict Mode replays the lifecycle effects") (jsdom only)

### Pointer

- Given `useHover(context)` with no delay wiring a `<button>` reference and a `role="tooltip"` floating element, when `mouseenter` fires on the button, then the tooltip is in the document immediately with no timer advance. (base-ui: `packages/react/src/floating-ui-react/hooks/useHover.test.tsx`: "opens on mouseenter") (jsdom only)
- Given the same hover setup already opened by `mouseenter`, when `mouseleave` fires on the button, then the `role="tooltip"` element is removed immediately. (base-ui: `packages/react/src/floating-ui-react/hooks/useHover.test.tsx`: "closes on mouseleave") (jsdom only)
- Given `useHover(context, { delay: 1000 })` (symmetric number) with fake timers, when `mouseenter` fires and timers advance 999ms, then no tooltip is rendered; after 1 more ms (1000ms total) the tooltip is rendered. (base-ui: `packages/react/src/floating-ui-react/hooks/useHover.test.tsx`: "prop: delay > symmetric number") (jsdom only)
- Given `useHover(context, { delay: { open: 500 } })`, when `mouseenter` fires and timers advance 499ms, then no tooltip; after 1 more ms (500ms) the tooltip appears. (base-ui: `packages/react/src/floating-ui-react/hooks/useHover.test.tsx`: "prop: delay > open") (jsdom only)
- Given `useHover(context, { delay: { close: 500 } })`, when `mouseenter` then `mouseleave` fire and timers advance 499ms, then the tooltip is still mounted; after 1 more ms (500ms) it is removed. (base-ui: `packages/react/src/floating-ui-react/hooks/useHover.test.tsx`: "prop: delay > close") (jsdom only)

(base-ui: `packages/react/src/floating-ui-react/hooks/useHover.test.tsx`: "prop: delay > open with close 0") (jsdom only)
- Given `useHover(context, { restMs: 100, delay: { close: 100 } })` — a `delay` object with no `open` key — when `mouseenter` fires and timers advance 99ms, then no tooltip is shown, so a nullish `delay.open` leaves `restMs` in charge of opening. (base-ui: `packages/react/src/floating-ui-react/hooks/useHover.test.tsx`: "prop: delay > restMs + nullish open delay should respect restMs") (jsdom only)

## interaction-hooks

### Pointer

- Given `useClick(context)` with default options on a `<button>` reference and a `role="tooltip"` floating element (and `requestAnimationFrame` stubbed to run synchronously), when a bubbling `click` MouseEvent with `button: 0` is dispatched on the button twice, then the tooltip mounts on the first click and unmounts on the second. (base-ui: `packages/react/src/floating-ui-react/hooks/useClick.test.tsx`: "opens and closes on repeated clicks") (jsdom only)
- Given `useClick(context, { toggle: false })`, when the button is clicked twice, then the tooltip stays mounted — a second click cannot close it. (base-ui: `packages/react/src/floating-ui-react/hooks/useClick.test.tsx`: "keeps open on repeated clicks when toggle is false") (jsdom only)
- Given `useClick(context, { event: 'mousedown' })` starting closed, when `pointerdown` (`pointerType: 'mouse'`), `mousedown` and `click` are dispatched in that order and microtasks flush, then the tooltip is mounted. (base-ui: `packages/react/src/floating-ui-react/hooks/useClick.test.tsx`: "opens from the mousedown event path") (jsdom only)
- Given `useClick(context, { event: 'mousedown' })` rendered with `initialOpen`, when the same `pointerdown` + `mousedown` + `click` mouse press sequence runs and microtasks flush, then the tooltip is removed. (base-ui: `packages/react/src/floating-ui-react/hooks/useClick.test.tsx`: "closes from the mousedown event path") (jsdom only)
- Given `useClick(context, { event: 'mousedown-only' })`, when a mouse press (`pointerdown` + `mousedown` + `click`) opens the tooltip and a further standalone `click` is dispatched, then the tooltip stays mounted — the trailing `click` is ignored rather than toggling it closed. (base-ui: `packages/react/src/floating-ui-react/hooks/useClick.test.tsx`: "ignores the click event after mousedown when event is mousedown-only") (jsdom only)
- Given `useClick(context, { ignoreMouse: true })`, when `pointerdown` with `pointerType: 'mouse'` is followed by `click`, then no tooltip is mounted. (base-ui: `packages/react/src/floating-ui-react/hooks/useClick.test.tsx`: "ignores mouse input when ignoreMouse is true") (jsdom only)
- Given `useClick(context, { touchOpenDelay: 100 })` with fake timers, when `pointerdown` with `pointerType: 'touch'` is followed by `click`, then the tooltip is not mounted until timers advance 100ms, after which it is mounted. (base-ui: `packages/react/src/floating-ui-react/hooks/useClick.test.tsx`: "delays touch opening when touchOpenDelay is set") (jsdom only)
- Given `useClick(context, { event: 'mousedown', touchOpenDelay: 100 })` with fake timers and `requestAnimationFrame` callbacks captured instead of run, when a touch press (`pointerdown` with `pointerType: 'touch'`, `mousedown`, `click`) is dispatched, then the tooltip is absent; after flushing the captured animation-frame callbacks it is still absent; only after advancing 100ms does it mount. (base-ui: `packages/react/src/floating-ui-react/hooks/useClick.test.tsx`: "delays touch opening from the deferred mousedown event path") (jsdom only)
- Given `useClick(context, { touchOpenDelay: 100 })` rendered with `initialOpen` and fake timers, when `pointerdown` with `pointerType: 'touch'` is followed by `click`, then the tooltip is removed immediately with no timer advance — `touchOpenDelay` applies only to opening. (base-ui: `packages/react/src/floating-ui-react/hooks/useClick.test.tsx`: "does not delay touch closing") (jsdom only)
- Given both `useHover(context)` and `useClick(context, { stickIfOpen: true })` on the same `<button>`, when the button is hovered open (`mouseover` + `mouseenter` with `relatedTarget: document.body`) and then clicked, then the tooltip stays mounted. (base-ui: `packages/react/src/floating-ui-react/hooks/useClick.test.tsx`: "stickIfOpen true keeps a hover-opened popup open on first click") (jsdom only)
- Given both `useHover(context)` and `useClick(context, { stickIfOpen: false })` on the same `<button>`, when the button is hovered open and then clicked, then the tooltip is removed on that first click. (base-ui: `packages/react/src/floating-ui-react/hooks/useClick.test.tsx`: "stickIfOpen false closes a hover-opened popup on first click") (jsdom only)

## visually-hidden

### Roles and attributes

(radix: `packages/react/visually-hidden/src/visually-hidden.test.tsx`: "spreads props it does not consume onto the element it renders")

(radix: `packages/react/visually-hidden/src/visually-hidden.test.tsx`: "forwards props to the child element when `asChild` is set")

### Notes and edge cases

- Given `new OrderedDict([['a',1],['b',2],['c',3]])`, when `delete('b')`, `set('d',4)` and `clear()` are applied in turn, then `size` reports 3, 2, 3 and 0 respectively. (radix: `packages/react/collection/src/ordered-dictionary.test.ts`: "size")

- Given an OrderedDict of a/b/c, when `set('b',4)` and `set('d',5)` are called, then the existing key's value is replaced and the new key is added. (radix: `packages/react/collection/src/ordered-dictionary.test.ts`: "set()")
- Given an OrderedDict of a/b/c, when `insert(1,'b',4)` re-inserts an existing key at its current index, then the value updates to 4. (radix: `packages/react/collection/src/ordered-dictionary.test.ts`: "insert(): existing key at its current index")
- Given an OrderedDict of a/b/c, when `insert(0,'b',1)` moves an existing key to a new index, then the value updates, `at(0)`/`keyAt(0)` report the moved entry, and the previous occupant (`'a'`) shifts to index 1. (radix: `packages/react/collection/src/ordered-dictionary.test.ts`: "insert(): existing key at a new index")
- Given an OrderedDict of a/b/c, when `insert(20,'d',4)` uses an out-of-range index, then the entry is appended at index 3. (radix: `packages/react/collection/src/ordered-dictionary.test.ts`: "insert(): existing key at out-of-range index")
- Given an OrderedDict of a/b/c/e where `a` is first, when `insert(0,'a',1)` re-inserts the first key at index 0, then `a` keeps index 0 with the new value, `b` stays at index 1, and `size` stays 4. (radix: `packages/react/collection/src/ordered-dictionary.test.ts`: "insert(): existing key at 0 index")
- Given an OrderedDict of b/c/e, when `insert(0,'a',1)` adds a new key at index 0, then `a` occupies index 0, `b` moves to index 1, and `size` becomes 4. (radix: `packages/react/collection/src/ordered-dictionary.test.ts`: "insert(): new key at 0 index")
- Given an OrderedDict of a/b/c/e/f, when `insert(-1,'f',6)` re-inserts the last key at relative index -1, then `keyAt(-1)` is `'f'` with value 6 and `size` stays 5. (radix: `packages/react/collection/src/ordered-dictionary.test.ts`: "insert(): existing key at relative negative index")
- Given an OrderedDict of a/b/c/e, when `insert(-1,'f',6)` then `insert(-3,'d',4)` use negative indices, then `f` lands last and `d` lands at index 3, so negative indices are resolved against the current length. (radix: `packages/react/collection/src/ordered-dictionary.test.ts`: "insert(): new key at relative negative index")
- Given an OrderedDict of a/b/c, when `insert(0,'b',1)` is called, then `get('b')` is 1 and both `at(0)` and `keyAt(0)` reflect the move. (radix: `packages/react/collection/src/ordered-dictionary.test.ts`: "insert(): existing key at a new index (second case)")
- Given an OrderedDict, when `insert` returns, then the return value is the SAME dictionary instance (`insert` mutates in place). (radix: `packages/react/collection/src/ordered-dictionary.test.ts`: "insert(): adds item to existing object")
- Given an OrderedDict, when `with(0,'b',1)` is called, then a NEW dictionary reference is returned. (radix: `packages/react/collection/src/ordered-dictionary.test.ts`: "with(): returns a new reference")
- Given an OrderedDict of a/b/c, when `with(0,'b',1)` is called, then the original dictionary is untouched — `get('b')` is still 2 and `keyAt(1)` is still `'b'`. (radix: `packages/react/collection/src/ordered-dictionary.test.ts`: "with(): does not update copied object")
- Given an OrderedDict of a/b/c/d, when `first()` is called, then it returns the entry tuple `['a', 1]`, and on an empty dictionary it returns `undefined`. (radix: `packages/react/collection/src/ordered-dictionary.test.ts`: "first()")
- Given an OrderedDict of a/b/c/d, when `last()` is called, then it returns `['d', 4]`, and on an empty dictionary `undefined`. (radix: `packages/react/collection/src/ordered-dictionary.test.ts`: "last()")
- Given an OrderedDict of a/b/c/d, when `before('b')` is called, then it returns `['a', 1]`, and `before('a')` returns `undefined`. (radix: `packages/react/collection/src/ordered-dictionary.test.ts`: "before()")

- Given `getFormatter(undefined, { currency: 'USD', style: 'currency', minimumFractionDigits: 2, maximumFractionDigits: 2 })` called twice with equal-but-distinct options objects, when the results are compared, then both calls return the identical `Intl.NumberFormat` instance, so the formatter cache keys on option values. - Given `stringifyLocale`, when called with no argument, with `'en-US'`, with `new Intl.Locale('fr-FR')`, and with `['fr-FR', new Intl.Locale('en-US')]`, then it returns `""`, `"en-US"`, `"fr-FR"` and `"fr-FR,en-US"` respectively, giving a stable cache key for any `Intl` locales argument. - Given `useSize(null)` with a mocked global `ResizeObserver`, when rendered, then the hook returns `undefined` (probe prints "none") and no `ResizeObserver` instance is constructed. (radix: `packages/react/use-size/src/use-size.test.tsx`: "useSize > returns `undefined` when the element is `null`")
- Given an element whose mocked `offsetWidth`/`offsetHeight` are 120 and 40, when `useSize` mounts on it, then the size is already `120x40` during the layout effect, before any observer callback fires. (radix: `packages/react/use-size/src/use-size.test.tsx`: "useSize > provides the size synchronously from offset dimensions on mount")
- Given `useSize` mounted on a real element, when the observer registration is inspected, then the element is observed with options `{ box: 'border-box' }`. (radix: `packages/react/use-size/src/use-size.test.tsx`: "useSize > observes the element using the `border-box` box model")
- Given `useSize` mounted on an element, when the observer emits an entry whose `borderBoxSize` is an array `[{ inlineSize: 200, blockSize: 100 }]`, then the reported size becomes `200x100`. (radix: `packages/react/use-size/src/use-size.test.tsx`: "useSize > updates the size from `borderBoxSize` reported as an array")
- Given the same setup, when the observer emits an entry whose `borderBoxSize` is a plain object `{ inlineSize: 320, blockSize: 240 }` (the non-spec shape some browsers report), then the reported size becomes `320x240`. (radix: `packages/react/use-size/src/use-size.test.tsx`: "useSize > updates the size from `borderBoxSize` reported as a plain object")
- Given mocked `offsetWidth`/`offsetHeight` of 55 and 66, when the observer emits an entry with no `borderBoxSize` key, then the hook falls back to the offset dimensions and reports `55x66`. (radix: `packages/react/use-size/src/use-size.test.tsx`: "useSize > falls back to offset dimensions when `borderBoxSize` is unavailable")
- Given a measured size of `10x20`, when the observer emits an empty entries array and then is invoked with `undefined` entries, then after an animation frame the size is still `10x20` and nothing throws. (radix: `packages/react/use-size/src/use-size.test.tsx`: "useSize > ignores empty or non-array observer payloads")
- Given `useSize` reporting `80x30` for a mounted element, when the harness is rerendered so `null` is passed instead of the element, then the size resets to `undefined` (probe prints "none"). (radix: `packages/react/use-size/src/use-size.test.tsx`: "useSize > resets the size to `undefined` when the element becomes `null`")
- Given `useSize` reporting `10x10`, when the observer emits `{ inlineSize: 300, blockSize: 300 }`, then the DOM still reads `10x10` synchronously and only updates to `300x300` after the next animation frame. (radix: `packages/react/use-size/src/use-size.test.tsx`: "useSize > requestAnimationFrame batching > defers observer-driven updates to the next animation frame")
- Given `useSize` mounted with `requestAnimationFrame`/`cancelAnimationFrame` spied, when the observer emits three sizes (1x1, 2x2, 3x3) in one act, then exactly three frames are scheduled, `cancelAnimationFrame` is called with the first two ids, and only the final `3x3` is reflected. (radix: `packages/react/use-size/src/use-size.test.tsx`: "useSize > requestAnimationFrame batching > coalesces rapid observations, cancelling the previously scheduled frames")
- Given a pending frame scheduled by an observer emit of 500x500, when the component unmounts, then `cancelAnimationFrame` is called with that frame id and the element is no longer observed. (radix: `packages/react/use-size/src/use-size.test.tsx`: "useSize > requestAnimationFrame batching > cancels a pending frame and un-observes on unmount")
- Given a pending frame scheduled by an observer emit of 999x999, when the component unmounts before the frame runs and one animation frame elapses, then `console.error` is never called, so no state update happens on the unmounted component. (radix: `packages/react/use-size/src/use-size.test.tsx`: "useSize > requestAnimationFrame batching > does not warn or error when unmounted before a pending frame runs")

## conformance-harness

### Notes and edge cases

- Given Base UI's `packages/react/test/describeConformance.tsx` and `packages/react/test/popupConformanceTests.tsx`, when read as a specification, then together they form the only shared, generated conformance suite in either library; the full description of what each takes, what each asserts test by test, how components opt in, and what neither covers is in the "Base UI's shared conformance harness" part of **Test infrastructure notes** at the end of this document. (base-ui: `packages/react/test/describeConformance.tsx`: "see Test infrastructure notes")
- Given any Base UI component section above, when you look for its harness opt-in, then each part that calls `describeConformance(...)` or `popupConformanceTests(...)` has exactly one bullet under that component's "Notes and edge cases" recording the options it passes (`refInstanceof`, `button`, `testRenderPropWith`, `wrappingAllowed`, `skip`, and for popups `triggerMouseAction`, `expectedPopupRole`, `expectedAriaHasPopupValue`, `alwaysMounted`, `combobox`). Those bullets are the machine-readable index of which parts are held to the shared contract. (base-ui: `packages/react/test/popupConformanceTests.tsx`: "see each component's Notes and edge cases")
- Given Radix, when the equivalent is looked for, then there is none: every part instead carries a hand-written matched pair named "spreads props it does not consume onto the element it renders" and "forwards props to the child element when `asChild` is set". Those two tests per part are Radix's de-facto conformance contract and appear as bullets under each component's "Notes and edge cases" and "Roles and attributes". (radix: `packages/react/primitive/src/primitive.test.tsx`: "house convention, not a shared harness")
