## Test infrastructure notes

### Radix UI Primitives

**Runner.** Vitest, configured in `vitest.config.mts` with two projects:

- `unit` — `environment: 'jsdom'`, `include: ['**/*.test.?(c|m)[jt]s?(x)']`, `setupFiles: ['./scripts/setup-tests.ts']`, `retry: 1`.
- `rsc` — `environment: 'node'`, `include: ['**/*.rsc.test.?(c|m)[jt]s?(x)']`, resolve `conditions: ['react-server', ...]` so React's Server Components build is loaded and every client-only API is `undefined`. A `rscClientBoundaryStub()` Vite plugin stubs out any module declaring `"use client"`, mimicking a real RSC bundler. React and React DOM are inlined (`server.deps.inline`) so Vite honours the export condition. Only `scripts/rsc-compatibility.rsc.test.ts` runs here.

**Global setup** (`scripts/setup-tests.ts`) does exactly four things:

1. imports `@testing-library/jest-dom/vitest`;
2. `expect.extend(axeMatchers)` from `vitest-axe/matchers`, which is what makes `expect(await axe(container)).toHaveNoViolations()` work;
3. installs a stub `global.ResizeObserver` whose `observe()` synchronously invokes the callback with `[{ borderBoxSize: { inlineSize: 0, blockSize: 0 } }]` — so any size-dependent code (Collapsible/Accordion content measurement, `useSize`) sees zero dimensions in jsdom;
4. polyfills `Element.prototype.scrollIntoView` as a no-op because jsdom lacks it and Select's focus management calls it.

Several component test files install their own copy of the same `ResizeObserver` stub at module scope (checkbox, radio-group), which matters for the tests that assert on presence/measurement.

**DOM driving.** Mostly `fireEvent` from `@testing-library/react` wrapped in `act(...)`. `@testing-library/user-event` is used where real event sequencing matters — slider keyboard stepping, the one-time-password field, the password-toggle field, and toggle-group. Tests that must simulate a real drag stub browser APIs jsdom lacks: the slider range tests replace `getBoundingClientRect` with a fixed 100x10 rect and stub `setPointerCapture`/`releasePointerCapture`/`hasPointerCapture` (jsdom/jsdom#2666).

**Fake timers.** Only where delay is the behaviour under test (hover card's 700/300ms open/close delays, tooltip's 100/300ms delay and its 0ms skip-delay window, toast timeouts). Elsewhere real microtasks plus `act` are used.

**Custom matchers / helpers.**

- `vitest-axe` matchers (`toHaveNoViolations`) — nearly every component has at least one axe test, usually one per visual state (closed, open, disabled).
- `internal/test-utils/ref-stability.tsx` exports `assertStableComposedRef(renderWithRef, { maxRenders = 25 })`. It renders the component with a *stable* callback ref that forces a re-render the first time it receives a node. If the component composes the forwarded ref with an unstable member, React 19 detaches and re-attaches on every commit, the forced render loops, and "Maximum update depth exceeded" is thrown. A correctly stabilized ref settles in a couple of renders. This is the regression guard for radix-ui/primitives#3963 and is used by slider, dismissable-layer and others.
- A house convention rather than a harness: **every** primitive part has a matched pair of tests named "spreads props it does not consume onto the element it renders" and "forwards props to the child element when `asChild` is set". The pair asserts `className` merging, inline `style` merging (never replacement — proved by picking `outlineColor: rgb(1, 2, 3)` alongside a library-owned property such as `pointer-events: none` or `position: absolute`), ref identity, `onClick` composition rather than replacement, the slotted element's `tagName`, and every attribute the part owns (`role`, `data-state`, `data-orientation`, `aria-*`). This pair is the closest Radix equivalent to Base UI's `describeConformance`, but it is hand-written per part rather than generated.

**End-to-end.** Playwright, `playwright.config.ts`: `testDir: './e2e'`, `testMatch: '**/*.spec.ts'`, chromium only, viewport 1024x768, `hasTouch: true` (needed for `locator.tap()`), `fullyParallel`, 30s test timeout with a deliberately generous 20s `expect` timeout "so retry-able assertions have time to settle while menus/popovers animate", `trace: 'on-first-retry'`, 2 retries and 2 workers on CI. The web server is Storybook (`pnpm dev`) on port 9009.

`e2e/helpers.ts` is a Cypress-compatibility layer, written when the Cypress specs were ported. It provides `visitStory(page, storyName)` (navigates to `/iframe.html?id=components-<storyName>`, so most specs load a story literally named `*--cypress`), `visitStoryById`, a named-position system (`topLeft`…`bottomRight`) matching `cypress-real-events` semantics with edges inset by 1px, `hoverAt`, `pointerOutAt`, `keydown`, `pointerOver`, `pointerExitRightToLeft`/`pointerExitLeftToRight` (for submenu safe-triangle exits), `longTouch` (dispatches a primary `pointerdown` with `pointerType: 'touch'` then waits 750ms), and `touchSwipe`, which drives the Chrome DevTools Protocol (`Input.dispatchTouchEvent`) in 6 steps because Playwright's `touchscreen` only supports taps.

### MUI Base UI

**Runner.** Vitest with projects declared in `vitest.config.mts` (`packages/*/vitest.config.mts`, `docs/vitest.config.mts`, `test/e2e/vitest.config.mts`, `test/regressions/vitest.config.mts`), `sequence.hooks: 'list'`, istanbul coverage, and a JUnit reporter on CI.

**Two environments from one suite.** `vitest.shared.mts` defaults to `environment: 'jsdom'` with `environmentOptions.jsdom = { pretendToBeVisual: true, url: 'http://localhost' }`. Setting `VITEST_ENV` to `chromium`, `webkit`, `firefox` or `all-browsers` flips the same suite into **Vitest browser mode** via `@vitest/browser-playwright` (`headless: true`, `screenshotFailures: false`, `contextOptions.timezoneId: 'UTC'`). `*.spec.*` files are excluded from the run (`exclude: ['node_modules', 'build', '**/*.spec.*']`) because they are type-only. `retry: 1` on CI. `globals: true`.

This dual environment is why `isJSDOM` appears everywhere. It is a one-liner in `packages/utils/src/testUtils.ts`:

```ts
export const isJSDOM = /jsdom/.test(window.navigator.userAgent);
```

Tests then use `describe.skipIf(isJSDOM)` / `it.skipIf(isJSDOM)` for anything needing real layout, real animations, real scroll or real focus (all positioning geometry, `alignItemWithTrigger`, scroll locking, exit animations, drag/scrub gestures), and `describe.skipIf(!isJSDOM)` for the reverse — fake-timer-driven and jsdom-only cases. There is no `describeSkipIf` helper; `describe.skipIf` is Vitest's own API. Browser-specific behaviour gets its own file suffix instead of a runtime branch: `*.webkit.test.tsx`, `*.gecko.test.tsx`, `*.iOS.test.tsx`, `*.android.test.tsx`, `*.non-mac.test.tsx`, `*.voiceOver.test.tsx`, `*.talkBack.test.tsx`, `*.react17.test.tsx`.

**Global setup** (`test/setupVitest.ts`):

- calls `@mui/internal-test-utils`'s `setupVitest()`, which is what installs `toErrorDev()` / `toWarnDev()` — the matchers that assert on `console.error`/`console.warn` output in development;
- imports `packages/react/test/addVitestMatchers`, adding `toEqualDateTime(expected)` (normalizes Luxon objects and strings to `Date` and compares down to milliseconds) for the Temporal adapters;
- imports `@testing-library/jest-dom/vitest`;
- sets `globalThis.BASE_UI_ANIMATIONS_DISABLED = true` by default and re-sets it in `afterEach`, so tests that need real animations must opt in by flipping it to `false` (the popup conformance suite and `useAnimationsFinished` tests do exactly that, restoring it in a `finally`);
- in `afterEach`: `vi.resetAllMocks()`, resets the module-level error-logging state in `@base-ui/utils/error` (both the built package copy and the source copy, because compiler tests can load them as separate instances), and calls `resetAnimationFrameScheduler()` on both copies to drop animation-frame callbacks that were scheduled but never ran — the scheduler is process-global, so a frame left pending under torn-down fake timers would otherwise fire in a later test against stale state;
- in jsdom, replaces `globalThis.requestAnimationFrame` with `setTimeout(cb, 0)`, which is what makes `rAF`-driven code advance under fake timers.

**DOM driving.** A wrapped renderer, `packages/react/test/createRenderer.ts`, built on `@mui/internal-test-utils`'s `createRenderer`. Its `render` is **async** and wraps the underlying render in `await act(...)`; it returns `rerender(newElement)` and `setProps(newProps)` that are also `act`-wrapped and awaited. The result also exposes a `user` object, so most interaction is `await user.click(...)` / `await user.keyboard(...)` (user-event in jsdom, `vitest/browser`'s `userEvent` in browser mode). Raw `fireEvent` is reserved for events user-event cannot express.

Supporting helpers in `packages/react/test/`:

- `advanceReactClock(clock, ms)` — `flushMicrotasks()`, then `clock.tickAsync(ms)`, then `flushMicrotasks()` again. This is the standard way the suite advances fake timers so React effects settle on both sides of the tick.
- `wait(ms)` and `waitSingleFrame()` (a `requestAnimationFrame` promise).
- `waitForPositioned(positioner)` — waits until `positioner.style.opacity !== '0'` and then until the element `toBeVisible()`; anchored popups are positioned at `opacity: 0` first, so this is the gate before asserting geometry.
- `pointer.ts` — `enterWithMouse(element, init)` fires `pointerenter` (with `pointerType: 'mouse'`) then `mouseenter` then `mousemove`; `moveMouse(from, to)` fires the full leave/enter pair with `relatedTarget` set both ways plus a trailing `mousemove`. `firePointer.down/move/up` require an explicit `timeStamp > 0` and then `Object.defineProperty` it onto the event, because `timeStamp` is read-only and not part of `PointerEventInit`, so `fireEvent` drops it silently and jsdom would stamp it off the (faked) clock. It throws if `timeStamp <= 0`. This exists so velocity-sensitive gesture code (`useSwipeDismiss`, number-field scrubbing, drawer swiping) describes a fixed timeline rather than inheriting the runner's real timing.
- `resetBrowserPointer()` — in browser mode only, `await userEvent.unhover(document.body)`, because Playwright's pointer state persists between tests.
- `useTestInteractions(propsList)` — a test-only stand-in for the floating-ui interaction hooks composition, returning `getReferenceProps`, `getFloatingProps`, `getItemProps` and `getTriggerProps` that merge a list of `ElementProps` objects. It is how the vendored floating-ui hooks are exercised in isolation, and it has its own test file.
- `mergeRefs.ts`.

**Type-only tests.** `*.spec.ts`/`*.spec.tsx` files contain no runtime assertions; they are compile-time contracts checked by `tsc`/`tsgo` and excluded from the Vitest run. They use `@ts-expect-error` to pin what must NOT type-check (for example `ComboboxRoot.spec.tsx` encodes the whole value/`multiple` inference matrix and the `onOpenChange` reason-to-event narrowing) and `expectType<Expected, typeof actual>(actual)` from `packages/utils/src/testUtils.ts`, which errors unless the two types are mutually assignable.

**End-to-end and regressions.** `test/e2e/` and `test/regressions/` are separate Vitest projects. `test/screen-reader/radio.spec.ts` exists as a screen-reader-specific spec. Base UI does not keep a Playwright-only suite parallel to the component tests the way Radix does — browser coverage comes from running the same `*.test.tsx` files in Vitest browser mode against chromium, webkit and firefox.

### Base UI's shared conformance harness

This is the closest existing thing to a conformance suite, and it is deliberately small. It lives in `packages/react/test/` and has two independent entry points.

#### 1. `describeConformance(minimalElement, () => options)`

Defined in `packages/react/test/describeConformance.tsx`. It is wrapped in `createDescribe('Base UI component API', ...)` from `@mui/internal-test-utils`, so every component's conformance block appears under a `Base UI component API` describe.

**What it takes.** A minimal JSX element for the part under test, and a *thunk* returning options (a thunk so the enclosing suite's `createRenderer()` result is available at call time). Options, from `BaseUiConformanceTestsOptions`:

- `render` (required) — the async `render` from `createRenderer()`. Missing it throws a pointed error: `missing "render" in options\n\n  > describeConformance(element, () => options)`.
- `refInstanceof` — the constructor the forwarded ref must be an instance of (`window.HTMLDivElement`, `window.HTMLButtonElement`, `window.HTMLSpanElement`, `window.HTMLInputElement`, …).
- `testRenderPropWith` — the intrinsic tag name to use when exercising the `render` prop; defaults to `'div'`. Setting it to `'button'` also flips the harness's internal `nativeButton` flag.
- `button` — when true, the harness passes `nativeButton: <testRenderPropWith === 'button'>` alongside the other props, for parts whose button-ness is a prop.
- `wrappingAllowed` — default `true`. When false the render-prop wrapper does not add an extra `<div data-testid="base-ui-wrapper">`, for parts that must not tolerate an extra element.
- `only` / `skip` — arrays selecting or excluding suites by key from `{ propsSpread, refForwarding, renderProp, className }`.
- `after` — an `afterAll` hook.

**What it asserts.** Four suites, 13 tests total.

`prop forwarding` (`conformanceTests/propForwarding.tsx`), 6 tests:

1. *forwards custom props to the default element* — `lang="fr"` and a random `data-foobar` land on the part's own element.
2. *forwards custom props to the customized element defined with a function* — same, when `render` is a function `(props) => <Element {...props} />`.
3. *forwards custom props to the customized element defined using JSX* — same, when `render` is an element `<Element />`.
4. *forwards the custom `style` attribute defined on the component* — `style={{ color: 'green' }}` on the part yields a `style` attribute containing `color: green`.
5. and 6. two tests with the identical name *forwards the custom `style` attribute defined on the render function* — one for the function form of `render`, one for the JSX form.

Each waits on `flushMicrotasks()` before asserting, so a part that sets props in an effect still passes.

`ref` (`conformanceTests/refForwarding.tsx`), 1 test:

7. *attaches the ref* — the part is cloned with a `React.createRef()` inside a `<React.Fragment>`, and `ref.current` must be `instanceof` the `refInstanceof` option. This is the only assertion; the harness does not check ref cleanup or stability.

`prop: render` (`conformanceTests/renderProp.tsx`), 6 tests, all against a `Wrapper` that renders `<Element data-testid="wrapped">` optionally inside `<div data-testid="base-ui-wrapper">`:

8. *renders a customized root element with a function* — the wrapper and the wrapped element are both present and the wrapped element carries a random `data-test-value` passed through the render function.
9. *renders a customized root element with an element* — same via the JSX form of `render`.
10. a second test with the same name *renders a customized root element with an element* — the no-extra-props case; asserts the wrapper exists when `wrappingAllowed`, otherwise that the wrapped element exists.
11. *should pass the ref to the custom component* — the part's `ref` resolves to the element the render prop produced: `instanceFromRef.tagName` equals `testRenderPropWith` uppercased and it carries the `data-testid`.
12. *should merge the rendering element ref with the custom component ref* — both the part's `ref` and a `ref` on the render element resolve to the same node, each with the right tag and testid.
13. *should merge the rendering element className with the custom component className* — `className="component-classname"` on the part and `className="render-prop-classname"` on the render element both end up in the element's `classList`.
14. *should merge the rendering element resolved className with the custom component className* — same, but the part's `className` is a **function** `(state) => string`, so the resolved value must also merge rather than replace.

`prop: className` (`conformanceTests/className.tsx`), 1 test:

15. *should apply the className when passed as a string* — `document.querySelector('.test-class')` is non-null.

(Counting the duplicated names, the four suites contribute 6 + 1 + 7 + 1 = 15 `it` blocks; the suite keys are the four names in `fullSuite`.)

**How components opt in.** A component's own test file calls it inside its top-level describe, e.g.

```tsx
describeConformance(<Select.Trigger />, () => ({
  refInstanceof: window.HTMLDivElement,
  button: true,
  testRenderPropWith: 'button',
  render(node) { return render(<Select.Root open>{node}</Select.Root>); },
}));
```

The `render` option is where the part gets wrapped in whatever context it needs (an open `Select.Root`, a `Field.Root`, a `Menu.Portal`, and so on), which is how a harness this small covers 100-plus parts. Parts that cannot satisfy a suite pass `skip: ['propsSpread']` and friends. Every bullet in the component sections below that cites `"describeConformance"` records the exact options that component used.

**What the harness does NOT check**, and would have to be added for a real conformance suite: roles and ARIA wiring, `data-*` state attributes, keyboard behaviour, focus, controlled/uncontrolled parity, SSR/hydration, or any form integration. All of that is hand-written per component.

#### 2. `popupConformanceTests(config)`

Defined in `packages/react/test/popupConformanceTests.tsx`. This one *is* behavioural, and it is the shared contract for every popup surface (dialog, popover, menu, select, combobox, tooltip, preview-card, …).

**What it takes** (`PopupTestConfig`):

- `createComponent(props)` — a function returning the full JSX tree, receiving `{ root, trigger, popup, portal }` prop bags to spread onto the corresponding parts. The harness always injects `data-testid="trigger"` and `data-testid="popup"`.
- `triggerMouseAction` — `'click'` or `'hover'`. Several suites only run for `'click'`.
- `render` — the `render` from `createRenderer()`.
- `expectedPopupRole` — the `role` the popup must carry.
- `expectedAriaHasPopupValue` — defaults to `expectedPopupRole`.
- `alwaysMounted` — `boolean | 'only-after-open'`, for popups that stay in the DOM.
- `combobox` — changes which attribute the open assertion waits on.

**What it asserts.**

- `controlled mode > opens the popup with the 'open' prop` — with `open={false}` the popup is either absent (`toBe(null)`) or, if `alwaysMounted`, present but `toBeInaccessible()`; re-rendering with `open={true}` makes it non-null.
- `uncontrolled mode > opens the popup when clicking on the trigger` (only when `triggerMouseAction === 'click'`) — same starting assertion, then `await user.click(trigger)` and `waitFor` the popup to exist.
- `ARIA attributes > has the <role> role on the popup` (when `expectedPopupRole` is set).
- `ARIA attributes > has the 'aria-controls' attribute on the trigger` — equals the popup's `id`.
- `ARIA attributes > has the 'aria-expanded' attribute on the trigger when open` — `"false"` while closed, `"true"` after clicking; the wait gate is `role="listbox"` on the popup for `combobox: true` popups and the presence of `data-open` otherwise.
- `ARIA attributes > has the 'aria-haspopup' attribute on the trigger` — equals `expectedAriaHasPopupValue` (skipped when that resolves falsy).
- `ARIA attributes > allows a custom 'id' prop` — passing `id: 'TestId'` to the popup keeps `trigger[aria-controls] === popup[id]`.
- `animations > removes the popup when there is no exit animation defined` — flips `BASE_UI_ANIMATIONS_DISABLED` to `false` in `beforeEach` and back to `true` in `afterEach`; skips itself under jsdom via the test-context `skip()`; asserts that going from `open` to closed removes the popup (or makes it inaccessible when always-mounted).
- `animations > removes the popup when the animation finishes` — **currently disabled**: the body calls `skip()` unconditionally with the comment "XXX: revisit after feedback from the team". Had it run, it would inject a `@keyframes` animation bound to `[data-ending-style]`, set `portal.keepMounted`, close the popup, and assert the popup becomes inaccessible while still mounted and that `onAnimationEnd` fires exactly once. This is a gap worth closing in a new conformance suite.

Both `toBeInaccessible()` and the `skip()` test-context argument come from the surrounding stack (`jest-dom` and Vitest respectively), not from Base UI.
